### GenericAccessor.reduce | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L2609-L2907)

```python
GenericAccessor.reduce(
    reduce_func_nb,
    *args,
    returns_array=False,
    returns_idx=False,
    flatten=False,
    order='C',
    to_index=True,
    broadcast_named_args=None,
    broadcast_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    wrapper=None,
    group_by=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None
)
```

Reduce data by column or for grouped data.

The internal reduction function is chosen based on the grouping status and provided flags.

__See__

If the data is grouped and `flatten` is True:

* [reduce_flat_grouped_to_array_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_flat_grouped_to_array_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_flat_grouped_to_array_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is True.

* [reduce_flat_grouped_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_flat_grouped_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_flat_grouped_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is False.

If the data is grouped and `flatten` is False:

* [reduce_grouped_to_array_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_to_array_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_to_array_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is True.

* [reduce_grouped_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is False.

If the data is not grouped:

* [reduce_to_array_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_to_array_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_to_array_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is True.

* [reduce_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_nb") is used
    when `returns_array` is False.

For meta reducing functions, the following internal functions are used:

* [reduce_grouped_to_array_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_to_array_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_to_array_meta_nb") for grouped data
    when `returns_array` is True.

* [reduce_grouped_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_meta_nb") for grouped data
    when `returns_array` is False.

* [reduce_to_array_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_to_array_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_to_array_meta_nb") for non-grouped data
    when `returns_array` is True.

* [reduce_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_meta_nb") for non-grouped data
    when `returns_array` is False.

__Args__

**```reduce_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyFlexReduceFunc]`
:   Callback function for flexible reducing.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `reduce_func_nb`.

**```returns_array```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   True if the reducing function returns an array.

    Determines whether the output should be processed with array-specific logic.

**```returns_idx```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   True if the reducing function returns row indices.

    When True, numeric positions may be converted to index labels if `to_index` is also True.

**```flatten```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   True to flatten grouped data before applying the reducing function.

    When operating on grouped data, a flattened array is passed to `reduce_func_nb`.

**```order```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Order in which to flatten the array ("C" for row-major or "F" for column-major).

**```to_index```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   True to convert positions to index labels when `returns_idx` is True.

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`
:   Array wrapper instance.

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification.

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap_reduced](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap_reduced "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap_reduced").

__Returns__

`MaybeSeriesFrame`
:   Reduced data as a Series or DataFrame.

__Examples__

Using regular function:

```pycon
>>> mean_nb = njit(lambda a: np.nanmean(a))

>>> df.vbt.reduce(mean_nb)
a    3.0
b    3.0
c    1.8
Name: reduce, dtype: float64

>>> argmax_nb = njit(lambda a: np.argmax(a))

>>> df.vbt.reduce(argmax_nb, returns_idx=True)
a   2020-01-05
b   2020-01-01
c   2020-01-03
Name: reduce, dtype: datetime64[ns]

>>> df.vbt.reduce(argmax_nb, returns_idx=True, to_index=False)
a    4
b    0
c    2
Name: reduce, dtype: int64

>>> min_max_nb = njit(lambda a: np.array([np.nanmin(a), np.nanmax(a)]))

>>> df.vbt.reduce(min_max_nb, returns_array=True, wrap_kwargs=dict(name_or_index=['min', 'max']))
      a  b  c
min  1  1  1
max  5  5  3

>>> group_by = pd.Series(['first', 'first', 'second'], name='group')
>>> df.vbt.reduce(mean_nb, group_by=group_by)
group
first     3.0
second    1.8
dtype: float64
```

Using meta function:

```pycon
>>> mean_meta_nb = njit(lambda col, a: np.nanmean(a[:, col]))

>>> pd.Series.vbt.reduce(
...     mean_meta_nb,
...     df['a'].vbt.to_2d_array(),
...     wrapper=df['a'].vbt.wrapper
... )
3.0

>>> vbt.pd_acc.reduce(
...     mean_meta_nb,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array(),
...     wrapper=df.vbt.wrapper
... )
a    3.0
b    3.0
c    1.8
Name: reduce, dtype: float64

>>> grouped_mean_meta_nb = njit(lambda group_idxs, group, a: np.nanmean(a[:, group_idxs]))

>>> group_by = pd.Series(['first', 'first', 'second'], name='group')
>>> vbt.pd_acc.reduce(
...     grouped_mean_meta_nb,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array(),
...     wrapper=df.vbt.wrapper,
...     group_by=group_by
... )
group
first     3.0
second    1.8
Name: reduce, dtype: float64
```

Using templates and broadcasting:

```pycon
>>> mean_a_b_nb = njit(lambda col, a, b: \
...     np.array([np.nanmean(a[:, col]), np.nanmean(b[:, col])]))

>>> vbt.pd_acc.reduce(
...     mean_a_b_nb,
...     vbt.Rep('arr1'),
...     vbt.Rep('arr2'),
...     returns_array=True,
...     broadcast_named_args=dict(
...         arr1=pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], index=df.index),
...         arr2=pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3]], columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])
...     ),
...     wrap_kwargs=dict(name_or_index=['arr1', 'arr2'])
... )
        a    b    c
arr1  3.0  3.0  3.0
arr2  1.0  2.0  3.0
```

### GenericAccessor.resample_apply | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L2254-L2442)

```python
GenericAccessor.resample_apply(
    rule,
    reduce_func_nb,
    *args,
    use_groupby_apply=False,
    freq=None,
    resample_kwargs=None,
    broadcast_named_args=None,
    broadcast_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    wrapper=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Resample the underlying data using a specified rule and reduction function.

__Args__

**```rule```** :&ensp;`AnyRuleLike`
:   Resampler-like specification.

    Can be one of the following:

    * [Resampler](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/resampling/base/#vectorbtpro.base.resampling.base.Resampler "vectorbtpro.base.resampling.base.Resampler") instance

    * Pandas `Resampler` instance

    * Instruction for any of the above

**```reduce_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyResampleReduceFunc]`
:   Callback function for resampling.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `reduce_func_nb`.

**```use_groupby_apply```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, apply the reduction function using
    [GenericAccessor.groupby_apply](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.groupby_apply "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.groupby_apply") with post-processing; otherwise, use
    [GenericAccessor.resample_to_index](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.resample_to_index "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.resample_to_index").

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the target index 
    (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```resample_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `pandas.Series.resample`.

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`
:   Array wrapper instance.

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `reduce_func_nb`.

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Result of the resampling and reduction.

__Examples__

Using regular function:

```pycon
>>> mean_nb = njit(lambda a: np.nanmean(a))

>>> df.vbt.resample_apply('2d', mean_nb)
              a    b    c
2020-01-01  1.5  4.5  1.5
2020-01-03  3.5  2.5  2.5
2020-01-05  5.0  1.0  1.0
```

Using meta function:

```pycon
>>> mean_ratio_meta_nb = njit(lambda idxs, group, col, a, b: \
...     np.mean(a[idxs, col]) / np.mean(b[idxs, col]))

>>> vbt.pd_acc.resample_apply(
...     '2d',
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() - 1,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() + 1,
...     wrapper=df.vbt.wrapper
... )
                    a         b         c
2020-01-01  0.200000  0.636364  0.200000
2020-01-03  0.555556  0.428571  0.428571
2020-01-05  0.666667  0.000000  0.000000
```

Using templates and broadcasting:

```pycon
>>> vbt.pd_acc.resample_apply(
...     '2d',
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     vbt.Rep('a'),
...     vbt.Rep('b'),
...     broadcast_named_args=dict(
...         a=pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], index=df.index),
...         b=pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3]], columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])
...     )
... )
              a     b         c
2020-01-01  1.5  0.75  0.500000
2020-01-03  3.5  1.75  1.166667
2020-01-05  5.0  2.50  1.666667
```

### GenericAccessor.resample_between_bounds | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L3737-L3957)

Resample between target index bounds.

__See__

* [reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb") for meta operations.

__Args__

**```target_lbound_index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`

**```target_rbound_index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`

**```reduce_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyRangeReduceFuncc]`
:   Callback function for reducing ranges.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**

**```closed_lbound```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if the lower bound of the interval is inclusive.

**```closed_rbound```** :&ensp;`bool`

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Resampled Series or DataFrame with aggregated values,
    wrapped based on the specified parameters.

__Examples__

Using regular function:

### GenericAccessor.resample_to_index | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L3515-L3735)

```python
GenericAccessor.resample_to_index(
    index,

    *args,

    before=False,

    wrap_kwargs=None,
    silence_warnings=None
```

Resample data to a specified target index.

This function applies the reduction function on segments of the source data corresponding to 
index ranges derived from the target index.

__See__

* [reduce_index_ranges_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_nb") for standard operations.

* [reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_index_ranges_meta_nb") for meta operations.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`AnyRuleLike`
:   Target index for resampling.

**```reduce_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyRangeReduceFunc]`
:   Callback function for reducing ranges.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `reduce_func_nb`.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Union[None, bool, FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the target index 
    (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```before```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, use index ranges preceding the target index.

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`
:   Array wrapper instance.

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Resampled data as a Pandas Series or DataFrame.

__Examples__

Downsampling:

```pycon
>>> h_index = pd.date_range('2020-01-01', '2020-01-05', freq='1h')
>>> d_index = pd.date_range('2020-01-01', '2020-01-05', freq='1d')

>>> h_sr = pd.Series(range(len(h_index)), index=h_index)
>>> h_sr.vbt.resample_to_index(d_index, njit(lambda x: x.mean()))
2020-01-01    11.5
2020-01-02    35.5
2020-01-03    59.5
2020-01-04    83.5
2020-01-05    96.0
Freq: D, dtype: float64

>>> h_sr.vbt.resample_to_index(d_index, njit(lambda x: x.mean()), before=True)
2020-01-01     0.0
2020-01-02    12.5
2020-01-03    36.5
2020-01-04    60.5
2020-01-05    84.5
Freq: D, dtype: float64
```

Upsampling:

```pycon
>>> d_sr = pd.Series(range(len(d_index)), index=d_index)
>>> d_sr.vbt.resample_to_index(h_index, njit(lambda x: x[-1]))
2020-01-01 00:00:00    0.0
2020-01-01 01:00:00    NaN
2020-01-01 02:00:00    NaN
2020-01-01 03:00:00    NaN
2020-01-01 04:00:00    NaN
...                    ...
2020-01-04 20:00:00    NaN
2020-01-04 21:00:00    NaN
2020-01-04 22:00:00    NaN
2020-01-04 23:00:00    NaN
2020-01-05 00:00:00    4.0
Freq: H, Length: 97, dtype: float64
```

Using meta function:

```pycon
>>> mean_ratio_meta_nb = njit(lambda from_i, to_i, col, a, b: \
...     np.mean(a[from_i:to_i][col]) / np.mean(b[from_i:to_i][col]))

>>> vbt.pd_acc.resample_to_index(
...     d_index,
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     h_sr.vbt.to_2d_array() - 1,
...     h_sr.vbt.to_2d_array() + 1,
...     wrapper=h_sr.vbt.wrapper
... )
2020-01-01   -1.000000
2020-01-02    0.920000
2020-01-03    0.959184
2020-01-04    0.972603
2020-01-05    0.979381
Freq: D, dtype: float64
```

Using templates and broadcasting:

```pycon
>>> vbt.pd_acc.resample_to_index(
...     d_index,
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     vbt.Rep('a'),
...     vbt.Rep('b'),
...     broadcast_named_args=dict(
...         a=h_sr - 1,
...         b=h_sr + 1
...     )
... )
2020-01-01   -1.000000
2020-01-02    0.920000
2020-01-03    0.959184
2020-01-04    0.972603
2020-01-05    0.979381
Freq: D, dtype: float64
```

### GenericAccessor.resolve_mapping | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L350-L375)

### GenericAccessor.rolling_apply | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L1735-L1926)

```python
GenericAccessor.rolling_apply(
    window,
    reduce_func_nb,
    *args,
    minp=None,
    broadcast_named_args=None,
    broadcast_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    wrapper=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None
)
```

Apply a rolling reduction function over a specified window.

__See__

* [rolling_reduce_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_reduce_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_reduce_nb") for integer windows.

* [rolling_freq_reduce_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_freq_reduce_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_freq_reduce_nb") for frequency windows.

* [rolling_reduce_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_reduce_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_reduce_meta_nb") for meta functions and integer windows.

* [rolling_freq_reduce_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_freq_reduce_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.rolling_freq_reduce_meta_nb") for meta functions and frequency windows.

__Args__

**```window```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Window size as an integer or a frequency string.

    If None, an expanding window is used.

**```reduce_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyReduceFunc]`
:   Callback function for reducing.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for the reduction function.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`
:   Array wrapper instance.

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Result of the rolling reduction.

__Examples__

Using regular function:

```pycon
>>> mean_nb = njit(lambda a: np.nanmean(a))

>>> df.vbt.rolling_apply(3, mean_nb)
              a    b         c
2020-01-01  NaN  NaN       NaN
2020-01-02  NaN  NaN       NaN
2020-01-03  2.0  4.0  2.000000
2020-01-04  3.0  3.0  2.333333
2020-01-05  4.0  2.0  2.000000
```

Using a frequency-based window:

```pycon
>>> df.vbt.rolling_apply("3d", mean_nb)
              a    b         c
2020-01-01  1.0  5.0  1.000000
2020-01-02  1.5  4.5  1.500000
2020-01-03  2.0  4.0  2.000000
2020-01-04  3.0  3.0  2.333333
2020-01-05  4.0  2.0  2.000000
```

Using meta function:

```pycon
>>> mean_ratio_meta_nb = njit(lambda from_i, to_i, col, a, b: \
...     np.mean(a[from_i:to_i, col]) / np.mean(b[from_i:to_i, col]))

>>> vbt.pd_acc.rolling_apply(
...     3,
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() - 1,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() + 1,
...     wrapper=df.vbt.wrapper,
... )
                    a         b         c
2020-01-01       NaN       NaN       NaN
2020-01-02       NaN       NaN       NaN
2020-01-03  0.333333  0.600000  0.333333
2020-01-04  0.500000  0.500000  0.400000
2020-01-05  0.600000  0.333333  0.333333
```

Using templates and broadcasting:

```pycon
>>> vbt.pd_acc.rolling_apply(
...     2,
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     vbt.Rep('a'),
...     vbt.Rep('b'),
...     broadcast_named_args=dict(
...         a=pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], index=df.index),
...         b=pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3]], columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])
...     )
... )
              a     b         c
2020-01-01  NaN   NaN       NaN
2020-01-02  1.5  0.75  0.500000
2020-01-03  2.5  1.25  0.833333
2020-01-04  3.5  1.75  1.166667
2020-01-05  4.5  2.25  1.500000
```

### GenericAccessor.rolling_pattern_similarity | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L1272-L1395)

```python
GenericAccessor.rolling_pattern_similarity(
    pattern,
    window=None,
    max_window=None,
    row_select_prob=1.0,
    window_select_prob=1.0,
    interp_mode='mixed',
    rescale_mode='minmax',
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type='absolute',
    distance_measure='mae',
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None,
    max_error_as_maxdist=False,
    max_error_strict=False,
    min_pct_change=nan,
    max_pct_change=nan,
    min_similarity=nan,
    minp=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None

```

Compute rolling pattern similarity.

__See__

[rolling_pattern_similarity_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/rolling/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.rolling_pattern_similarity_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.rolling_pattern_similarity_nb")

__Args__

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Reference pattern array for similarity comparison.

**```window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Window size.

    Defaults to the length of `pattern`.

**```max_window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Maximum length of the rolling window for matching.

    If None, defaults to `window`.

**```row_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a row.

**```window_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a window size.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Interpolation mode.

    Mapped using [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode") if provided as a string.

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Rescaling mode.

    Mapped using [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode") if provided as a string.

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Error calculation type.

    Mapped using [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType") if provided as a string.

**```distance_measure```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Distance measure for error computation.

    Mapped using [DistanceMeasure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure") if provided as a string.

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Maximum allowed error.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, str]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    Mapped using [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode") if provided as a string.

**```max_error_as_maxdist```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether `max_error` represents the maximum distance at each point.

**```max_error_strict```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, any instance of exceeding `max_error` results in a similarity of NaN.

**```min_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum percent change applied during rescaling.

**```max_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum percentage change allowed for a window to remain a search candidate.

**```min_similarity```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum similarity threshold.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Rolling pattern similarity result.

### GenericAccessor.squeeze_grouped | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L3067-L3227)

```python
GenericAccessor.squeeze_grouped(
    squeeze_func_nb,
    *args,
    broadcast_named_args=None,
    broadcast_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    wrapper=None,
    group_by=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None
)
```

Squeeze each group of columns into a single column.

__See__

* [squeeze_grouped_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_nb") for the standard version.

* [squeeze_grouped_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_meta_nb") for the meta version.

__Args__

**```squeeze_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Union[str, AnyGroupSqueezeFunc]`
:   Callback function for squeezing groups.

    For specification, see the underlying Numba function.

    If provided as a string, selects the corresponding Numba callback function
    from [vectorbtpro.generic.nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb") with the suffix `_reduce_nb`.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `squeeze_func_nb`.

**```broadcast_named_args```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional named arguments for broadcasting.

    Use templates such as [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep") to substitute
    callback function arguments with their broadcasted values.

**```broadcast_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for broadcasting.

    See [broadcast](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.broadcast").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayWrapper]`
:   Array wrapper instance.

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification.

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

__Returns__

`MaybeSeriesFrame`
:   Squeezed data as a Series or DataFrame.

__Examples__

Using regular function:

```pycon
>>> mean_nb = njit(lambda a: np.nanmean(a))

>>> group_by = pd.Series(['first', 'first', 'second'], name='group')
>>> df.vbt.squeeze_grouped(mean_nb, group_by=group_by)
group       first  second
2020-01-01    3.0     1.0
2020-01-02    3.0     2.0
2020-01-03    3.0     3.0
2020-01-04    3.0     2.0
2020-01-05    3.0     1.0
```

Using meta function:

```pycon
>>> mean_ratio_meta_nb = njit(lambda i, group_idxs, group, a, b: \
...     np.mean(a[i][group_idxs]) / np.mean(b[i][group_idxs]))

>>> vbt.pd_acc.squeeze_grouped(
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() - 1,
...     df.vbt.to_2d_array() + 1,
...     wrapper=df.vbt.wrapper,
...     group_by=group_by
... )
group       first    second
2020-01-01    0.5  0.000000
2020-01-02    0.5  0.333333
2020-01-03    0.5  0.500000
2020-01-04    0.5  0.333333
2020-01-05    0.5  0.000000
```

Using templates and broadcasting:

```pycon
>>> vbt.pd_acc.squeeze_grouped(
...     mean_ratio_meta_nb,
...     vbt.Rep('a'),
...     vbt.Rep('b'),
...     broadcast_named_args=dict(
...         a=pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], index=df.index),
...         b=pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3]], columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])
...     ),
...     group_by=[0, 0, 1]
... )
                    0         1
2020-01-01  0.666667  0.333333
2020-01-02  1.333333  0.666667
2020-01-03  2.000000  1.000000
2020-01-04  2.666667  1.333333
2020-01-05  3.333333  1.666667
```

### GenericAccessor.std | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L4209-L4272)

```python
GenericAccessor.std(
    ddof=1,
    use_jitted=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    group_by=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None
)
```

Return the standard deviation of non-NaN elements.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [generic](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.generic "vectorbtpro._settings.generic").

__See__

* [std_reduce_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.std_reduce_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.std_reduce_nb") for grouped operations.

* [nanstd_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.nanstd_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.nanstd_nb") for non-grouped operations.

__Args__

**```ddof```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Delta degrees of freedom.

**```use_jitted```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Whether to use jitted execution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification.

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

### GenericAccessor.transform | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L5059-L5110)

```python
GenericAccessor.transform(
    transformer,
    wrap_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Transform the data using the specified transformer.

Applies the given transformer to the dataset. The transformer must be an instance with
`transform` and `fit_transform` methods, ideally subclassing `sklearn.base.TransformerMixin`
and `sklearn.base.BaseEstimator`.

If the transformer is not already fitted, it is fitted using `fit_transform`;
otherwise, `transform` is applied.

__Args__

**```transformer```** :&ensp;`Transformer`
:   Instance with `transform` and `fit_transform` methods.

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for the transformer methods.

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Transformed data as a Series or DataFrame.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler

>>> df.vbt.transform(MinMaxScaler((-1, 1)))
              a    b    c
2020-01-01 -1.0  1.0 -1.0
2020-01-02 -0.5  0.5  0.0
2020-01-03  0.0  0.0  1.0
2020-01-04  0.5 -0.5  0.0
2020-01-05  1.0 -1.0 -1.0

>>> fitted_scaler = MinMaxScaler((-1, 1)).fit(np.array([[2], [4]]))
>>> df.vbt.transform(fitted_scaler)
              a    b    c
2020-01-01 -2.0  2.0 -2.0
2020-01-02 -1.0  1.0 -1.0
2020-01-03  0.0  0.0  0.0
2020-01-04  1.0 -1.0 -1.0
2020-01-05  2.0 -2.0 -2.0
```

### GenericAccessor.value_counts | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L4826-L5019)

```python
GenericAccessor.value_counts(
    axis=1,
    normalize=False,
    sort_uniques=True,
    sort=False,
    ascending=False,
    dropna=False,
    group_by=None,
    mapping=None,
    incl_all_keys=False,
    jitted=None,

    wrap_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Return a Series/DataFrame containing counts of unique values.

__See__

* [value_counts_per_row_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_per_row_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_per_row_nb") for `axis=0`.

* [value_counts_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_nb") for `axis=1`.

* [value_counts_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.value_counts_1d_nb") for `axis=-1`.

__Args__

**```axis```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Axis along which to compute counts.

    Valid options:

    * 0: Count per row.

    * 1: Count per column.

    * -1: Count across the entire object.

**```normalize```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return relative frequencies of unique values.

**```sort_uniques```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Sort unique values before further processing.

**```sort```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Sort the results based on frequency counts.

**```ascending```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   True for ascending order, False for descending.

**```dropna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Exclude NaN values from the counts.

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification.

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```mapping```** :&ensp;`Union[None, bool, MappingLike]`
:   Mapping to relabel unique values.

**```incl_all_keys```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Include keys from `mapping` that are missing in the data.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [apply_mapping](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/mapping/#vectorbtpro.utils.mapping.apply_mapping "vectorbtpro.utils.mapping.apply_mapping").

__Returns__

`SeriesFrame`
:   Series or DataFrame with counts of unique values.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> df.vbt.value_counts()
    a  b  c
1  1  1  2
2  1  1  2
3  1  1  1
4  1  1  0
5  1  1  0

>>> df.vbt.value_counts(axis=-1)
1    4
2    4
3    3
4    2
5    2
Name: value_counts, dtype: int64

>>> mapping = {x: 'test_' + str(x) for x in pd.unique(df.values.flatten())}
>>> df.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping)
        a  b  c
test_1  1  1  2
test_2  1  1  2
test_3  1  1  1
test_4  1  1  0
test_5  1  1  0

>>> sr = pd.Series([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, np.nan])
>>> sr.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping)
test_1    1
test_2    2
test_3    3
NaN       1
dtype: int64

>>> sr.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping, dropna=True)
test_1    1
test_2    2
test_3    3
dtype: int64

>>> sr.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping, sort=True)
test_3    3
test_2    2
test_1    1
NaN       1
dtype: int64

>>> sr.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping, sort=True, ascending=True)
test_1    1
NaN       1
test_2    2
test_3    3
dtype: int64

>>> sr.vbt.value_counts(mapping=mapping, incl_all_keys=True)
test_1    1
test_2    2
test_3    3
test_4    0
test_5    0
NaN       1
dtype: int64
```

### GenericDFAccessor.band | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L7258-L7362)

```python
GenericDFAccessor.band(
    band_name,
    return_meta=False
)
```

Calculate the band value based on the given band name.

__Args__

**```band_name```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Band name determining the calculation.

    Possible values include:

    * "50%": 50th quantile.

    * "Q=50%": 50th quantile.

    * "Q=0.5": 50th quantile.

    * "Z=1.96": Z-score of 1.96.

    * "P=95%": One-tailed significance level of 0.95 (translated into z-score).

    * "P=0.95": One-tailed significance level of 0.95 (translated into z-score).

    * "median": Median (50th quantile).

    * "mean": Mean across all columns.

    * "min": Minimum across all columns.

    * "max": Maximum across all columns.

    * "lowest": Column with the lowest final value.

    * "highest": Column with the highest final value.

**```return_meta```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to return metadata including band details.

__Returns__

`Union[Series, dict]`
:   Computed band as a Series if `return_meta` is False, or a dict containing
    band metadata (`band_name`, `band_title`, and `band_func`) if `return_meta` is True.

### GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L7364-L7760)

```python
GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections(
    plot_projections=True,
    plot_bands=True,
    plot_lower=True,
    plot_middle=True,
    plot_upper=True,
    plot_aux_middle=True,
    plot_fill=True,
    colorize=True,
    rename_levels=None,
    projection_trace_kwargs=None,
    lower_trace_kwargs=None,
    middle_trace_kwargs=None,
    upper_trace_kwargs=None,
    aux_middle_trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Plot DataFrame columns as projections with optional bands and colorization.

Plots each column of the DataFrame as a projection line. Optionally, bands
(lower, middle, upper, and auxiliary middle) are computed and plotted to provide
additional context. Projections are drawn with semi-transparent lines, and
colorization is applied based on band metrics if specified.

!!! note
    When using z-scores, the upper band should be positive, the middle computed as "mean", and
    the lower negative. For significance levels, the middle remains "mean" whereas the lower should be
    positive and lower than the upper (e.g., 25% and 75%).

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```plot_projections```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot each projection as a semi-transparent line if True.

**```plot_bands```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot computed bands if True.

    Disabled for single-column DataFrames.

**```plot_lower```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Specification for the lower band.

    Accepts:

    * True: Compute using the default "20%" quantile.

    * False: Do not plot the band.

    * str: Use a custom band identifier.

    * Callable: Function to compute the band by reducing the DataFrame.

**```plot_middle```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Specification for the middle band.

    Accepts:

    * True: Compute using the default "50%" quantile.

    * False: Do not plot the band.

    * str: Use a custom band identifier.

    * Callable: Function to compute the band by reducing the DataFrame.

**```plot_upper```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Specification for the upper band.

    Accepts:

    * True: Compute using the default "80%" quantile.

    * False: Do not plot the band.

    * str: Use a custom band identifier.

    * Callable: Function to compute the band by reducing the DataFrame.

**```plot_aux_middle```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Specification for an auxiliary middle band.

    Accepts:

    * True: Compute using "mean".

    * False: Do not plot the band.

    * str: Use a custom band identifier.

    * Callable: Function to compute the band by reducing the DataFrame.

**```plot_fill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Fill the area between band traces if True.

**```colorize```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Strategy for colorizing projections or bands.

    Accepts:

    * False: Do not colorize.

    * True or "median": Colorize by median.

    * "mean": Colorize by mean.

    * "last": Colorize by last value.

    * Callable: Function that reduces a Series or DataFrame to compute a metric.

**```rename_levels```** :&ensp;`Union[None, dict, Sequence]`
:   Mapping or sequence to rename multi-index legend levels.

**```projection_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the projections.

**```lower_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the lower band.

**```middle_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the middle band.

**```upper_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the upper band.

**```aux_middle_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the auxiliary middle band.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Updated figure with plotted projections and bands.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     0: [10, 11, 12, 11, 10],
...     1: [10, 12, 14, np.nan, np.nan],
...     2: [10, 12, 11, 12, np.nan],
...     3: [10, 9, 8, 9, 8],
...     4: [10, 11, np.nan, np.nan, np.nan],
... })
>>> df.vbt.plot_projections().show()
```

## GenericSRAccessor | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/accessors.py#L7029-L7230)

```python
GenericSRAccessor(
    wrapper,
    obj=None,
    mapping=None,
    **kwargs
```

```python
GenericSRAccessor.fit_pattern(
    pattern,
    interp_mode='mixed',
    rescale_mode='minmax',
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type='absolute',
    max_error=nan,

    jitted=None
)
```

Fit a pattern on the series data using [fit_pattern_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/patterns/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.fit_pattern_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.fit_pattern_nb").

__Args__

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Reference pattern array for similarity comparison.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Interpolation mode.

    Mapped using [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode") if provided as a string.

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Rescaling mode.

    Mapped using [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode") if provided as a string.

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`Union[int, str]`
:   Error calculation type.

    Mapped using [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType") if provided as a string.

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Maximum allowed error.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, str]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    Mapped using [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode") if provided as a string.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Series, Series]`
:   Tuple containing the fitted pattern series and the maximum error series.

:   Maximum length of the output.

**```reset_index```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to reset the index in the resulting Series.

**```return_uptrend```** :&ensp;`bool`

`Union[Series, Tuple[Series, Series]]`

    the Renko series and the uptrend series.

# vectorbtpro.generic.decorators | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/decorators.py)

Module providing class decorators for generic accessors.

## attach_nb_methods | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/decorators.py#L25-L113)

```python
attach_nb_methods(
    config
)
```

Class decorator to attach Numba methods to a class.

The decorated class must be a subclass of [Wrapping](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.Wrapping "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.Wrapping").

__Args__

**```config```** :&ensp;`Config`
:   Dictionary mapping target method names (str) to
    configuration dictionaries with the following keys:

    * `func` (Callable): Function to be wrapped, where the first argument accepts a 2-dim array.

    * `is_reducing` (bool): Specifies if the function performs a reduction.

    * `disable_jitted` (bool): Disables the jitted option when set.

    * `disable_chunked` (bool): Disables the chunked option when set.

    * `replace_signature` (bool): Replaces the target method signature with
        that of the source function.

    * `wrap_kwargs` (KwargsLike): Keyword arguments for wrapping that
        will be merged with user-supplied values.

__Returns__

`ClassWrapper`
:   Decorated class with the new methods attached.

## attach_transform_methods | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/decorators.py#L116-L176)

```python
attach_transform_methods(

```

Class decorator to add transformation methods to a class.

The decorated class must be a subclass of [GenericAccessor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor").

__Args__

**```config```** :&ensp;`Config`
:   Dictionary mapping target method names (str) to
    configuration dictionaries with the following keys:

    * `transformer` (MaybeType[Transformer]): Transformer class or instance.

    * `docstring` (str): Docstring assigned to the generated method.

    * `replace_signature` (bool): Replaces the target method signature with that of the transformer.

__Returns__

`ClassWrapper`
:   Decorated class with the new methods attached.

# vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/drawdowns.py)

Module providing the base class for managing drawdown records.

Drawdown records capture critical information about drawdown intervals and are
implemented as a subclass of [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges").

!!! warning
    [Drawdowns](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/drawdowns/#vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns "vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns") include both recovered and active drawdowns, which may skew performance
    results.

    To focus on recovered drawdowns only, explicitly use the `status_recovered` attribute.

Call [Drawdowns.from_price](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/drawdowns/#vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns.from_price "vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns.from_price") to generate drawdown records from any time series for
immediate analysis.

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> price = vbt.YFData.pull(
...     "BTC-USD",
...     start="2019-10 UTC",
...     end="2020-01 UTC"
... ).get('Close')
```

[=100% "100%"]{: .candystripe .candystripe-animate }

```pycon
>>> price = price.rename(None)

>>> drawdowns = vbt.Drawdowns.from_price(price, wrapper_kwargs=dict(freq='d'))

>>> drawdowns.readable
    Drawdown Id  Column               Start Index              Valley Index  \
0            0       0 2019-10-02 00:00:00+00:00 2019-10-06 00:00:00+00:00
1            1       0 2019-10-09 00:00:00+00:00 2019-10-24 00:00:00+00:00
2            2       0 2019-10-27 00:00:00+00:00 2019-12-17 00:00:00+00:00

                  End Index   Peak Value  Valley Value    End Value     Status
0 2019-10-09 00:00:00+00:00  8393.041992   7988.155762  8595.740234  Recovered
1 2019-10-25 00:00:00+00:00  8595.740234   7493.488770  8660.700195  Recovered
2 2019-12-31 00:00:00+00:00  9551.714844   6640.515137  7193.599121     Active

>>> drawdowns.duration.max(wrap_kwargs=dict(to_timedelta=True))
Timedelta('66 days 00:00:00')
```

## From accessors

Generic accessors provide a `drawdowns` property and a `get_drawdowns` method:

```pycon
>>> # vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.drawdowns.coverage
>>> price.vbt.drawdowns.coverage
0.967391304347826
```

## Stats

!!! tip
    See [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats") and [Drawdowns.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/drawdowns/#vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns.metrics "vectorbtpro.generic.drawdowns.Drawdowns.metrics").

```pycon
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     'a': [1, 2, 1, 3, 2],
...     'b': [2, 3, 1, 2, 1]
... })

>>> drawdowns = df.vbt(freq='d').drawdowns

>>> drawdowns['a'].stats()
Start                                        0
End                                          4
Period                         5 days 00:00:00
Coverage [%]                              80.0
Total Records                                2
Total Recovered Drawdowns                    1
Total Active Drawdowns                       1

Active Duration                2 days 00:00:00
Active Recovery [%]                        0.0
Active Recovery Return [%]                 0.0
Active Recovery Duration       0 days 00:00:00
Max Drawdown [%]                          50.0
Avg Drawdown [%]                          50.0
Max Drawdown Duration          2 days 00:00:00
Avg Drawdown Duration          2 days 00:00:00
Max Recovery Return [%]                  200.0
Avg Recovery Return [%]                  200.0

Avg Recovery Duration Ratio                1.0
Name: a, dtype: object
```

exclude active drawdowns. To include active drawdowns, pass `incl_active=True`:


## Drawdowns | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/drawdowns.py#L278-L1502)

Class extending [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges") for working with drawdown records.

Requires `records_arr` to have all fields defined in [drawdown_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.drawdown_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.drawdown_dt").

!!! info
    For default settings, see [drawdowns](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.drawdowns "vectorbtpro._settings.drawdowns").

```python
        start_idx=dict(
            title='Start Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        end_idx=dict(
            title='End Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        status=dict(
            title='Status',
            mapping=DrawdownStatusT(
                Active=0,
                Recovered=1
            )
        ),
        valley_idx=dict(
            title='Valley Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        start_val=dict(
            title='Start Value'
        ),
        valley_val=dict(
            title='Valley Value'
        ),
        end_val=dict(
            title='End Value'
        )
    )
)
```

### Drawdowns.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/drawdowns.py#L1106-L1471)

```python
Drawdowns.plot(
    column=None,
    top_n=5,
    plot_ohlc=True,
    plot_close=True,
    plot_markers=True,
    plot_zones=True,
    ohlc_type=None,
    ohlc_trace_kwargs=None,
    close_trace_kwargs=None,
    peak_trace_kwargs=None,
    valley_trace_kwargs=None,
    recovery_trace_kwargs=None,
    active_trace_kwargs=None,
    decline_shape_kwargs=None,
    recovery_shape_kwargs=None,
    active_shape_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    xref='x',
    yref='y',
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Plot drawdowns.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```top_n```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Display only the top N records sorted by maximum duration.

**```plot_ohlc```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to plot the OHLC data.

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to plot the close price if OHLC data is not plotted.

**```plot_markers```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot markers for significant drawdown events.

**```plot_zones```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot zones delineating drawdown phases.

**```ohlc_type```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, BaseTraceType]`
:   Specifies the OHLC plot type.

    Use 'OHLC', 'Candlestick', or a Plotly trace type. Pass None to use the default.

**```ohlc_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `ohlc_type` for the OHLC data.

**```close_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the close price.

**```peak_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for peak markers.

**```valley_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for valley markers.

**```recovery_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for recovery markers.

**```active_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for active recovery markers.

**```decline_shape_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_shape` for shapes representing decline zones.

**```recovery_shape_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_shape` for shapes representing recovery zones.

**```active_shape_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_shape` for shapes representing active recovery zones.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```xref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the x-axis (e.g., "x", "x2").

**```yref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the y-axis (e.g., "y", "y2").

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Figure object containing the plotted drawdowns and price data.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> index = pd.date_range("2020", periods=8)
>>> price = pd.Series([1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2], index=index)
>>> vbt.Drawdowns.from_price(price, wrapper_kwargs=dict(freq='1 day')).plot().show()
```

## InterpMode | named tuple | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/enums.py#L129-L130)

Interpolation mode enumeration.

```python
InterpModeT(
    Linear=0,
    Nearest=1,
    Discrete=2,
    Mixed=3
)
```

__Fields__

**```Linear```**
:   Linear interpolation.

    For example: `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` to 5 yields `[1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0]`

**```Nearest```**
:   Nearest-neighbor interpolation.

    For example: `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` to 5 yields `[1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 3.0]`

**```Discrete```**
:   Discrete interpolation.

    For example: `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` to 5 yields `[1.0, np.nan, 2.0, np.nan, 3.0]`

**```Mixed```**
:   Mixed interpolation.

    For example: `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` to 5 yields `[1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0]`

## OverlapMode | named tuple | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/enums.py#L244-L245)

Overlap mode enumeration.

```python
OverlapModeT(
    AllowAll=-2,
    Allow=-1,
    Disallow=0
)
```

__Fields__

**```AllowAll```**
:   Allows any overlapping ranges, including those starting at the same row.

**```Allow```**
:   Allows overlapping ranges only if they do not share the same starting row.

**```Disallow```**
:   Disallows any overlapping ranges.

Any other positive number specifies a minimum number of overlapping rows required to 
select the range with the highest similarity.

## RangeStatus | named tuple | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/enums.py#L109-L110)

## RescaleMode | named tuple | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/enums.py#L162-L163)

Rescaling mode enumeration.

```python
RescaleModeT(
    MinMax=0,
    Rebase=1,
    Disable=2
)
```

__Fields__

**```MinMax```**
:   Rescales an array from its min-max range to match the min-max range of another array.

    For example: `[3.0, 2.0, 1.0]` to `[10, 11, 12]` yields `[12.0, 11.0, 10.0]`

    Use this to search for patterns irrespective of their vertical scale.

**```Rebase```**
:   Rebases an array to the first value of another array.

    For example: `[3.0, 2.0, 1.0]` to `[10, 11, 12]` yields `[10.0, 6.6, 3.3]`

    Use this to search for percentage changes.

**```Disable```**
:   Disables rescaling, leaving the array unchanged.

    For example: `[3.0, 2.0, 1.0]` to `[10, 11, 12]` yields `[3.0, 2.0, 1.0]`

    Use this to search for particular numbers.

### PlotsBuilderMixin.plots | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plots_builder.py#L121-L896)

```python
PlotsBuilderMixin.plots(
    subplots=None,
    tags=None,
    column=None,
    group_by=None,
    per_column=None,
    split_columns=None,
    silence_warnings=None,
    template_context=None,
    settings=None,
    filters=None,
    subplot_settings=None,
    show_titles=None,
    show_legend=None,
    show_column_label=None,
    hide_id_labels=None,
    group_id_labels=None,
    make_subplots_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Plot various parts of this object.

!!! note
    [PlotsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plots_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin") and [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin")
    share similar designs, differing mainly in nomenclature:

    * `plots_defaults` vs `stats_defaults`

    * `subplots` vs `metrics`

    * `subplot_settings` vs `metric_settings`

    See further details in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```subplots```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeIterable[Union[str, Tuple[str, Kwargs]]]]`
:   Subplots to plot.

    Each element may be:

    * Subplot name (as defined in [PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plots_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots "vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots")).

    * Tuple containing a subplot name and a settings dictionary
        (as defined in [PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plots_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots "vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots")).

    * Tuple containing a subplot name and a [CustomTemplate](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.CustomTemplate "vectorbtpro.utils.template.CustomTemplate") instance.

    * Tuple containing a subplot name and a list of settings dictionaries
        to be expanded into multiple subplots.

    The settings dictionary may include:

    * `title`: Subplot title; defaults to the subplot name.

    * `plot_func` (required): Plotting function for custom subplots.
        It must modify the provided figure `fig` in-place.

    * `xaxis_kwargs`: Layout keyword arguments for the x-axis;
        defaults to `{'title': 'Index'}`.

    * `yaxis_kwargs`: Layout keyword arguments for the y-axis;
        defaults to an empty dict.

    * `tags`, `check_{filter}`, `inv_check_{filter}`, `resolve_plot_func`,
        `pass_{arg}`, `resolve_path_{arg}`, `resolve_{arg}`, and `template_context`:
        As described in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin") for `calc_func`.

    * Any additional keyword argument that overrides settings or is passed directly to `plot_func`.

    If `resolve_plot_func` is True, the plotting function may request extra parameters
    by accepting them or if `pass_{arg}` was found in the settings dictionary:

    * Each alias from [AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases")
        representing the original object (ungrouped, without column selection).

    * `group_by` (unless already used to resolve the first attribute of `plot_func`;
        use `pass_group_by=True` to force its inclusion).

    * `column`

    * `subplot_name`

    * `trace_names`: List containing the subplot name (cannot be used in templates).

    * `add_trace_kwargs`: Dict with subplot row and column index.

    * `xref`

    * `yref`

    * `xaxis`

    * `yaxis`

    * `x_domain`

    * `y_domain`

    * `fig`

    * `silence_warnings`

    * Any parameter from `settings`

    * Any attribute of the object intended for resolution
        (see [AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr")).

    !!! note
        Layout-related resolution arguments (such as `add_trace_kwargs`) are unavailable
        before filtering and cannot be used in templates, though they may still be overridden.

    Pass `subplots='all'` to plot all supported subplots.

**```tags```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeIterable[str]]`
:   Tag or tags to filter metrics, as described in
    [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot, as described in
    [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification, as described in
    [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag indicating whether to plot per column,
    as in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag indicating whether to split columns,
    as in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```filters```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Filters as specified in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings as specified in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin").

**```subplot_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Subplot-specific settings, analogous to
    `metric_settings` in `StatsBuilderMixin`.

**```show_titles```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to display titles for subplots.

**```show_legend```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Whether to display the legend.

    If None and plotting per column, the value is inferred.

**```show_column_label```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Whether to display the column label next to each legend label.

    If None and plotting per column, the value is inferred.

**```hide_id_labels```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to hide duplicate legend labels (duplicates have the same name,
    marker style, and line style).

**```group_id_labels```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to group identical legend labels.

**```make_subplots_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making subplots.

    See [make_subplots](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_subplots "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_subplots").

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Plotly figure containing subplots.

### PlotsBuilderMixin.subplots | property | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plots_builder.py#L102-L119)

Subplots configuration for [PlotsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plots_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin").

```python
HybridConfig()
```

This property returns a hybrid copy of `PlotsBuilderMixin._subplots` created at instance initialization,
ensuring that modifications do not affect the class-level configuration.

To modify the subplots, update the configuration in-place, override this property, or assign a new value
to `PlotsBuilderMixin._subplots` on the instance.

__Returns__

`Config`
:   Hybrid copy of the subplots configuration.

# vectorbtpro.generic.plotting | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py)

Module providing base plotting functions.

Provides functions to visualize data using interactive figure widgets that integrate with
ipywidgets in Jupyter Notebook and JupyterLab.

For more details on using Plotly, refer to
[Getting Started with Plotly in Python](https://plotly.com/python/getting-started/).

!!! warning
    Errors related to plotting in the Jupyter environment may appear in the logs rather than in the cell output.

## clean_data | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L75-L89)
