## Bar | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L334-L466)

```python
Bar(
    data=None,
    trace_names=None,
    x_labels=None,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a bar plot.

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    Must have shape corresponding to (`x_labels`, `trace_names`).

**```trace_names```** :&ensp;`TraceNames`
:   Names for traces corresponding to data columns.

**```x_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   X-axis labels corresponding to the index in pandas.

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLikeSequence`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Bar`.

    Can be provided per trace as a sequence of dictionaries.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> bar = vbt.Bar(
...     data=[[1, 2], [3, 4]],
...     trace_names=['a', 'b'],
...     x_labels=['x', 'y']
... )
>>> bar.fig.show()
```

## Box | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L875-L1104)

```python
Box(
    data=None,
    trace_names=None,
    horizontal=False,
    remove_nan=True,
    from_quantile=None,
    to_quantile=None,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a box plot.

This class creates a box plot from the provided data and configuration parameters.
For additional keyword arguments for trace customization, see [Histogram](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plotting/#vectorbtpro.generic.plotting.Histogram "vectorbtpro.generic.plotting.Histogram").

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    The second axis must correspond to `trace_names`.

**```trace_names```** :&ensp;`TraceNames`
:   Names for traces corresponding to data columns.

**```horizontal```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the plot is oriented horizontally.

**```remove_nan```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag determining whether NaN values are removed from the data.

**```from_quantile```** :&ensp;`Optional[float]`
:   Lower quantile threshold to filter out data.

    Data below this quantile are excluded.

**```to_quantile```** :&ensp;`Optional[float]`
:   Upper quantile threshold to filter out data.

    Data above this quantile are excluded.

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLikeSequence`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Box`.

    Can be provided per trace as a sequence of dictionaries.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> box = vbt.Box(
...     data=[[1, 2], [3, 4], [2, 1]],
...     trace_names=['a', 'b']
... )
>>> box.fig.show()
```

### Box.update_trace | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L1035-L1081)

```python
Box.update_trace(
    trace,
    data,
    i,
    horizontal=False,
    remove_nan=True,
    from_quantile=None,
    to_quantile=None
)
```

Update a single box trace with new data.

__Args__

**```trace```** :&ensp;`BaseTraceType`
:   Plotly trace to update.

**```data```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    The second axis must correspond to `trace_names`.

**```i```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Index of the trace to update.

**```horizontal```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the plot is oriented horizontally.

**```remove_nan```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag determining whether NaN values are removed from the data.

**```from_quantile```** :&ensp;`Optional[float]`
:   Lower quantile threshold to filter out data.

    Data below this quantile are excluded.

**```to_quantile```** :&ensp;`Optional[float]`
:   Upper quantile threshold to filter out data.

    Data above this quantile are excluded.

__Returns__

None

## Gauge | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L162-L331)

```python
Gauge(
    value=None,
    label=None,
    value_range=None,
    cmap_name='Spectral',
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a gauge plot.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```value```** :&ensp;`Optional[float]`
:   Value to display on the gauge.

**```label```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Label shown on the gauge.

**```value_range```** :&ensp;`Optional[Tuple[float, float]]`
:   Range of values for the gauge.

**```cmap_name```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Matplotlib-compatible colormap name.

    See the [list of available colormaps](https://matplotlib.org/tutorials/colors/colormaps.html).

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Indicator`.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> gauge = vbt.Gauge(
...     value=2,
...     value_range=(1, 3),
...     label='My Gauge'
... )
>>> gauge.fig.show()
```

## Heatmap | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L1107-L1263)

```python
Heatmap(
    data=None,
    x_labels=None,
    y_labels=None,
    is_x_category=False,
    is_y_category=False,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a heatmap plot.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    Must have shape (`y_labels`, `x_labels`).

**```x_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the x-axis corresponding to DataFrame columns.

**```y_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the y-axis corresponding to DataFrame index.

**```is_x_category```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether the x-axis represents categorical data.

**```is_y_category```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to treat the y-axis as categorical.

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Heatmap`.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> heatmap = vbt.Heatmap(
...     data=[[1, 2], [3, 4]],
...     x_labels=['a', 'b'],
...     y_labels=['x', 'y']
... )
>>> heatmap.fig.show()
```

## Histogram | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L641-L872)

```python
Histogram(
    data=None,
    trace_names=None,
    horizontal=False,
    remove_nan=True,
    from_quantile=None,
    to_quantile=None,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a histogram plot.

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    The second axis must correspond to `trace_names`.

**```trace_names```** :&ensp;`TraceNames`
:   Names for traces corresponding to data columns.

**```horizontal```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the plot is oriented horizontally.

**```remove_nan```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag determining whether NaN values are removed from the data.

**```from_quantile```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Lower quantile threshold used to filter out data points.

    Must be in the range [0, 1].

**```to_quantile```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Upper quantile threshold used to filter out data points.

    Must be in the range [0, 1].

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLikeSequence`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Histogram`.

    Can be provided per trace as a sequence of dictionaries.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> hist = vbt.Histogram(
...     data=[[1, 2], [3, 4], [2, 1]],
...     trace_names=['a', 'b']
... )
>>> hist.fig.show()
```

### Histogram.update_trace | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L803-L849)

```python
Histogram.update_trace(
    trace,
    data,
    i,
    horizontal=False,
    remove_nan=True,
    from_quantile=None,
    to_quantile=None
)
```

Update a single histogram trace with new data.

__Args__

**```trace```** :&ensp;`BaseTraceType`
:   Plotly trace to update.

**```data```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    The second axis must correspond to `trace_names`.

**```i```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Index of the trace to update.

**```horizontal```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the plot is oriented horizontally.

**```remove_nan```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag determining whether NaN values are removed from the data.

**```from_quantile```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Lower quantile threshold used to filter out data points.

    Must be in the range [0, 1].

**```to_quantile```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Upper quantile threshold used to filter out data points.

    Must be in the range [0, 1].

__Returns__

None

## Scatter | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L469-L638)

```python
Scatter(
    data=None,
    trace_names=None,
    x_labels=None,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    use_webgl=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a scatter plot.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    Must have shape corresponding to (`x_labels`, `trace_names`).

**```trace_names```** :&ensp;`TraceNames`
:   Names for traces corresponding to data columns.

**```x_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the x-axis, typically representing the index in a Pandas DataFrame.

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLikeSequence`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter`.

    Can be provided per trace as a sequence of dictionaries.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```use_webgl```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag to use `plotly.graph_objects.Scattergl`.

    If the global configuration is True and the data has more than 10,000 points,
    this flag becomes True.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> scatter = vbt.Scatter(
...     data=[[1, 2], [3, 4]],
...     trace_names=['a', 'b'],
...     x_labels=['x', 'y']
... )
>>> scatter.fig.show()
```

## Volume | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/plotting.py#L1266-L1446)

```python
Volume(
    data=None,
    x_labels=None,
    y_labels=None,
    z_labels=None,
    trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    scene_name='scene',
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Class for creating a volume plot.

!!! note
    Figure widgets currently have issues displaying NaNs. Use the `.show()` method for rendering.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Data convertible to a NumPy array.

    Must have shape corresponding to (`x_labels`, `y_labels`, `z_labels`).

**```x_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the x-axis.

**```y_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the y-axis.

**```z_labels```** :&ensp;`Optional[Labels]`
:   Labels for the z-axis.

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Volume`.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```scene_name```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Name of the 3D scene.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> volume = vbt.Volume(
...     data=np.random.randint(1, 10, size=(3, 3, 3)),
...     x_labels=['a', 'b', 'c'],
...     y_labels=['d', 'e', 'f'],
...     z_labels=['g', 'h', 'i']
... )
>>> volume.fig.show()
```

# vectorbtpro.generic.ranges | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py)

Module for working with range records.

Range records capture information on time intervals. They are useful for analyzing durations
of processes, such as drawdowns, trades, and positions, as well as evaluating time between events
(e.g., entry and exit signals).

Each range has a starting and an ending point. For example, `range(20)` yields a start of 0 and
an end of 20 (not 19).

!!! note
    If a range remains open in a column, its `end_idx` points to the latest index.
    Ensure you account for this when calculating custom duration metrics.

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> start = '2019-01-01 UTC'  # crypto is in UTC
>>> end = '2020-01-01 UTC'
>>> price = vbt.YFData.pull('BTC-USD', start=start, end=end).get('Close')
```

[=100% "100%"]{: .candystripe .candystripe-animate }

```pycon
>>> fast_ma = vbt.MA.run(price, 10)
>>> slow_ma = vbt.MA.run(price, 50)
>>> fast_below_slow = fast_ma.ma_above(slow_ma)

>>> ranges = vbt.Ranges.from_array(fast_below_slow, wrapper_kwargs=dict(freq='d'))

>>> ranges.readable
    Range Id  Column           Start Timestamp             End Timestamp  \
0         0       0 2019-02-19 00:00:00+00:00 2019-07-25 00:00:00+00:00
1         1       0 2019-08-08 00:00:00+00:00 2019-08-19 00:00:00+00:00
2         2       0 2019-11-01 00:00:00+00:00 2019-11-20 00:00:00+00:00

    Status
0  Closed
1  Closed
2  Closed

>>> ranges.duration.max(wrap_kwargs=dict(to_timedelta=True))
Timedelta('156 days 00:00:00')
```

## From accessors

All generic accessors have a `ranges` property and a `get_ranges` method:

```pycon
>>> # vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericAccessor.ranges.coverage
>>> fast_below_slow.vbt.ranges.coverage
0.5081967213114754
```

## Stats

!!! tip
    See [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats") and [Ranges.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.metrics "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.metrics").

```pycon
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     'a': [1, 2, np.nan, np.nan, 5, 6],
...     'b': [np.nan, 2, np.nan, 4, np.nan, 6]
... })
>>> ranges = df.vbt(freq='d').ranges

>>> ranges['a'].stats()
Start                             0
End                               5
Period              6 days 00:00:00
Total Records                     2
Coverage                   0.666667
Overlap Coverage                0.0
Duration: Min       2 days 00:00:00
Duration: Median    2 days 00:00:00
Duration: Max       2 days 00:00:00
Name: a, dtype: object
```

[StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.stats") also supports re-grouping:

```pycon
>>> ranges.stats(group_by=True)
Start                                       0
End                                         5
Period                        6 days 00:00:00
Total Records                               5
Coverage                             0.416667
Overlap Coverage                          0.4
Duration: Min                 1 days 00:00:00
Duration: Median              1 days 00:00:00
Duration: Max                 2 days 00:00:00
Name: group, dtype: object
```

### PSC.max_error_as_maxdist | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L1995-L2001)

Indicates whether [PSC.max_error](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_error "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_error") represents the maximum distance at each point.

[PSC.pmin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pmin "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pmin"), [PSC.pmax](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pmax "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pmax"), and the pattern value at that point. If True and any point 
in a window is NaN, that point is skipped.

### PSC.vmax | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L1939-L1946)

Use only when the array has fixed bounds. Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax` 
and for verifying [PSC.min_pct_change](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.min_pct_change "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.min_pct_change") and [PSC.max_pct_change](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_pct_change "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_pct_change"). 

If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

## PatternRanges | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L2079-L2730)

```python
PatternRanges(
    wrapper,
    records_arr,
    search_configs,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class for working with range records generated from pattern search, extending [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges").

Requires `records_arr` to have all fields defined in [pattern_range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt").

__Args__

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`ArrayWrapper`
:   Array wrapper instance.

    See [ArrayWrapper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper").

**```records_arr```** :&ensp;`RecordArray`
:   Array of records.

    Must adhere to the [pattern_range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt") dtype.

**```search_configs```** :&ensp;`List[PSC]`
:   List of [PSC](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC") instances.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges").

### PatternRanges.from_pattern_search | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L2177-L2440)

```python
PatternRanges.from_pattern_search(
    arr,
    pattern=None,
    window=None,
    max_window=None,
    row_select_prob=1.0,
    window_select_prob=1.0,
    roll_forward=False,
    interp_mode='mixed',
    rescale_mode='minmax',
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type='absolute',
    distance_measure='mae',
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None,
    max_error_as_maxdist=False,
    max_error_strict=False,
    min_pct_change=nan,
    max_pct_change=nan,
    min_similarity=0.85,
    minp=None,
    overlap_mode='disallow',
    max_records=None,
    random_subset=None,
    seed=None,
    search_configs=None,
    jitted=None,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    attach_as_close=True,
    clean_index_kwargs=None,
    wrapper_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Build [PatternRanges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges") from all occurrences of a pattern in an array.

This class method searches for parameters of type [Param](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/params/#vectorbtpro.utils.params.Param "vectorbtpro.utils.params.Param") among the
provided arguments. If such parameters are found, they are broadcasted and combined via
[combine_params](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/params/#vectorbtpro.utils.params.combine_params "vectorbtpro.utils.params.combine_params") into one or more search configurations. If no `Param`
arguments are detected, a single search configuration is built from the given parameters.
When `search_configs` is supplied, it is used directly without modification. For example,
passing `min_similarity` of 95% will use it in all search configurations except where
it was explicitly overridden.

Each search configuration is resolved using [PatternRanges.resolve_search_config](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges.resolve_search_config "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges.resolve_search_config").
The configurations are executed with [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute"), the resulting
records arrays are concatenated, and the outcome is wrapped in a [PatternRanges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PatternRanges") instance.

__See__

[find_pattern_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/records/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.find_pattern_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.find_pattern_1d_nb")

    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```top_n```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Display only the top N records sorted by maximum duration.

**```fit_ranges```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, MaybeSequence[int]]`
:   Select the range records to fit.

    Use True to fit all records, or provide an integer or sequence of
    integers to select specific records.

**```plot_patterns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether to plot the [PSC.pattern](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pattern "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.pattern").

**```plot_max_error```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether to plot the [PSC.max_error](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_error "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.PSC.max_error").

**```fill_distance```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Controls whether to fill the space between close and pattern.

    Visible for every interpolation mode except discrete.

**```pattern_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the pattern.

**```lower_max_error_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the lower error bound.

**```upper_max_error_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the upper error bound.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```xref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the x-axis (e.g., "x", "x2").

**```yref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the y-axis (e.g., "y", "y2").

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Ranges.plot](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.plot "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.plot").

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Figure with plotted pattern ranges.

## Ranges | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L225-L1871)

```python
Ranges(
    wrapper,
    records_arr,
    open=None,
    high=None,
    low=None,
    close=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class for handling range records that extends [PriceRecords](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/price_records/#vectorbtpro.generic.price_records.PriceRecords "vectorbtpro.generic.price_records.PriceRecords").

Requires `records_arr` to have all fields defined in [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt").

!!! info
    For default settings, see [ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.ranges "vectorbtpro._settings.ranges").

```python
Ranges.crop()
```

Crop the range records to the valid index span.

Trims the data to include only records between the minimum start index and
one more than the maximum end index.

__Returns__

### Ranges.field_config | property | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L237-L239)

```python
HybridConfig(
    dtype=np.dtype([
        ('id', 'int64'),
        ('col', 'int64'),
        ('start_idx', 'int64'),
        ('end_idx', 'int64'),
        ('status', 'int64')
    ]),
    settings=dict(
        id=dict(
            name='id',
            title='Range Id',
            mapping='ids'
        ),
        col=dict(
            name='col',
            title='Column',
            mapping='columns',
            as_customdata=False
        ),
        idx=dict(
            name='end_idx',
            title='Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        start_idx=dict(
            title='Start Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        end_idx=dict(
            title='End Index',
            mapping='index'
        ),
        status=dict(
            title='Status',
            mapping=RangeStatusT(
                Open=0,
                Closed=1
            )
        )
    )
)
```

To modify the fields, update the config in-place, override this property,
or set `Ranges._field_config` on the instance.

    do not affect the class-level configuration.

### Ranges.from_array | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L241-L300)

```python
Ranges.from_array(
    arr,
    gap_value=None,
    attach_as_close=True,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    wrapper_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Build [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges") from an array.

Constructs a [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges") instance by identifying consecutive sequences of valid data points.

It searches for sequences of:

* True values in boolean arrays (with False as a gap),

* Positive integers in integer arrays (with -1 as a gap), and

* Non-NaN values in other data types (with NaN acting as a gap).

__See__

[get_ranges_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/records/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.get_ranges_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.get_ranges_nb")

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Input array to analyze.

**```gap_value```** :&ensp;`Optional[Scalar]`
:   Value indicating a gap in the data.

**```attach_as_close```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to attach the input array as the `close` field.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```wrapper_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for configuring the wrapper.

    See [ArrayWrapper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges").

__Returns__

[Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges")
:   New instance constructed from the array.

### Ranges.from_delta | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L302-L389)

```python
Ranges.from_delta(
    records_or_mapped,
    delta,
    shift=None,
    idx_field_or_arr=None,
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Build [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges") from a record or mapped array with an applied time delta on its index.

This method applies a time delta to the index field of the input records. When `delta`
is an integer, it represents a number of rows; otherwise, it is converted to a timedelta,
requiring the index to be datetime-like or have a defined frequency. Conversion is performed
using [to_timedelta64](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.to_timedelta64 "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.to_timedelta64").

__See__

[get_ranges_from_delta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/records/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.get_ranges_from_delta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.get_ranges_from_delta_nb")

__Args__

**```records_or_mapped```** :&ensp;`Union[Records, MappedArray]`
:   Record or mapped array to convert into ranges.

**```delta```** :&ensp;`Union[str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Time difference to apply, as a row count or timedelta.

**```shift```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Number of rows to shift the delta application.

**```idx_field_or_arr```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, Array1d]`
:   Field name or array for extracting index values.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges").

__Returns__

[Ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges")
:   New instance constructed based on the applied delta.

```python
    wrap_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Return the maximum duration among ranges as a timedelta.

The duration is computed as the maximum of either the real or effective range durations.

__Args__

**```real```** :&ensp;`bool`

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

### Ranges.get_projections | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L798-L958)

```python
Ranges.get_projections(
    close=None,
    proj_start=None,
    proj_period=None,
    incl_end_idx=True,
    extend=False,
    rebase=True,
    start_value=1.0,
    ffill=False,
    remove_empty=True,
    return_raw=False,
    start_index=None,
    id_level=None,
    jitted=None,
    wrap_kwargs=None,
    clean_index_kwargs=None
)
```

Generate projections for each range record.

This method generates projections based on range records and provided close price data.

!!! note
    As opposed to the Numba-compiled function, the returned DataFrame has projections
    stacked along columns rather than rows. Set `return_raw` to True to obtain the original format.

__See__

[map_ranges_to_projections_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/records/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.map_ranges_to_projections_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.records.map_ranges_to_projections_nb")

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Array of close price values.

    If None, uses [Ranges.close](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/price_records/#vectorbtpro.generic.price_records.PriceRecords.close "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.close").

**```proj_start```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Defines when to start the projection.

    Use an integer for a specified number of rows after the start row or a timedelta-like value.
    The second option requires the index to be datetime-like, or at least the frequency to be set.
    The conversion uses [to_timedelta64](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.to_timedelta64 "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.to_timedelta64").

**```proj_period```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Defines the projection length.

    Use an integer for row count or a timedelta-like value.

**```incl_end_idx```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether the end index of a range is inclusive.

**```extend```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to extend the projection to a fixed length (beyond the end).

    The extension period is taken from the longest range duration if `proj_period`
    is None, and from the longest `proj_period` if not None.

**```rebase```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Rebase projection values so that each projection starts with `start_value`.

    If False, the projection retains the original close values.

**```start_value```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Initial value for rebasing.

    Can be a scalar or an array per column. If set to -1, uses the latest close value.

**```ffill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Forward fill NaN values in the projection, even if they are NaN in `close`.

**```remove_empty```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Remove projections that are NaN or contain only a single element.

**```return_raw```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Return the raw output (range indices and projections)
    instead of a wrapped DataFrame.

**```start_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Timestamp]`
:   Starting timestamp to define
    the DataFrame index of the projection.

**```id_level```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, IndexLike]`
:   Identifier or key for naming range IDs.

    If a string, it may refer to a field mapping.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```wrap_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for wrapping the result.

    See [ArrayWrapper.wrap](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.wrap").

**```clean_index_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for cleaning MultiIndex levels.

    See [clean_index](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/indexes/#vectorbtpro.base.indexes.clean_index "vectorbtpro.base.indexes.clean_index").

__Returns__

`Union[Tuple[Array1d, Array2d], Frame]`
:   If `return_raw` is True, returns a tuple with
    a 1D array of record indices and a 2D array of projections, with each row corresponding
    to a range; otherwise, returns a DataFrame with projections.

Plot range data including OHLC, close prices, start/end markers,
and shaded zones for open and closed ranges.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, Series]`

    Use 'OHLC', 'Candlestick', or a Plotly trace type. Pass None to use the default.

Plot projections.

Generate and plot projection lines and bands based on filtered range records.
This method filters range records by duration constraints and selection criteria,
computes projections using [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections"), and visualizes the results with
[GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections").
It also overlays OHLC or close price data if available.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```min_duration```** :&ensp;`Union[str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Filter range records by minimum duration.

**```max_duration```** :&ensp;`Union[str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Filter range records by maximum duration.

**```last_n```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Number of most recent range records to select.

**```top_n```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Display only the top N records sorted by maximum duration.

**```random_n```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Number of range records to select randomly.

**```seed```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Random seed for deterministic output.

**```proj_start```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Defines when to start the projection.

    See [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections").

    Allows an option "current_or_{value}", which sets `proj_start` to the duration
    of the current open range or to the specified value if no open range exists.

**```proj_period```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Defines the projection length.

    See [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections").

    Allows options such as "current_or_{option}", "mean", "min", "max", "median",
    or a percentage like "50%" representing a quantile derived from closed ranges.

**```incl_end_idx```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether the end index of a range is inclusive.

    See [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections").

**```extend```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to extend the projection to a fixed length (beyond the end).

    See [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections").

**```ffill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Forward fill NaN values in the projection, even if they are NaN in `close`.

    See [Ranges.get_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/ranges/#vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.ranges.Ranges.get_projections").

**```plot_past_period```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, int, FrequencyLike]`
:   Past period for plotting.

    Accepts the same options as `proj_period` plus "proj_period" and "current_or_proj_period".

**```plot_ohlc```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, DataFrame]`
:   Flag or data specifying whether to plot OHLC.

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, Series]`
:   Flag or data specifying whether to plot close prices.

**```plot_projections```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot each projection as a semi-transparent line if True.

    See [GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections")

**```plot_bands```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot computed bands if True.

    See [GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections").

**```plot_lower```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`
:   Specification for the lower band.

    See [GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor.plot_projections")

**```plot_middle```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str, Callable]`

**```ohlc_type```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, BaseTraceType]`
:   Specifies the OHLC plot type.

    Use 'OHLC', 'Candlestick', or a Plotly trace type. Pass None to use the default.

:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the upper band.

:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the auxiliary middle band.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Figure object containing the plotted projections and price data.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> price = pd.Series(
...     [11, 12, 13, 14, 11, 12, 13, 12, 11, 12],
...     index=pd.date_range("2020", periods=10),
... )
>>> vbt.Ranges.from_array(
...     price >= 12,
...     attach_as_close=False,
...     close=price,
... ).plot_projections(
...     proj_start=0,
...     proj_period=4,
...     extend=True,
...     plot_past_period=None
... ).show()
```

### Ranges.plot_shapes | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/ranges.py#L1380-L1562)

Plot range shapes on a figure.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```plot_ohlc```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, DataFrame]`
:   Flag or data specifying whether to plot OHLC.

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, Series]`
:   Flag or data specifying whether to plot close prices.

**```ohlc_type```** :&ensp;`Union[None, str, BaseTraceType]`
:   Specifies the OHLC plot type.

    Use 'OHLC', 'Candlestick', or a Plotly trace type. Pass None to use the default.

**```ohlc_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `ohlc_type` for the OHLC data.

**```close_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the close price.

**```add_shape_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_shape` for each shape.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```xref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the x-axis (e.g., "x", "x2").

**```yref```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Reference for the y-axis (e.g., "y", "y2").

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```make_figure_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for making the figure.

    See [make_figure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/figure/#vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure "vectorbtpro.utils.figure.make_figure").

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Figure object containing the plotted shapes.

__Examples__

Plot zones colored by duration:

```pycon
>>> price = pd.Series(
...     [1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3],
...     index=pd.date_range("2020", periods=9),
... )

>>> def get_opacity(self_col, i):
...     real_duration = self_col.get_real_duration().values
...     return real_duration[i] / real_duration.max() * 0.5

>>> vbt.Ranges.from_array(price >= 2).plot_shapes(
...     add_shape_kwargs=dict(fillcolor="teal", opacity=vbt.RepFunc(get_opacity))
... ).show()
```

:   Indicates whether to merge the provided value with defaults.

__Returns__

`Any`
:   Resolved configuration setting.

### StatsBuilderMixin.stats | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/stats_builder.py#L148-L773)

```python
StatsBuilderMixin.stats(
    metrics=None,
    tags=None,
    column=None,
    group_by=None,
    per_column=None,
    split_columns=None,
    agg_func=<function mean>,
    dropna=None,
    silence_warnings=None,
    template_context=None,
    settings=None,
    filters=None,
    metric_settings=None
)
```

Compute various metrics on this object.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [stats_builder](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder "vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder") and [StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults").

    See [vectorbtpro.utils.template](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/ "vectorbtpro.utils.template") for template logic.

!!! tip
    Optional (resolution) arguments are passed only if they appear in the function's signature,
    while mandatory arguments are always passed. Optional arguments are defined via `settings`
    (globally), whereas mandatory arguments can be set using default metric settings or
    `{metric_name}_kwargs`. Overriding optional arguments does not make them mandatory;
    use `pass_{arg}=True` to enforce passing.

!!! tip
    Resolve and reuse object attributes wherever possible to leverage built-in caching,
    even if global caching is disabled.

__Args__

**```metrics```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeIterable[Union[str, Tuple[str, Kwargs]]]]`
:   Metric or metrics to calculate.

    Each element can be one of the following:

    * Metric name (see keys in [StatsBuilderMixin.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.metrics "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.metrics")).

    * Tuple with a metric name and a settings dictionary as defined in [StatsBuilderMixin.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.metrics "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.metrics").

    * Tuple with a metric name and a [CustomTemplate](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.CustomTemplate "vectorbtpro.utils.template.CustomTemplate") instance.

    * Tuple with a metric name and a list of settings dictionaries to be expanded into multiple metrics.

    The settings dictionary can include:

    * `title`: Metric title. Defaults to the metric name.

    * `tags`: Single tag or multiple tags to associate with the metric.
        The metric is retained if any tag matches those in `tags`.

    * `check_{filter}` and `inv_check_{filter}`: Flags to evaluate the metric against
        a filter defined in `filters`. True indicates inclusion.

    * `calc_func` (required): Function to compute custom metrics.
        It should return a scalar for a single column/group, a pandas.Series
        for multiple columns/groups, or a dictionary of such values for sub-metrics.

    * `resolve_calc_func`: If True, resolve `calc_func` as an attribute of the object
        if not callable. You can specify the path to this function as a string
        (see [deep_getattr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.deep_getattr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.deep_getattr") for the path format).
        If `calc_func` is a function, arguments from merged metric settings are matched with
        arguments in the signature (see below). If False, `calc_func` must accept the resolved
        object and a dictionary of merged metric settings. Defaults to True.

    * `use_shortcuts`: If True, employ shortcut properties when resolving `calc_func`.
        Defaults to True.

    * `post_calc_func`: Function to post-process the output of `calc_func`.
        It must accept the resolved object, the output from `calc_func`, and
        merged metric settings, and return a valid metric result. Defaults to None.

    * `fill_wrap_kwargs`: If True, populate `wrap_kwargs` with `to_timedelta` and
        `silence_warnings`. Defaults to False.

    * `apply_to_timedelta`: If True, apply [ArrayWrapper.arr_to_timedelta](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.arr_to_timedelta "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.arr_to_timedelta")
        on the result. To disable globally, set `to_timedelta` to False in `settings`.
        Defaults to False.

    * `pass_{arg}`: If True, pass the corresponding argument from settings when found
        in the function's signature (see below). If False, the argument is not passed.
        This key is removed if the argument does not exist.

    * `resolve_path_{arg}`: If True, resolve an argument intended as an attribute of the object
        and used as the first part of `calc_func`'s attribute path. Applies only to
        optional arguments. Defaults to True.
        See [AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr").

    * `resolve_{arg}`: If True, resolve an argument found in the function's signature
        as an attribute of the object. Defaults to False.
        See [AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr").

    * `use_shortcuts_{arg}`: If True, use shortcut properties when resolving the argument.
        Defaults to True.

    * `select_col_{arg}`: If True, select a specific column from an argument that represents
        an attribute of the object. Defaults to False.

    * `template_context`: Mapping for template substitution in metric settings.

    * Any other keyword argument overrides settings or is passed directly to `calc_func`.

    If `resolve_calc_func` is True, `calc_func` may accept additional arguments, including:

    * Each alias in [AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.self_aliases")
        representing the original object (ungrouped, with no column selected).

    * group_by: Not passed if used in resolving the first attribute of `calc_func`'s path,
        unless `pass_group_by=True` is specified.

    * `column`

    * `metric_name`

    * `agg_func`

    * `silence_warnings`

    * `to_timedelta`: Replaced with True if set to None and a frequency is available.

    * Any argument from `settings`

    * Any attribute of the object intended for resolution
        (see [AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.AttrResolverMixin.resolve_attr")).

    Pass `metrics='all'` to calculate all supported metrics.

**```tags```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeIterable[str]]`
:   Tag or tags to filter metrics.

    See [match_tags](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/tagging/#vectorbtpro.utils.tagging.match_tags "vectorbtpro.utils.tagging.match_tags").

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to select.

    !!! tip
        There are two methods to select a column:

        * `obj['a'].stats()` computes statistics for column 'a' only.

        * `obj.stats(column='a')` computes statistics for all columns and then selects column 'a'.

        Use the first method for large datasets or when caching is disabled,
        and the second when most attributes are cached.

**```group_by```** :&ensp;`GroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification.

    See [Grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/grouping/base/#vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper "vectorbtpro.base.grouping.base.Grouper").

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, compute metrics for each column and stack the results.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True and `per_column` is True, split the instance
    into multiple columns; otherwise, iterate over columns and apply `column` to the entire instance.

**```agg_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function to aggregate computed statistics across columns.

    By default, calculates the mean across columns. If None, returns all columns as a DataFrame.
    The function should accept a pandas.Series and return a scalar. Aggregation is applied
    if `column` is specified or if the object has only one column.

    If overridden by a metric:

    * It takes effect only if the global `agg_func` is not None.

    * Warning is raised if it is None but the calculation returns multiple values.

**```dropna```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, omit metrics that are entirely NaN.

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

    Merged with `template_context` from [stats_builder](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder "vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder") and
    [StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults"). Applied first to `settings` and then to
    individual metric settings.

**```filters```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Filters to apply to metrics.

    Each key is a filter name with its corresponding settings dictionary, which can include:

    * filter_func: Function that takes the resolved object and merged metric settings,
        returning True or False.

    * warning_message: Warning to display when skipping a metric
        (supports template substitution).

    * inv_warning_message: Warning for inverse checks.

    These filters are merged with those from [stats_builder](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder "vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder")
    and [StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults").

**```settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Global settings and resolution arguments.

    These override values from [stats_builder](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder "vectorbtpro._settings.stats_builder") and
    [StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats_defaults") and can be extended or overridden
    by metric-specific settings.

**```metric_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Overrides for individual metrics.

    Extend or override all global and metric settings on a per-metric basis.

__Returns__

`Optional[SeriesFrame]`
:   Computed metrics as a Pandas Series
    (for single-dimensional output) or DataFrame (for multi-dimensional output).

Default configuration for [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats").

# vectorbtpro.generic.nb | package | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/__init__.py)

Package providing Numba-compiled functions for generic data.

This package offers a collection of functions compiled with Numba that are used by accessors
and various parts of a backtesting pipeline, including technical indicators. All functions
accept only NumPy arrays and other Numba-compatible types.

!!! note
    Vectorbtpro treats matrices as first-class citizens and expects input arrays to be 2-dim,
    unless a function has the `_1d` suffix or is intended for use as input to another function.
    Data is processed along the index (axis 0).

    Rolling functions with `minp=None` set `min_periods` to the window size.

    All functions passed as arguments must be Numba-compiled.

    Records retain the order in which they are created.

!!! warning
    Use `parallel=True` only if your columns are independent.

## Sub-modules

* [vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/ "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce")

:   Delta degrees of freedom.

__Returns__

:   Covariance of the selected group elements.

## describe_reduce_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/apply_reduce.py#L2182-L2211)

```python
describe_reduce_nb(
    arr,
    perc,
    ddof
)
```

Return descriptive statistics for a 1D array while ignoring NaN values.

The returned array contains the statistics in the following order:
count, mean, standard deviation, minimum, the specified percentiles, and maximum.

!!! note
    This function is a Numba equivalent to `pd.Series(arr).describe(perc)`.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input array.

**```perc```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of percentiles as fractions (e.g., 0.25, 0.5, 0.75).

**```ddof```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Delta degrees of freedom.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array of descriptive statistics.

:   Positional arguments for `reduce_func_nb`.

`Array2d`
:   2D array where each column is the reduction result of a flattened group.

This function is similar to [reduce_grouped_meta_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_meta_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.reduce_grouped_meta_nb") but requires that `reduce_func_nb`

:   Positional arguments for `apply_func_nb`.

`Array2d`

## squeeze_grouped_meta_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/apply_reduce.py#L1694-L1745)

```python
squeeze_grouped_meta_nb(
    n_rows,
    group_map,
    squeeze_func_nb,
    *args
)
```

Return a meta squeezed array by applying a meta squeeze function to grouped indices.

This meta function operates similarly to [squeeze_grouped_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/apply_reduce/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.apply_reduce.squeeze_grouped_nb") but works with index information.
It applies `squeeze_func_nb` using the row index, group column indices, and group index to
produce a single value for each element.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```n_rows```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of rows in the output array.

**```group_map```** :&ensp;`GroupMap`
:   Tuple of indices and lengths for each group.

**```squeeze_func_nb```** :&ensp;`GroupSqueezeMetaFunc`
:   Callback function that accepts a row index,
    group column indices, group index, and additional arguments, and returns a single value.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `squeeze_func_nb`.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2D array with the meta squeezed values for each row and group.

## squeeze_grouped_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/apply_reduce.py#L1645-L1691)

```python
squeeze_grouped_nb(
    arr,
    group_map,
    squeeze_func_nb,
    *args
)
```

Return a squeezed array by applying a squeeze function to each grouped segment.

This function reduces each group of columns in the input array into a single column
by applying `squeeze_func_nb`. It processes each row independently, applying the squeeze
function to the corresponding group slice.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D input array.

**```group_map```** :&ensp;`GroupMap`
:   Tuple of indices and lengths for each group.

**```squeeze_func_nb```** :&ensp;`ReduceFunc`
:   Callback function that accepts a group within a row as a 1D array
    and additional arguments, and returns a single value.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for `squeeze_func_nb`.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2D array in which each column is the squeezed result of the corresponding group.

## crossed_above_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/base.py#L1776-L1817)

```python
    arr1,

    dropna=False
)
```

Return a boolean mask indicating where the first array crosses above the second array.

__Args__

**```arr1```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   One-dimensional array of values.

**```arr2```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   One-dimensional array or scalar for comparison.

**```wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of consecutive data points required above the threshold to confirm a crossover.

**```dropna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, treat indices with NaN values as missing, mimicking the removal of rows with NaN.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Boolean array with True at positions where a crossover from below to above occurs.

## nanpartition_mean_noarr_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/base.py#L1265-L1317)

```python
nanpartition_mean_noarr_1d_nb(
    arr,
    q
)
```

Compute the average value using a partitioning algorithm while ignoring NaN values
without additional allocations.

!!! note
    Has worst case time complexity of O(N^2), which makes it much slower than `np.partition`,
    but still faster if used in rolling calculations, especially for `q` near 0.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   One-dimensional array containing numerical values that may include NaNs.

**```q```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Percentile threshold guiding the partitioning,
    where 0 represents the minimum and 100 represents the maximum.

__Returns__

`float`
:   Computed average of the partitioned elements.

## realign_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/base.py#L2306-L2354)

```python
realign_1d_nb(
    arr,
    source_index,
    target_index,
    source_freq=None,
    target_freq=None,
    source_rbound=False,
    target_rbound=False,
    nan_value=nan,
    ffill=True
)
```

Return the latest available value in `arr` for each index in `target_index` based on `source_index`.

This function identifies, for each target index, the most recent corresponding value from `arr`.
If `source_rbound` is True, each element in `source_index` is treated as a right-bound value,
determined using the specified `source_freq` or the next index when `source_freq` is None.
The same approach applies to `target_rbound` and `target_index`.

!!! note
    Both index arrays must be increasing. Repeating values are allowed.

    If `arr` contains bar data, both index arrays must represent the opening time.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   One-dimensional array of values.

**```source_index```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Indices corresponding to the values in `arr`.

**```target_index```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of target indices, which must be strictly increasing.

**```source_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[Scalar]`
:   Frequency applied to `source_index`.

**```target_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[Scalar]`
:   Frequency applied to `target_index`.

**```source_rbound```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if `source_index` values represent right bounds.

**```target_rbound```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if `target_index` values represent right bounds.

**```nan_value```** :&ensp;`Scalar`
:   Value representing missing data.

**```ffill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, forward fill missing values.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Realigned 1-dimensional array.

## realign_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/base.py#L2422-L2481)

```python
realign_nb(
    arr,
    source_index,
    target_index,
    source_freq=None,
    target_freq=None,
    source_rbound=False,
    target_rbound=False,
    nan_value=nan,
    ffill=True
)
```

Return a two-dimensional array with values realigned for each column based on `target_index`.

This function applies [realign_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.realign_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.base.realign_1d_nb") to each column of the input array, aligning values
according to corresponding source and target indices.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of values.

**```source_index```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Indices corresponding to the rows of `arr`.

**```target_index```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of target indices, which must be strictly increasing.

**```source_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[Scalar]`
:   Frequency applied to `source_index`.

**```target_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[Scalar]`
:   Frequency applied to `target_index`.

**```source_rbound```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if `source_index` values represent right bounds.

**```target_rbound```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if `target_index` values represent right bounds.

**```nan_value```** :&ensp;`Scalar`
:   Value representing missing data.

**```ffill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, forward fill missing values.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   Realigned 2-dimensional array.

## fit_pattern_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/patterns.py#L187-L301)

```python
fit_pattern_nb(
    arr,
    pattern,
    interp_mode=3,
    rescale_mode=0,
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type=0,
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None
)
```

Fit pattern.

Resize and rescale the specified `pattern` to match the length and scale of the input array `arr`.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input array determining the target length and rescaling range.

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Pattern array to be resized and rescaled.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Interpolation mode.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Rescaling mode for adjusting the ranges of `arr` and `pattern`.

    See [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode").

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum threshold for clipping the input array.

    If NaN, the minimum of `arr` is used.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum threshold for clipping the input array.

    If NaN, the maximum of `arr` is used.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum threshold for clipping the resized pattern.

    If NaN, the minimum of the resized pattern is used.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum threshold for clipping the resized pattern.

    If NaN, the maximum of the resized pattern is used.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Error computation mode.

    See [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType").

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Maximum error threshold for normalization.

    Provided as a scalar or per element in the pattern.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple containing the resized and rescaled pattern and
    the corresponding maximum error.

## pattern_similarity_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/patterns.py#L304-L629)

```python
pattern_similarity_nb(
    arr,
    pattern,
    interp_mode=3,
    rescale_mode=0,
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type=0,
    distance_measure=0,
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None,
    max_error_as_maxdist=False,
    max_error_strict=False,
    min_pct_change=nan,
    max_pct_change=nan,
    min_similarity=nan,
    minp=None
)
```

Return the similarity between an input array and a pattern array.

This function maps each element of `arr` into the range of `pattern` and computes
the absolute difference (error) between the actual and mapped values. It then normalizes
the error by the corresponding maximum error at that position to obtain a relative error
between 0 and 1, and aggregates these normalized errors to derive the overall similarity measure.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1-dimensional array to compare with the pattern.

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1-dimensional array representing the reference pattern.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Interpolation mode.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Rescaling mode for adjusting the ranges of `arr` and `pattern`.

    See [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode").

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `arr`.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Error computation mode.

    See [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType").

**```distance_measure```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Method for measuring distance (e.g., MAE, MSE, RMSE).

    See [DistanceMeasure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure").

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Maximum error threshold for normalization.

    Provided as a scalar or per element in the pattern.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```max_error_as_maxdist```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether `max_error` represents the maximum distance at each point.

**```max_error_strict```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, any instance of exceeding `max_error` results in a similarity of NaN.

**```min_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum percent change applied during rescaling.

**```max_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum percentage change allowed for a window to remain a search candidate.

**```min_similarity```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum similarity threshold.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

__Returns__

`float`
:   Similarity measure between `arr` and `pattern`,
    or NaN if the computation conditions are not met.

## bar_price_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L1479-L1502)

```python
bar_price_nb(
    records,
    price
)
```

Return the bar prices corresponding to each record.

This function retrieves the bar price for each record using a flex selection from the price array.
If the price array is not provided, NaN is returned for the corresponding record.

__Args__

**```records```** :&ensp;`RecordArray`
:   Array of records.

**```price```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray2d]`
:   Two-dimensional array of bar prices to select
    from using record indices and columns.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array of bar prices for each record, with NaN for records
    when the price array is None.

## dd_recovery_return_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L1447-L1476)

This function calculates the recovery return as the relative change from
