## find_pattern_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L558-L827)

```python
find_pattern_1d_nb(
    arr,
    pattern,
    window=None,
    max_window=None,
    row_select_prob=1.0,
    window_select_prob=1.0,
    roll_forward=False,
    interp_mode=3,
    rescale_mode=0,
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type=0,
    distance_measure=0,
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None,
    max_error_as_maxdist=False,
    max_error_strict=False,
    min_pct_change=nan,
    max_pct_change=nan,
    min_similarity=0.85,
    minp=None,
    overlap_mode=0,
    max_records=None,
    col=0
)
```

Find all occurrences of a pattern in a 1D array.

Iterate through the input array to identify segments that closely match the provided pattern.
For each valid window length between `window` and `max_window`, compute a similarity score
using [pattern_similarity_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/patterns/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.pattern_similarity_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.pattern_similarity_nb"). If the similarity meets the
`min_similarity` threshold, record the segment in a record array.

If `roll_forward` is True, windows are processed forward ensuring sorted `start_idx`;
otherwise, windows are processed backward with sorted `end_idx`. The function selectively
processes rows and windows based on `row_select_prob` and `window_select_prob`.
The length of the output record array is limited by `max_records` when specified.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input one-dimensional array in which to search for the pattern.

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array representing the pattern to locate.

    Can be smaller or larger than the source array. In such cases,
    the smaller array is stretched using the interpolation mode specified by `interp_mode`.

**```window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Window size.

    If None, defaults to the length of `pattern`.

**```max_window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Maximum length of the rolling window for matching.

    If None, defaults to `window`.

**```row_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a row.

**```window_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a window size.

**```roll_forward```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Process windows in forward direction if True; otherwise, in backward direction.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Interpolation mode.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Rescaling mode for adjusting the ranges of `arr` and `pattern`.

    See [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode").

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `arr`.

    Use only when the array has fixed bounds. Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax`
    and for verifying `min_pct_change` and `max_pct_change`.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `arr`.

    Use only when the array has fixed bounds. Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax`
    and for verifying `min_pct_change` and `max_pct_change`.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

    Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax` and for computing the maximum distance
    at each point when `max_error_as_maxdist` is disabled.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

    Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax` and for computing the maximum distance
    at each point when `max_error_as_maxdist` is disabled.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Error computation mode.

    See [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType").

**```distance_measure```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Method for measuring distance (e.g., MAE, MSE, RMSE).

    See [DistanceMeasure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure").

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Maximum error threshold for normalization.

    Provided as a scalar or per element in the pattern.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    If None, defaults to `interp_mode`.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```max_error_as_maxdist```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether `max_error` represents the maximum distance at each point.

    If False, exceeding `max_error` sets the distance to the maximum derived from
    `pmin`, `pmax`, and the pattern value at that point. If True and any point
    in a window is NaN, that point is skipped.

**```max_error_strict```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, any instance of exceeding `max_error` results in a similarity of NaN.

**```min_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum percentage change required for a window to remain a search candidate.

    Window similarity is set to NaN if this threshold is not met.

**```max_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum percentage change allowed for a window to remain a search candidate.

    Window similarity is set to NaN if this threshold is exceeded.

**```min_similarity```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum similarity threshold.

    If the computed similarity falls below this, returns NaN.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```overlap_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Mode for handling overlapping matches.

    See [OverlapMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.OverlapMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.OverlapMode").

**```max_records```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Maximum number of records to be filled.

    If None, defaults to the number of rows in `arr`.

**```col```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Column index assigned to the result records.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Array of matching segment records with fields such as
    `id`, `col`, `start_idx`, `end_idx`, `status`, and `similarity`.

    Has the [pattern_range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.pattern_range_dt") dtype.

## get_drawdowns_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L1127-L1324)

```python
get_drawdowns_nb(
    open,
    high,
    low,
    close,
    sim_start=None,
    sim_end=None
)
```

Fill drawdown records by analyzing a time series.

This function computes drawdown records using the provided price series arrays.
Only `close` is mandatory; other arrays supply supplementary price information.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```open```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   Open price time series for each asset column.

**```high```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   High price time series for each asset column.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   Low price time series for each asset column.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Close price time series for each asset column.

**```sim_start```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Start position of the simulation range (inclusive).

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```sim_end```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   End position of the simulation range (exclusive).

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Array of computed drawdown records.

    Has the [drawdown_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.drawdown_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.drawdown_dt") dtype.
__Examples__

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> close = np.array([
...     [1, 5, 1, 3],
...     [2, 4, 2, 2],
...     [3, 3, 3, 1],
...     [4, 2, 2, 2],
...     [5, 1, 1, 3]
... ])
>>> records = vbt.nb.get_drawdowns_nb(None, None, None, close)

>>> pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)
    id  col  start_idx  valley_idx  end_idx  start_val  valley_val  end_val  \
0   0    1          0           4        4        5.0         1.0      1.0
1   0    2          2           4        4        3.0         1.0      1.0
2   0    3          0           2        4        3.0         1.0      3.0

    status
0       0
1       0
2       1
```

## get_ranges_from_delta_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L128-L233)

```python
get_ranges_from_delta_nb(
```

Build delta-based ranges for record indices.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```n_rows```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Total number of rows in the dataset.

**```idx_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of row indices.

**```id_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of IDs.

**```col_map```** :&ensp;`GroupMap`
:   Tuple of indices and lengths for each column.

:   Index array in nanosecond format.

:   Delta offset to compute range boundaries.

:   Flag indicating whether to use the index values for delta calculation.

**```shift```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Shift applied to the starting index.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Record array with fields `id`, `col`, `start_idx`, `end_idx`,
    and `status` indicating the computed ranges.

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.

## get_ranges_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L35-L125)

```python
get_ranges_nb(
    arr,
    gap_value
)
```

Fill range records in a 2D array by detecting gaps.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D NumPy array where each column represents a time series.

**```gap_value```** :&ensp;`Scalar`
:   Value that signifies a gap in the data.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Record array containing range details with fields
    `id`, `col`, `start_idx`, `end_idx`, and `status`.

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.
__Examples__

Find ranges in time series:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> a = np.array([
...     [np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, np.nan],
...     [     2, np.nan, np.nan, np.nan],
...     [     3,      3, np.nan, np.nan],
...     [np.nan,      4,      4, np.nan],
...     [     5, np.nan,      5,      5],
...     [     6,      6, np.nan,      6]
... ])
>>> records = vbt.nb.get_ranges_nb(a, np.nan)

>>> pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)
    id  col  start_idx  end_idx  status
0   0    0          1        3       1
1   1    0          4        5       0
2   0    1          2        4       1
3   1    1          5        5       0
4   0    2          3        5       1
5   0    3          4        5       0
```

## map_ranges_to_projections_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L409-L555)

```python
map_ranges_to_projections_nb(
    close,
    col_arr,
    start_idx_arr,
    end_idx_arr,
    status_arr,
    index=None,
    proj_start=0,
    proj_start_use_index=False,
    proj_period=None,
    proj_period_use_index=False,
    incl_end_idx=True,
    extend=False,
    rebase=True,
    start_value=1.0,
    ffill=False,
    remove_empty=False
)
```

Map each specified range to a projection.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D array of close prices.

**```col_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array of column indices for selecting data from `close`.

**```start_idx_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array of starting row indices for each range.

**```end_idx_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array of ending row indices for each range.

**```status_arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array indicating the status of each range.

**```index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array1d]`
:   Index array in nanosecond format.

**```proj_start```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Offset from the start index to begin the projection.

**```proj_start_use_index```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to compute the projection start using the `index` array.

**```proj_period```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Period or duration for the projection.

**```proj_period_use_index```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to determine the projection period based on the `index` array.

**```incl_end_idx```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether the end index of a range is inclusive.

**```extend```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to extend the projection to a fixed length (beyond the end).

    The extension period is taken from the longest range duration if `proj_period`
    is None, and from the longest `proj_period` if not None.

**```rebase```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Rebase projection values so that each projection starts with `start_value`.

    If False, the projection retains the original close values.

**```start_value```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Initial value for rebasing.

    Can be a scalar or an array per column. If set to -1, uses the latest close value.

**```ffill```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Forward fill NaN values in the projection, even if they are NaN in `close`.

**```remove_empty```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Remove projections that are NaN or contain only a single element.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple where the first element is a 1D array of
    record indices and the second element is a 2D array of projections,
    with each row corresponding to a range.

## range_coverage_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/records.py#L278-L353)

## ewm_mean_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/rolling.py#L816-L870)

```python
ewm_mean_1d_nb(
    arr,
    span,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

Compute the exponential weighted moving average for a 1D array using [ewm_mean_acc_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/rolling/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_mean_acc_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_mean_acc_nb").

This function serves as a Numba equivalent to:
`pd.Series(arr).ewm(span=span, min_periods=minp, adjust=adjust).mean()`, and is adapted from
`pd._libs.window.aggregations.window_aggregations.ewma` with default arguments.

!!! note
    In contrast to the Pandas implementation, `minp` is applied within `span`.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input 1D array.

**```span```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window span for the exponential weighting.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array of computed exponential weighted moving averages.

## ewm_std_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/rolling.py#L989-L1056)

```python
ewm_std_1d_nb(
    arr,
    span,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

Compute the exponential weighted moving standard deviation for a 1-dimensional array.

Updates the accumulator state with [ewm_std_acc_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/rolling/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_std_acc_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_std_acc_nb") at each iteration.

Numba equivalent to `pd.Series(arr).ewm(span=span, min_periods=minp).std()`
and adapted from `pd._libs.window.aggregations.window_aggregations.ewmcov`.

!!! note
    In contrast to Pandas, the parameter `minp` is applied within the span.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input data array.

**```span```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window span for the exponential weighting.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Computed exponential weighted moving standard deviation.

## rolling_pattern_similarity_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/rolling.py#L2405-L2595)

```python
rolling_pattern_similarity_1d_nb(
    arr,
    pattern,
    window=None,
    max_window=None,
    row_select_prob=1.0,
    window_select_prob=1.0,
    interp_mode=3,
    rescale_mode=0,
    vmin=nan,
    vmax=nan,
    pmin=nan,
    pmax=nan,
    invert=False,
    error_type=0,
    distance_measure=0,
    max_error=nan,
    max_error_interp_mode=None,
    max_error_as_maxdist=False,
    max_error_strict=False,
    min_pct_change=nan,
    max_pct_change=nan,
    min_similarity=0.85,
    minp=None
)
```

Compute rolling pattern similarity on a 1D array.

Uses [pattern_similarity_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/patterns/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.pattern_similarity_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.patterns.pattern_similarity_nb").

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1-dimensional array to compare with the pattern.

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D array representing the pattern to locate.

    Can be smaller or larger than the source array. In such cases,
    the smaller array is stretched using the interpolation mode specified by `interp_mode`.

**```window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Window size.

    If None, defaults to the length of `pattern`.

**```max_window```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Maximum length of the rolling window for matching.

    If None, defaults to `window`.

**```row_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a row.

**```window_select_prob```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Probability of selecting a window size.

**```interp_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Interpolation mode.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```rescale_mode```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Rescaling mode for adjusting the ranges of `arr` and `pattern`.

    See [RescaleMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.RescaleMode").

**```vmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `arr`.

    Use only when the array has fixed bounds. Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax`
    and for verifying `min_pct_change` and `max_pct_change`.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```vmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `arr`.

    Use only when the array has fixed bounds. Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax`
    and for verifying `min_pct_change` and `max_pct_change`.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```pmin```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

    Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax` and for computing the maximum distance
    at each point when `max_error_as_maxdist` is disabled.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```pmax```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum value used for rescaling `pattern`.

    Used in rescaling with `RescaleMode.MinMax` and for computing the maximum distance
    at each point when `max_error_as_maxdist` is disabled.

    If set to NaN, it is calculated dynamically.

**```invert```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Invert the pattern by reflecting its values.

**```error_type```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Error computation mode.

    See [ErrorType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.ErrorType").

**```distance_measure```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Method for measuring distance (e.g., MAE, MSE, RMSE).

    See [DistanceMeasure](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.DistanceMeasure").

**```max_error```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Maximum error threshold for normalization.

    Provided as a scalar or per element in the pattern.

**```max_error_interp_mode```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Interpolation mode for `max_error`.

    If None, defaults to `interp_mode`.

    See [InterpMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.InterpMode").

**```max_error_as_maxdist```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether `max_error` represents the maximum distance at each point.

    If False, exceeding `max_error` sets the distance to the maximum derived from
    `pmin`, `pmax`, and the pattern value at that point. If True and any point
    in a window is NaN, that point is skipped.

**```max_error_strict```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, any instance of exceeding `max_error` results in a similarity of NaN.

**```min_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum percentage change required for a window to remain a search candidate.

    Window similarity is set to NaN if this threshold is not met.

**```max_pct_change```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Maximum percentage change allowed for a window to remain a search candidate.

    Window similarity is set to NaN if this threshold is exceeded.

**```min_similarity```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Minimum similarity threshold.

    If the computed similarity falls below this, returns NaN.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array containing the computed pattern similarity values.

## wwm_mean_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/rolling.py#L1087-L1104)

```python
wwm_mean_1d_nb(
    arr,
    period,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

Compute Wilder's exponential weighted moving average for a 1-dimensional array.

Applies [ewm_mean_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/nb/rolling/#vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_mean_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.nb.rolling.ewm_mean_1d_nb") internally with a span calculated as `2 * period - 1`.

__Args__

**```arr```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Input data array.

**```period```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Period used for the moving average computation.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Wilder's exponential weighted moving average.

# vectorbtpro.generic.nb.sim_range | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/sim_range.py)

Module providing generic Numba-compiled functions for simulation ranges.

!!! warning
    Resolution is more flexible and may return None while preparation always returns NumPy arrays.
    Thus, use preparation, not resolution, in Numba-parallel workflows.

## prepare_grouped_sim_end_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/nb/sim_range.py#L664-L715)

Prepare grouped simulation end positions for grouped data.

:   Array defining the number of columns in each group.

:   End position of the simulation range (exclusive).

    Provided as a scalar or per column or group.

:   Flag to validate that simulation positions are within bounds.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array containing the prepared simulation end positions for each group.

### RelRange.is_gap | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L148-L149)

### RelRange.length | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L116-L122)

Range length value.

Floating numbers between 0 and 1 are interpreted as relative.

Can be negative.

### RelRange.length_space | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L124-L135)

Space used for applying the relative length.

Supported values:

* 'all': Use the entire available space.

* 'free': Use the remaining space after the offset.

* 'free_or_prev': Use the remaining space after the offset or the size of the previous range, 
    depending on which comes first in the direction of [RelRange.length](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.length "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.length").

Applied only when [RelRange.length](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.length "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.length") is relative.

### RelRange.offset | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L83-L89)

Offset value.

Floating numbers between 0 and 1 are interpreted as relative.

Can be negative.

### RelRange.offset_anchor | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L91-L102)

Anchor used for offset.

Supported values:

* 'start': Start of the range.

* 'end': End of the range.

* 'prev_start': Start of the previous range.

* 'prev_end': End of the previous range.

* 'next_start': Next start.

* 'next_end': Next end.

### RelRange.offset_space | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L104-L114)

Space used for applying the relative offset.

Supported values:

* 'all': Use the entire available space.

* 'free': Use the remaining space after the offset anchor.

* 'prev': Use the length of the previous range.

Applied only when [RelRange.offset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset") is relative.

### RelRange.out_of_bounds | field | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L137-L146)

Strategy for handling indices that are out of bounds.

Supported values:

* 'keep': Retain out-of-bounds values.

* 'ignore': Silently ignore out-of-bound positions.

* 'warn': Emit a warning if values are out of bounds.

* 'raise': Raise an error for out-of-bound values.

### RelRange.to_slice | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L165-L331)

## Splitter | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L369-L6745)

Base class for splitting.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.splitter "vectorbtpro._settings.splitter").

__Args__

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`ArrayWrapper`
:   Array wrapper instance.

    See [ArrayWrapper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper").

:   Index used for splitting.

**```splits_arr```** :&ensp;`SplitsArray`
:   Two-dimensional array representing splits.

    The first axis represents splits and the second axis represents sets.
    Each element is a range defined as a slice, a sequence of indices, a mask,
    or a callable returning such.

### Splitter.apply | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L4224-L5081)

```python
Splitter.apply(
    apply_func,
    *apply_args,
    split=None,
    set_=None,
    split_group_by=None,
    set_group_by=None,
    squeeze_one_split=True,
    squeeze_one_set=True,
    remap_to_obj=True,
    obj_index=None,
    obj_freq=None,
    range_format='slice_or_any',
    point_wise=False,
    attach_bounds=False,
    right_inclusive=False,
    template_context=None,
    silence_warnings=False,
    index_combine_kwargs=None,
    freq=None,
    iteration='split_wise',
    execute_kwargs=None,
    filter_results=True,
    raise_no_results=True,
    merge_func=None,
    merge_kwargs=None,
    merge_all=True,
    wrap_results=True,
    eval_id=None,
    **apply_kwargs
)
```

Apply a function over each data range.

Divides the index into ranges based on selected splits and sets, optionally grouping using
`split_group_by` and `set_group_by`. For each combination of split and set, retrieves
the corresponding range via [Splitter.select_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.select_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.select_range") and [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range").
Positional and keyword arguments that are instances of [Takeable](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Takeable "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Takeable") are sliced based on
these ranges using [Splitter.take_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.take_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.take_range"). Before slicing, the range into each object's index
using [Splitter.get_ready_obj_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_obj_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_obj_range"). The function and its arguments are then
template-substituted and scheduled for execution via [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").
After execution, the results are optionally merged using `merge_func` and wrapped in
a Pandas object if specified.

Template substitution variables include:

* `split/set_group_indices`: Indices for selected row/column groups.

* `split/set_indices`: Indices for selected rows/columns.

* `n_splits/sets`: Number of selected splits/sets.

* `split/set_labels`: Labels for split or set groups.

* `split/set_idx`: Index of the selected split or set.

* `split/set_label`: Label of the selected split or set.

* `range_`: Range used for indexing (see [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range")).

* `range_meta`: Metadata regarding the range.

* `obj_range_meta`: Metadata for the ranges taken from each takeable argument.
    Positional arguments are denoted by position, keyword arguments are denoted by keys.

* `args`: Positional arguments with selected ranges.

* `kwargs`: Keyword arguments with selected ranges.

* `bounds`: Tuple of range boundaries.

* `template_context`: Template context provided for substitutions.

Iteration over ranges is controlled by the `iteration` parameter:

* `split_major`: Iterate over ranges in split-major order.

* `set_major`: Iterate over ranges in set-major order.

* `split_wise`: Process ranges sequentially within each split.

* `set_wise`: Process ranges sequentially within each set.

__Args__

**```apply_func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Function to apply over each range.

**```*apply_args```**
:   Positional arguments for `apply_func`.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[Selection]`
:   Selection criteria for splits.

**```set_```** :&ensp;`Optional[Selection]`
:   Selection criteria for sets.

**```split_group_by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification for defining splits.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```set_group_by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification for defining sets.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```squeeze_one_split```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to squeeze the output if only one split exists.

**```squeeze_one_set```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to squeeze the output if only one set exists.

**```remap_to_obj```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to remap the range to the object's index.

**```obj_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[IndexLike]`
:   Target index for remapping, if available.

**```obj_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the target index
    (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```range_format```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Format of the returned range.

    See [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range").

**```point_wise```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to perform point-wise range extraction.

**```attach_bounds```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str]`
:   Specifies if and how to attach bounds to the result.

    If True or "source", attaches the source bounds; other string options are supported.

**```right_inclusive```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether the right bound is inclusive.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

**```index_combine_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for combining indexes.

    See [combine_indexes](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/indexes/#vectorbtpro.base.indexes.combine_indexes "vectorbtpro.base.indexes.combine_indexes").

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```iteration```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Iteration mode over ranges.

    Options: "split_major", "set_major", "split_wise", "set_wise".

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```filter_results```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to filter out results that are [NoResult](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.NoResult "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.NoResult").

**```raise_no_results```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to raise a
    [NoResultsException](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.NoResultsException "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.NoResultsException") exception if no results remain.

**```merge_func```** :&ensp;`MergeFuncLike`
:   Function to merge the results.

    See [MergeFunc](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/merging/#vectorbtpro.utils.merging.MergeFunc "vectorbtpro.utils.merging.MergeFunc").

**```merge_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `merge_func`.

**```merge_all```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to merge all results across iterations regardless of the iteration mode.

**```wrap_results```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to wrap the final merged result in a Pandas object.

**```eval_id```** :&ensp;`Optional[Hashable]`
:   Evaluation identifier.

**```**apply_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `apply_func`.

__Returns__

`Any`
:   Result of applying `apply_func` over each range, which may be a merged result,
    a Pandas Series, or a tuple of Pandas objects depending on the processing and
    output wrapping options.

__Examples__

Get the return of each data range:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> data = vbt.YFData.pull(
...     "BTC-USD",
...     start="2020-01-01 UTC",
...     end="2021-01-01 UTC"
... )
>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_n_rolling(data.wrapper.index, 5)

>>> def apply_func(data):
...     return data.close.iloc[-1] - data.close.iloc[0]

>>> splitter.apply(apply_func, vbt.Takeable(data))
split
0    -1636.467285
1     3706.568359
2     2944.720703
3     -118.113281
4    17098.916016
dtype: float64
```

The same but by indexing manually:

```pycon
>>> def apply_func(range_, data):
...     data = data.iloc[range_]
...     return data.close.iloc[-1] - data.close.iloc[0]

>>> splitter.apply(apply_func, vbt.Rep("range_"), data)
split
0    -1636.467285
1     3706.568359
2     2944.720703
3     -118.113281
4    17098.916016
dtype: float64
```

Divide into two windows, each consisting of 50% train and 50% test, compute SMA for
each range, and row-stack the outputs of each set upon merging:

```pycon
>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_n_rolling(data.wrapper.index, 2, split=0.5)

>>> def apply_func(data):
...     return data.run("SMA", 10).real

>>> splitter.apply(
...     apply_func,
...     vbt.Takeable(data),
...     merge_func="row_stack"
... ).unstack("set").vbt.drop_levels("split", axis=0).vbt.plot().show()
```

### Splitter.from_expanding | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L988-L1119)

```python
Splitter.from_expanding(
    index,
    min_length,
    offset,
    split=None,
    split_range_kwargs=None,
    range_bounds_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    freq=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance from an expanding range.

Creates an expanding sequence of slices based on the provided index.
The first slice uses a minimum length defined by min_length, and each subsequent
slice begins after an offset from the previous slice's right boundary.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index to split.

**```min_length```** :&ensp;`Union[int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Minimum length for the first expanding range.
    If specified as a float between 0 and 1, it is interpreted relative to the length of the index.

**```offset```** :&ensp;`Union[int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Offset after the previous range's
    right boundary to determine the start of the next range.

    It may also be provided as a float relative to the index length.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```range_bounds_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for getting range bounds.

    See [Splitter.get_range_bounds](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")
:   New [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

__Examples__

Roll an expanding range with a length of 10 and an offset of 10, and split it into 3/4:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> index = pd.date_range("2020", "2021", freq="D")

>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_expanding(
...     index,
...     10,
...     10,
...     split=3/4,
...     set_labels=["train", "test"]
... )
>>> splitter.plot().show()
```

### Splitter.from_grouper | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L1332-L1444)

```python
Splitter.from_grouper(
    index,
    by,
    groupby_kwargs=None,
    grouper_kwargs=None,
    split=None,
    split_range_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    split_labels=None,
    freq=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance from a grouper.

Uses [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper") to group the index and generate splits.
Each group's indices may be adjusted using the provided `split` specification before being passed to
[Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits") to build the instance.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index to be grouped and split.

**```by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouper-like specification.

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance from multiple expanding ranges.

Selects n evenly spaced expanding ranges based on the given index. Each range uses
a minimum length specified by min_length, which is automatically computed if not provided.
An optional split configuration can be applied to transform each range.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index to split.

**```n```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of expanding ranges to select.

**```min_length```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Minimum length for each expanding range.

    If specified as a float between 0 and 1, it is interpreted relative to the length of the index.
    If None, it is determined based on the index length and the specified number of ranges.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")
:   New [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

### Splitter.from_n_random | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L1446-L1698)

```python
Splitter.from_n_random(
    index,
    n,
    min_length,
    max_length=None,
    min_start=None,
    max_end=None,
    length_choice_func=None,
    start_choice_func=None,
    length_p_func=None,
    start_p_func=None,
    seed=None,
    split=None,
    split_range_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    freq=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance with randomly generated ranges.

Generate random ranges by selecting a range length and a start position.
The range length is chosen between `min_length` and `max_length` (inclusive)
using `length_choice_func`, which selects one value from the candidate lengths.
Optionally, `length_p_func` returns probability weights for the length selection.

The start position is selected from positions between `min_start` and `max_end`
(adjusted to accommodate the chosen range length) using `start_choice_func`.
Optionally, `start_p_func` returns probability weights for the start selection.

!!! note
    Both choice functions must accept two arguments: the iteration index and the array of
    possible values.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index from which ranges are generated.

**```n```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of random ranges to generate.

**```min_length```** :&ensp;`Union[int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Minimum length for each range.

**```max_length```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Maximum length for each range.
    If not provided, it defaults to the same value as `min_length`.

**```min_start```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, float, DatetimeLike]`
:   Minimum allowable start position for a range.

**```max_end```** :&ensp;`Union[None, int, float, DatetimeLike]`
:   Maximum allowable end position for a range.

**```length_choice_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function to select a range length
    from candidate values.

    It should accept the iteration index and an array of candidate lengths.

**```start_choice_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function to select a start position
    from candidate values.

    It should accept the iteration index and an array of candidate start positions.

**```length_p_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function that returns probability weights
    for the length selection.

    It should accept the iteration index and candidate lengths.

**```start_p_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function that returns probability weights
    for the start selection.

    It should accept the iteration index and candidate start positions.

**```seed```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Random seed for deterministic output.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")
:   New [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

__Examples__

```pycon

>>> index = pd.date_range("2020", "2021", freq="D")

>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_n_random(
...     index,
...     20,
...     min_length=40,
...     max_length=100,
...     split=3/4,
...     set_labels=["train", "test"]
... )
>>> splitter.plot().show()
```

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_rolling](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_rolling "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_rolling") if `length` is None or "optimize",

Uses [get_index_ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/indexing/#vectorbtpro.base.indexing.get_index_ranges "vectorbtpro.base.indexing.get_index_ranges") to generate start and end indices
for splitting the index. Keyword arguments relevant to index range generation are
extracted from `**kwargs`, while the remaining ones are passed to [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index to be divided into ranges.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments distributed between [get_index_ranges](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/indexing/#vectorbtpro.base.indexing.get_index_ranges "vectorbtpro.base.indexing.get_index_ranges")
    and [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")
:   New [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

__Examples__

Translate each quarter into a range:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> index = pd.date_range("2020", "2021", freq="D")

>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_ranges(index, every="QS")
>>> splitter.plot().show()
```

In addition to the above, reserve the last month for testing purposes:

```pycon
>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_ranges(
...     index,
...     every="QS",
...     split=(1.0, lambda index: index.month == index.month[-1]),

... )
>>> splitter.plot().show()
```

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance from a rolling range of fixed length.

Uses [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits") to generate an array of splits and corresponding labels, and then
construct the [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index over which the rolling range is computed.

**```length```** :&ensp;`Union[int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Desired length of the rolling range.

**```offset```** :&ensp;`Union[int, float, TimedeltaLike]`
:   Offset after the previous range's
    right boundary to determine the start of the next range.

    See [RelRange.offset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset").

**```offset_anchor```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Anchor point used when applying the offset.

    See [RelRange.offset_anchor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset_anchor "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset_anchor").

**```offset_anchor_set```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Index of the set from the previous range
    used as the offset anchor.

    If None, the entire previous split is used as a single anchor.
    By default, the first set is used.

**```offset_space```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Type of offset space.

    See [RelRange.offset_space](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset_space "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange.offset_space").

**```backwards```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, str]`
:   Determines whether rolling occurs in reverse order.

    If set to `'sorted'`, splits are sorted by their start index after rolling.

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```range_bounds_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for getting range bounds.

    See [Splitter.get_range_bounds](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")

### Splitter.from_split_func | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L1888-L2073)

```python
Splitter.from_split_func(
    index,
    split_func,
    split_args=None,
    split_kwargs=None,
    fix_ranges=True,
    split=None,
    split_range_kwargs=None,
    range_bounds_kwargs=None,
    template_context=None,
    freq=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create a [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance from a custom split function.

This method repeatedly calls `split_func` with substituted templates in `split_args`
and `split_kwargs`. The function should return a split or a single range (if not iterable)
or None to terminate the loop. When `fix_ranges` is True or if `split` is provided,
the returned split is processed using [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") and its bounds are
determined via [Splitter.get_range_bounds](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds").

Template substitutions have access to the following:

* `split_idx`: Current split index, starting at 0.

* `splits`: Nested list of splits generated so far.

* `bounds`: Nested list of bounds generated so far.

* `prev_start`: Left bound of the previous split.

* `prev_end`: Right bound of the previous split.

* All arguments for [Splitter.from_split_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_split_func "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_split_func").

__Args__

**```index```** :&ensp;`IndexLike`
:   Index used for splitting.

**```split_func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Function that returns a new split based on substituted arguments.

**```split_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Positional arguments for `split_func`.

**```split_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `split_func`.

**```fix_ranges```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to convert relative ranges ([RelRange](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.RelRange")) into fixed ([FixRange](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.FixRange "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.FixRange")).

**```split```** :&ensp;`Optional[SplitLike]`
:   Specification for further splitting of each range.

    If None, the entire range is treated as a single split;
    otherwise, [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range") is used.

**```split_range_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for range splitting.

    See [Splitter.split_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.split_range").

**```range_bounds_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for getting range bounds.

    See [Splitter.get_range_bounds](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_range_bounds").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the index (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.from_splits](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.from_splits").

__Returns__

[Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter")
:   New [Splitter](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter") instance.

__Examples__

Rolling window of 30 elements, 20 for train and 10 for test:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> index = pd.date_range("2020", "2021", freq="D")

>>> def split_func(splits, bounds, index):
...     if len(splits) == 0:
...         new_split = (slice(0, 20), slice(20, 30))
...     else:
...         # Previous split, first set, right bound
...         prev_end = bounds[-1][0][1]
...         new_split = (
...             slice(prev_end, prev_end + 20),
...             slice(prev_end + 20, prev_end + 30)
...         )
...     if new_split[-1].stop > len(index):
...         return None
...     return new_split

>>> splitter = vbt.Splitter.from_split_func(
...     index,
...     split_func,
...     split_args=(
...         vbt.Rep("splits"),
...         vbt.Rep("bounds"),
...         vbt.Rep("index"),
...     ),
...     set_labels=["train", "test"]
... )
>>> splitter.plot().show()
```

![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/from_split_func.light.svg#only-light){: .iimg loading=lazy }
![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/from_split_func.dark.svg#only-dark){: .iimg loading=lazy }

### Splitter.get_bounds | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L5572-L5631)

* [norm_set_overlap_matrix_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/nb/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.nb.norm_set_overlap_matrix_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.nb.norm_set_overlap_matrix_nb") for `by="set"` and `normalize=True`.

* [set_overlap_matrix_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/nb/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.nb.set_overlap_matrix_nb "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.nb.set_overlap_matrix_nb") for `by="set"` and `normalize=False`.

__Args__

:   Specifies which overlap matrix to compute; must be one of "split", "set", or "range".

**```normalize```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to normalize overlaps relative to the
    total True values in both ranges.

**```squeeze_one_split```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to squeeze the output if only one split exists.

**```squeeze_one_set```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to squeeze the output if only one set exists.

**```index_combine_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for combining indexes.

    See [combine_indexes](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/indexes/#vectorbtpro.base.indexes.combine_indexes "vectorbtpro.base.indexes.combine_indexes").

:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.get_mask_arr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_mask_arr "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_mask_arr").

### Splitter.get_ready_obj_range | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L3559-L3645)

```python
Splitter.get_ready_obj_range(
    obj,
    range_,
    remap_to_obj=True,
    obj_index=None,
    obj_freq=None,
    template_context=None,
    jitted=None,
    silence_warnings=False,
    index=None,
    freq=None,
    return_obj_meta=False,
    **ready_range_kwargs
)
```

Get a ready-to-use range for indexing an array-like object.

Determine and process a range that aligns with the object index. When the object
is Pandas-like or an index is provided, obtain the index using [Splitter.get_obj_index](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_obj_index "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_obj_index")
(if needed) and remap the range using [Splitter.remap_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.remap_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.remap_range"). Finally, convert the range
into a form suitable for direct indexing using [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range").

__Args__

**```obj```** :&ensp;`Any`
:   Array-like object to be indexed.

**```range_```** :&ensp;`FixRangeLike`
:   Input range to be processed.

**```remap_to_obj```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to remap the range to the object's index.

**```obj_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[IndexLike]`
:   Target index for remapping, if available.

**```obj_freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the target index
    (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

**```index```** :&ensp;`Optional[IndexLike]`
:   Source index associated with the range.

**```freq```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Frequency of the source index
    (e.g., "daily", "15 min", "index_mean").

    See [infer_index_freq](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/datetime_/#vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq "vectorbtpro.utils.datetime_.infer_index_freq").

**```return_obj_meta```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to return metadata about the object.

**```**ready_range_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range").

    Allows zero-length ranges by default.

__Returns__

`Any`
:   Processed range ready for indexing, or a tuple with object metadata and the range if requested.

### Splitter.get_ready_range | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L2756-L3004)

```python
Splitter.get_ready_range(
    range_,
    allow_relative=False,
    allow_zero_len=False,
    range_format='slice_or_any',
    template_context=None,
    index=None,
    return_meta=False
)
```

Return a range directly usable for array indexing.

This function converts an input range into a format suitable for array indexing.
The converted range can be one of the following:
a datetime-like or integer slice with an exclusive right bound, a 1D NumPy array of indices,
or a 1D boolean mask matching the length of the index.

__Args__

**```range_```** :&ensp;`FixRangeLike`
:   Initial range specification.

    This may be a callable, slice, fixed range, or array.

**```allow_relative```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Allow relative ranges.

    Relative ranges must be fixed unless this is True.

**```allow_zero_len```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Permit ranges with zero length.

**```range_format```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Format of the returned range.

    Accepted options are:

    * "any": Return any supported format.

    * "indices": Return integer indices.

    * "mask": Return a boolean mask matching the index length.

    * "slice": Return a slice.

    * "slice_or_indices": Return a slice, or indices if slice conversion fails.

    * "slice_or_mask": Return a slice, or a mask if slice conversion fails.

    * "slice_or_any": Return a slice, or any available format if slice conversion fails.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```index```** :&ensp;`Optional[IndexLike]`
:   Index used for aligning and validating the range.

    If not provided, the index is taken from [Splitter.index](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.index "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.index").

**```return_meta```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Return a metadata dictionary (which includes the converted range) if True.

__Returns__

`Union[RelRangeLike, ReadyRangeLike, dict]`
:   Range converted to the specified format,
    or a metadata dictionary if `return_meta` is True.

### Splitter.get_set_coverage | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L6083-L6139)

```python
Splitter.get_set_coverage(
    overlapping=False,
    normalize=True,
    relative=False,
    split_group_by=None,
    set_group_by=None,
    squeeze_one_set=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Return the coverage of each set mask.

Coverage is calculated based on the provided parameters:

* If `overlapping` is True, compute the count of overlapping True values
    between splits for each set.

* If `normalize` is True, the count is normalized by the length of the index.

* If both `normalize` and `relative` are True, compute the coverage relative
    to the total True count across all sets.

__Args__

**```overlapping```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to compute overlapping True values between splits.

**```normalize```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to normalize the coverage by the index length.

**```relative```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   When normalized, whether to compute coverage relative to the overall True count.

**```split_group_by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification for defining splits.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```set_group_by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification for defining sets.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```squeeze_one_set```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to squeeze the output if only one set exists.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.get_mask_arr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_mask_arr "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_mask_arr").

__Returns__

`MaybeSeries`
:   Coverage for each set, either as a scalar or as a Series indexed by set labels.

### Splitter.guess_method | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L2075-L2118)

```python
Splitter.guess_method(
    **kwargs
)
```

Guess the appropriate factory method based on provided keyword arguments.

This method inspects the keyword arguments and compares them against the required and optional
arguments of factory methods (i.e., methods starting with `from_`) defined in the class. If multiple
methods match, it selects the one with the fewest combined required and optional arguments,
preferring `from_n_rolling` when available. Returns None if no suitable method is found.

__Args__

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments used to determine the factory method.

__Returns__

`Optional[str]`
:   Name of the factory method if a unique match is found; otherwise, None.

### Splitter.merge_split | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L3201-L3292)

```python
Splitter.merge_split(
    split,
    range_format=None,
    wrap_with_template=False,
    wrap_with_fixrange=False,
    wrap_with_hslice=False,
    template_context=None,
    index=None
)
```

Merge multiple fixed ranges from a split into a single fixed range.

Create a single fixed range by merging individual ranges from the provided split.
The function constructs a boolean mask marking True for elements within any range.
If all input ranges are masks, the result is a mask; if all are slices, a slice is
returned when possible; otherwise, integer indices are returned.

__Args__

**```split```** :&ensp;`FixSplit`
:   Collection of fixed ranges to merge.

**```range_format```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Format for the range.

    See [Splitter.get_ready_range](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_ready_range").

**```wrap_with_template```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to wrap the resulting ranges with a template of type
    [Rep](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/template/#vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep "vectorbtpro.utils.template.Rep").

**```wrap_with_fixrange```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, wrap the merged range with [FixRange](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.FixRange "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.FixRange").

    When None, the type is determined based on sequence checking.

**```wrap_with_hslice```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, and applicable, wrap a slice result with an `hslice`.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```index```** :&ensp;`Optional[IndexLike]`
:   Index used for alignment.

    If not provided, [Splitter.index](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.index "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.index") is used.

__Returns__

`FixRangeLike`
:   Merged fixed range, represented as a mask, slice,
    or integer indices depending on input types.

### Splitter.plot_coverage | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L6596-L6708)

Plot index coverage as rows and sets as lines.

This method generates a plot where each index is represented as a row and
each set is shown as a line. A stacked area plot is created if `stacked` is True;
otherwise, a line plot is produced.

__Args__

**```stacked```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Plot using a stacked area plot if True; otherwise, use a line plot.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```set_group_by```** :&ensp;`AnyGroupByLike`
:   Grouping specification for defining sets.

    See [BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/accessors/#vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.accessors.BaseIDXAccessor.get_grouper").

**```mask_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for [Splitter.get_iter_set_masks](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/splitting/base/#vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_iter_set_masks "vectorbtpro.generic.splitting.base.Splitter.get_iter_set_masks").

**```trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLikeSequence`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for the mask.

    If provided as a sequence, each set uses its corresponding settings.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`

    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

### Splitter.remap_range | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/generic/splitting/base.py#L3477-L3536)
