### IndicatorFactory.get_indicator | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/factory.py#L3973-L4045)

```python
IndicatorFactory.get_indicator(
    name,
    location=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Return the indicator class corresponding to the given name and location.

The indicator name can include a location prefix separated by a colon. For example,
`"talib:sma"` or `"talib_sma"` returns the TA-Lib SMA indicator. If no location is specified,
the indicator is searched across all available sources, including vectorbtpro indicators.

__Args__

**```name```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Name of the indicator, optionally including a location prefix.

**```location```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Location to filter the search for the indicator.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for the respective indicator constructor.

__Returns__

`Type[IndicatorBase]`
:   Indicator class matching the provided name.

Return a list of indicator names optionally filtered by a pattern or location.

A pattern may also represent a location, in which case all indicators from that location are returned.
For supported locations, see [IndicatorFactory.list_locations](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.list_locations "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.list_locations").

__Args__

**```pattern```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Pattern to filter indicator names.

    If the pattern matches a location, all indicators from that location are returned.

**```case_sensitive```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to treat the pattern as case-sensitive.

**```use_regex```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the pattern is a regular expression.

**```location```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Specific location from which to list indicators.

**```prepend_location```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   When True, indicator names are prefixed with their location.

__Returns__

`List[str]`
:   List of matching indicator names.

Parse the configuration of a Pandas TA indicator.

This class method inspects the signature of the provided indicator function to determine
its inputs, parameters, and outputs. It creates a test DataFrame using random data, passes
it to the function, and parses the output to extract column names. The resulting configuration
dictionary encapsulates details required for further processing.

__Args__

**```func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Pandas TA indicator function to parse.

    The function is inspected to detect input and parameter names.

**```test_input_names```** :&ensp;`Optional[Sequence[str]]`
:   Collection of potential input parameter names.

    Used to identify input columns if not explicitly annotated.

**```test_index_len```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of rows in the generated test DataFrame.

**```silence_warnings```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to suppress warning messages.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for the indicator function.

__Returns__

`Kwargs`
:   Dictionary containing the following keys:

    * `class_name`: Uppercase name of the indicator function.

    * `class_docstring`: Original docstring of the indicator function.

    * `input_names`: List of detected input parameter names.

    * `param_names`: List of parameter names that have default values.

    * `output_names`: List of output column names extracted from the function's result.

    * `defaults`: Mapping of parameter names to their default values.

### IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/factory.py#L2941-L3547)

```python
IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func(
    apply_func,
    cache_func=None,
    takes_1d=False,
    select_params=True,
    pass_packed=False,
    cache_pass_packed=None,
    pass_per_column=False,
    cache_pass_per_column=None,
    forward_skipna=False,
    kwargs_as_args=None,
    jit_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Build indicator class around a custom apply function.

Construct and return an indicator class that wraps a custom apply function for calculations.
This method simplifies indicator creation by handling caching, parameter selection, and
concatenation of outputs automatically. In contrast to [IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func"),
it works with one parameter selection at a time, limiting the ability to view all combinations.

The computation and concatenation are executed using [apply_and_concat_each](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/combining/#vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat_each "vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat_each").

!!! note
    If `apply_func` is a Numba-compiled function:

    * All inputs are automatically converted to NumPy arrays.

    * Each positional argument must be of a Numba-compatible type.

    * Keyword arguments cannot be passed.

    * Output arrays must have identical shapes, data types, and data orders.

!!! note
    Reserved arguments such as `per_column` are passed as positional arguments when
    `jitted_loop` is True, and as keyword arguments otherwise.

__Args__

**```apply_func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Function that receives inputs, a selection of parameters,
    and additional arguments, and performs calculations.

    Arguments are passed in the following order:

    * `i`, the index of the parameter combination, if `select_params` is False.

    * `input_shape` if `pass_input_shape` is True and `input_shape` is not in `kwargs_as_args`.

    * Input arrays corresponding to `input_names`, passed as a tuple if `pass_packed` is True,
        or unpacked otherwise. When `select_params` is True, each argument is a list of arrays
        (one per parameter combination). If `per_column` is True, each array corresponds to a column;
        otherwise, they all refer to the same array. If `takes_1d` is True, each array is further split
        into multiple column arrays. Still passed as a single array to the caching function.

    * In-place output arrays corresponding to `in_output_names`, with similar behavior as input arrays.

    * Parameter values corresponding to `param_names`, passed as a tuple if `pass_packed` is True,
        or unpacked otherwise. If `select_params` is True, each argument is a list with one value per
        parameter combination. When `per_column` is True, each value corresponds to a column; if
        `takes_1d` is True, each value is repeated by the number of columns.

    * Variable arguments if `var_args` is set to True.

    * `per_column` argument if `pass_per_column` is True and not present in `kwargs_as_args`
        and if `jitted_loop` is True.

    * Positional arguments listed in `kwargs_as_args`.

    * Other keyword arguments if `jitted_loop` is False, also including `takes_1d` and `per_column`
        if needed.

    !!! note
        The shape of each output must match the corresponding input.

**```cache_func```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Function to preprocess inputs via caching
    before invoking `apply_func`.

    It accepts the same arguments as `apply_func` and must return a single object or
    a tuple of objects. The returned objects are appended as additional arguments to `apply_func`.

**```takes_1d```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split 2D arrays into multiple 1D arrays along the column axis.

**```select_params```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to automatically select in-place outputs and parameters.

    If False, the current iteration index is prepended to the arguments.

**```pass_packed```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to pass inputs, in-place outputs, and parameters as packed tuples.

    For Numba-compiled functions, tuples are passed instead.

**```cache_pass_packed```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Overrides `pass_packed` for the caching function.

**```pass_per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to pass the `per_column` flag to the apply function.

**```cache_pass_per_column```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Overrides `pass_per_column` for the caching function.

**```forward_skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to forward the `skipna` argument to the apply function.

**```kwargs_as_args```** :&ensp;`Optional[Iterable[str]]`
:   Names of keyword arguments from `**kwargs`
    to pass as positional arguments to the apply function.

    Should be used with `jitted_loop=True` as Numba does not support variable keyword arguments.

**```jit_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the `@njit` decorator of the parameter
    selection function.

    Has `nogil` set to True by default.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func")
    and ultimately to [apply_and_concat_each](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/combining/#vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat_each "vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat_each").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Indicator class constructed around the provided apply function.

__Examples__

Following example produces the same indicator as the [IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func") example.

```pycon
>>> @njit
... def apply_func_nb(ts1, ts2, p1, p2, arg1, arg2):
...     return ts1 * p1 + arg1, ts2 * p2 + arg2

>>> MyInd = vbt.IF(
...     input_names=['ts1', 'ts2'],
...     param_names=['p1', 'p2'],
...     output_names=['out1', 'out2']
... ).with_apply_func(
...     apply_func_nb, var_args=True,
...     kwargs_as_args=['arg2'], arg2=200)

>>> myInd = MyInd.run(price, price * 2, [1, 2], [3, 4], 100)
>>> myInd.out1
custom_p1              1             2
custom_p2              3             4
                a      b      a      b
2020-01-01  101.0  105.0  102.0  110.0
2020-01-02  102.0  104.0  104.0  108.0
2020-01-03  103.0  103.0  106.0  106.0
2020-01-04  104.0  102.0  108.0  104.0
2020-01-05  105.0  101.0  110.0  102.0
>>> myInd.out2
custom_p1              1             2
custom_p2              3             4
                a      b      a      b
2020-01-01  206.0  230.0  208.0  240.0
2020-01-02  212.0  224.0  216.0  232.0
2020-01-03  218.0  218.0  224.0  224.0
2020-01-04  224.0  212.0  232.0  216.0
2020-01-05  230.0  206.0  240.0  208.0
```

To change the execution engine or specify other engine-related arguments, use `execute_kwargs`:

```pycon
>>> import time

>>> def apply_func(ts, p):
...     time.sleep(1)
...     return ts * p

>>> MyInd = vbt.IF(
...     input_names=['ts'],
...     param_names=['p'],
...     output_names=['out']
... ).with_apply_func(apply_func)

>>> %timeit MyInd.run(price, [1, 2, 3])
3.02 s ± 3.47 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)

>>> %timeit MyInd.run(price, [1, 2, 3], execute_kwargs=dict(engine='dask'))
1.02 s ± 2.67 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)
```

### IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/factory.py#L2462-L2939)

```python
IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func(
    custom_func,
    require_input_shape=False,
    param_settings=None,
    in_output_settings=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    var_args=False,
    keyword_only_args=False,
    **pipeline_kwargs
)
```

Build an indicator class based on a custom calculation function.

This method offers full flexibility compared to [IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func").
The caller is responsible for handling caching and concatenation of columns for each
parameter (e.g., via [apply_and_concat](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/combining/#vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat "vectorbtpro.base.combining.apply_and_concat")). Additionally,
ensure that each output array has the correct number of columns, which should equal
the number of input array columns multiplied by the number of parameter combinations.

__Args__

**```custom_func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Function that processes broadcast arrays corresponding to
    `input_names`, in-place output arrays corresponding to `in_output_names`, and
    broadcast parameter arrays corresponding to `param_names`, along with additional
    positional and keyword arguments.

    It returns outputs corresponding to `output_names` and any extra objects to be
    included with the indicator instance.

    It can be Numba-compiled.

    !!! note
        Each output's shape must match the input shape repeated n times (where n is
        the number of parameter values) along the column axis.

**```require_input_shape```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether the input shape is required.

**```param_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Dictionary of parameter settings keyed by name.

    See [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline").

**```in_output_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Dictionary of in-place output settings keyed by name.

    See [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline").

**```hide_params```** :&ensp;`Union[None, bool, Sequence[str]]`
:   Either a boolean to hide all parameter column
    levels or a list of parameter names for which the column levels should be hidden.

**```hide_default```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, hides column levels for parameters that have default values.

**```var_args```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Specifies whether run methods should accept variable positional arguments (`*args`).

    Set to True if `custom_func` requires additional positional arguments
    not defined in the configuration.

**```keyword_only_args```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Specifies whether run methods should enforce keyword-only arguments.

    Set to True to require keyword arguments and avoid misplacement.

**```**pipeline_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline").

    These can include default values and references using [Ref](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/reshaping/#vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.Ref "vectorbtpro.base.reshaping.Ref").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the indicator.

    If `custom_func` returns more objects than defined in `output_names`,
    the additional objects are returned as a tuple alongside the indicator instance.
__Examples__

Following example produces the same indicator as the [IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func") example.

```pycon
>>> @njit
>>> def apply_func_nb(i, ts1, ts2, p1, p2, arg1, arg2):
...     return ts1 * p1[i] + arg1, ts2 * p2[i] + arg2

>>> @njit
... def custom_func(ts1, ts2, p1, p2, arg1, arg2):
...     return vbt.base.combining.apply_and_concat_multiple_nb(
...         len(p1), apply_func_nb, ts1, ts2, p1, p2, arg1, arg2)

>>> MyInd = vbt.IF(
...     input_names=['ts1', 'ts2'],
...     param_names=['p1', 'p2'],
...     output_names=['o1', 'o2']
... ).with_custom_func(custom_func, var_args=True, arg2=200)

>>> myInd = MyInd.run(price, price * 2, [1, 2], [3, 4], 100)
>>> myInd.o1
custom_p1              1             2
custom_p2              3             4
                a      b      a      b
2020-01-01  101.0  105.0  102.0  110.0
2020-01-02  102.0  104.0  104.0  108.0
2020-01-03  103.0  103.0  106.0  106.0
2020-01-04  104.0  102.0  108.0  104.0
2020-01-05  105.0  101.0  110.0  102.0
>>> myInd.o2
custom_p1              1             2
custom_p2              3             4
                a      b      a      b
2020-01-01  206.0  230.0  208.0  240.0
2020-01-02  212.0  224.0  216.0  232.0
2020-01-03  218.0  218.0  224.0  224.0
2020-01-04  224.0  212.0  232.0  216.0
2020-01-05  230.0  206.0  240.0  208.0
```

The primary difference between `apply_func_nb` in this example and in
[IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorFactory.with_apply_func") is that here the function receives an index for
the current parameter combination, which can be used for parameter selection.

Alternatively, you can omit the separate `apply_func_nb` function and implement your
logic directly in `custom_func` (which need not be Numba-compiled):

```pycon
>>> @njit
... def custom_func(ts1, ts2, p1, p2, arg1, arg2):
...     input_shape = ts1.shape
...     n_params = len(p1)
...     out1 = np.empty((input_shape[0], input_shape[1] * n_params), dtype=float_)
...     out2 = np.empty((input_shape[0], input_shape[1] * n_params), dtype=float_)
...     for k in range(n_params):
...         for col in range(input_shape[1]):
...             for i in range(input_shape[0]):
...                 out1[i, input_shape[1] * k + col] = ts1[i, col] * p1[k] + arg1
...                 out2[i, input_shape[1] * k + col] = ts2[i, col] * p2[k] + arg2
...     return out1, out2
```

    See [HurstMethod](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod").

**```max_lag```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum lag parameter for the standard computation.

**```min_log```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Minimum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```max_log```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```log_step```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Increment on the logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```min_chunk```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Minimum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

**```max_chunk```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

**```num_chunks```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of chunks for RS and DMA methods.

**```stabilize```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to enable stabilization in the polynomial fit.

__Returns__

`float`
:   Estimated Hurst exponent.

## macd_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/nb.py#L1012-L1094)

```python
macd_1d_nb(
    close,
    fast_window=12,
    slow_window=26,
    signal_window=9,
    wtype=2,
    macd_wtype=None,
    signal_wtype=None,
    minp=None,
    macd_minp=None,
    signal_minp=None,
    adjust=False,
    macd_adjust=None,
    signal_adjust=None
)
```

Calculate MACD and signal line for a 1-D series of close prices.

Compute the fast and slow moving averages, derive the MACD as their difference,
and calculate the signal line as the moving average of the MACD.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1-D array of close prices.

**```fast_window```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window size for computing the fast moving average.

**```slow_window```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window size for computing the slow moving average.

**```signal_window```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window size for computing the signal moving average.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Weighting type.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```macd_wtype```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Weighting type for MACD computation.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType"). Uses `wtype` if not provided.

**```signal_wtype```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Weighting type for signal computation.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType"). Uses `wtype` if not provided.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```macd_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum period for the MACD moving average.

    Uses `minp` if not provided.

**```signal_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum period for the signal moving average.

    Uses `minp` if not provided.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

**```macd_adjust```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Alternative flag for MACD moving average adjustment.

    Uses `adjust` if not provided.

**```signal_adjust```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Alternative flag for signal moving average adjustment.

    Uses `adjust` if not provided.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple where the first element is the MACD and the second is the signal line.

## signal_detection_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/nb.py#L2635-L2747)

```python
signal_detection_1d_nb(
    close,
    lag=14,
    factor=1.0,
    influence=1.0,
    up_factor=None,
    down_factor=None,
    mean_influence=None,
    std_influence=None
)
```

Detect signals from a one-dimensional close price series.

Analyzes the input array using a moving window defined by `lag` to detect upward or downward
signals based on dynamic thresholding with influence factors. Computed signals and corresponding
upper/lower bands are returned.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   Array of close prices.

**```lag```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window size for computing moving averages and standard deviations.

**```factor```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Factor to determine the threshold for signal detection.

    Provided as a scalar or per row.

**```influence```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Influence factor for updating the filtering process.

    Provided as a scalar or per row.

**```up_factor```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Factor for the upward threshold.

    Provided as a scalar or per row.

    If None, uses `factor`.

**```down_factor```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Factor for the downward threshold.

    Provided as a scalar or per row.

    If None, uses `factor`.

**```mean_influence```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Influence factor for updating the moving average filter.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    If None, uses `influence`.

**```std_influence```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Influence factor for updating the standard deviation filter.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    If None, uses `influence`.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple containing
    the signal array, upper band, and lower band.

:   Weighting type for the slow %D moving average.

**```slow_k_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`

    Falls back to `minp` if not specified.

**```slow_d_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`

    Falls back to `minp` if not specified.

:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

    Defaults to `adjust` if not provided.

**```slow_d_adjust```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag for adjusting the slow %D moving average.

    Defaults to `adjust` if not provided.

:   Tuple containing fast %K, slow %K, and slow %D values.

**```group_lens```** :&ensp;`GroupLens`
:   Array defining the number of columns in each group.

## talib_func | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/talib_.py#L35-L325)

```python
talib_func(
    func_name
)
```

Get a TA-Lib indicator function.

Verifies the availability of TA-Lib and returns a callable that applies the specified TA-Lib
indicator on provided data. The returned function handles input arrays in various formats and
optionally performs broadcasting, resampling, and output wrapping.

__Args__

**```func_name```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Name of the TA-Lib indicator function.

    Case is ignored.

__Returns__

`Callable`
:   Function that executes `talib.<FUNC_NAME>` on NumPy arrays, Pandas Series, or DataFrames.


Class representing the Average Directional Movement Index (ADX) indicator.

Measures trend strength to assist traders in assessing market conditions.

__See__

* [ADX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run") for the main entry point.

* [adx_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.adx_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.adx_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/adx.asp> for the definition of ADX.

### ADX.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/adx.py#L1505-L1571)

```python
ADX.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=3,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

2-dim version of `adx_1d_nb`.

Computes the average directional movement index components (+DI, -DI, DX, and ADX)
for 2-dimensional input arrays column-wise.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of close prices.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   +DI, -DI, DX, and ADX values for each column.

### ADX.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/adx.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
ADX.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,

```

Forward inputs and parameters to [ADX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[ADX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func"). If [ADX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[ADX.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [ADX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### ADX.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/adx.py#L1-L206)

```python
ADX.run(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    short_name='adx',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [ADX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `plus_di`: Positive Directional Indicator (DI) series.

* `minus_di`: Negative Directional Indicator (DI) series.

* `dx`: Directional Movement Index (DX) series.

* `adx`: Average Directional Index (ADX) series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [ADX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### ADX.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/adx.py#L1-L206)

```python
ADX.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [ADX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `plus_di`: Positive Directional Indicator (DI) series.

* `minus_di`: Negative Directional Indicator (DI) series.

* `dx`: Directional Movement Index (DX) series.

* `adx`: Average Directional Index (ADX) series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [ADX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [ADX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/adx/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.adx.ADX.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py)

Module defining the [ATR](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR") class for calculating the Average True Range indicator.

## ATR | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L25-L66)

```python
ATR(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the Average True Range (ATR) indicator.

Calculates the average true range to measure price volatility.
Large price movements that result in extensive trading ranges typically yield a higher ATR,
indicating periods of increased market volatility.

__See__

* [ATR.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run") for the main entry point.

* [atr_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.atr_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.atr_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/atr.asp> for the definition of ATR.

### ATR.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L1376-L1439)

```python
ATR.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=3,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

2-dim version of `atr_1d_nb`.

Computes the True Range and Average True Range for 2-dimensional input arrays column-wise.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-dimensional array of close prices.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d]`
:   True Range and Average True Range for each column.

### ATR.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
ATR.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [ATR.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[ATR.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func"). If [ATR.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[ATR.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

:   Additional positional arguments.

:   Shape of the input arrays.

:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`

### ATR.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L1-L206)

```python
ATR.run(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    short_name='atr',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [ATR](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `tr`: True Range (TR) series.

* `atr`: Average True Range (ATR) series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [ATR](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### ATR.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L1-L206)

```python
ATR.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [ATR](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `tr`: True Range (TR) series.

* `atr`: Average True Range (ATR) series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [ATR.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [ATR.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/atr/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.atr.ATR.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

### ATR.tr | class property | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/atr.py#L1995-L1996)

Output array for `tr`.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py)

Module defining the [BBANDS](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS") class for Bollinger Bands indicator.

## BBANDS | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L27-L93)

```python
BBANDS(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the Bollinger Bands (BBANDS) indicator.

Bollinger Bands is a technical analysis tool that plots three lines:

* Upper band (calculated a specified number of standard deviations above the middle band).

* Middle band (a simple moving average of the security's price).

* Lower band (calculated a specified number of standard deviations below the middle band).

These bands help identify market volatility and potential overbought or oversold conditions.

__See__

* [BBANDS.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run") for the main entry point.

* [bbands_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* [bbands_percent_b_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_percent_b_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_percent_b_nb") for the underlying implementation of [BBANDS.percent_b](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.percent_b "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.percent_b").

* [bbands_bandwidth_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_bandwidth_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.bbands_bandwidth_nb") for the underlying implementation of [BBANDS.bandwidth](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.bandwidth "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.bandwidth").

* <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/bollingerbands.asp> for the definition of BBANDS.

### BBANDS.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L252-L319)

```python
BBANDS.apply_func(
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=0,
    alpha=2.0,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False,
    ddof=0
)
```

2-dim version of `bbands_1d_nb`.

Computes Bollinger Bands for each column of a 2-dimensional array.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D array where each column is a data series.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```alpha```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Multiplier for the standard deviation.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

**```ddof```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Delta degrees of freedom.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Upper, middle, and lower Bollinger Bands for each column.

### BBANDS.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
BBANDS.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [BBANDS.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[BBANDS.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func"). If [BBANDS.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[BBANDS.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [BBANDS.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### BBANDS.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L115-L229)

```python
    column=None,
```

Plot the BBANDS traces.

Return the updated figure with plotted [BBANDS.upper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.upper "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.upper"), [BBANDS.middle](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.middle "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.middle"), [BBANDS.lower](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.lower "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.lower"),
and optionally [BBANDS.close](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.close "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.close").

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to plot the close price.

**```close_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [BBANDS.close](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.close "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.close").

**```upper_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [BBANDS.upper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.upper "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.upper").

**```middle_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [BBANDS.middle](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.middle "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.middle").

### BBANDS.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L1-L206)

```python
BBANDS.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    alpha=Default(value=2),
    short_name='bb',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [BBANDS](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `alpha`: Number of standard deviations from the middle band to the upper and lower bands.

__Outputs__

* `upper`: Upper Bollinger Band series.

* `middle`: Middle Bollinger Band series.

* `lower`: Lower Bollinger Band series.

__Lazy outputs__

* `percent_b`: Percent B series.

* `bandwidth`: Bollinger Bandwidth series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [BBANDS](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### BBANDS.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/bbands.py#L1-L206)

```python
BBANDS.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    alpha=Default(value=2),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [BBANDS](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `alpha`: Number of standard deviations from the middle band to the upper and lower bands.

__Outputs__

* `upper`: Upper Bollinger Band series.

* `middle`: Middle Bollinger Band series.

* `lower`: Lower Bollinger Band series.

__Lazy outputs__

* `percent_b`: Percent B series.

* `bandwidth`: Bollinger Bandwidth series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [BBANDS.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [BBANDS.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/bbands/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.bbands.BBANDS.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py)

Module defining the [HURST](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST") class for calculating the rolling Hurst exponent.

## HURST | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py#L25-L95)

```python
HURST(
    wrapper,
    input_list,

    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,

```

Class representing the moving Hurst exponent indicator.

This indicator measures the long-term memory of a time series.

__See__

* [HURST.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run") for the main entry point.

* [rolling_hurst_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.rolling_hurst_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.rolling_hurst_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurst-Exponent> for the definition of the Hurst exponent.

### HURST.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py#L3200-L3273)

```python
HURST.apply_func(
    close,
    window,
    method=0,
    max_lag=20,
    min_log=1,
    max_log=2,
    log_step=0.25,
    min_chunk=8,
    max_chunk=100,
    num_chunks=5,
    minp=None,
    stabilize=False
)
```

Compute the rolling Hurst exponent for each column in a two-dimensional array.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of price data where each column represents a series.

**```window```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Window size.

**```method```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Hurst exponent computation method.

    See [HurstMethod](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod").

**```max_lag```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum lag parameter for the standard computation.

**```min_log```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Minimum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```max_log```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```log_step```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Increment on the logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

**```min_chunk```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Minimum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

**```max_chunk```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Maximum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

**```num_chunks```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of chunks for RS and DMA methods.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```stabilize```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to enable stabilization in the polynomial fit.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of rolling Hurst exponent values for each column.

### HURST.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
HURST.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [HURST.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[HURST.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func"). If [HURST.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[HURST.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [HURST.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### HURST.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py#L1-L206)

```python
HURST.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=200),
    method=Default(value='standard'),
    max_lag=Default(value=20),
    min_log=Default(value=1),
    max_log=Default(value=2),
    log_step=Default(value=0.25),
    min_chunk=Default(value=8),
    max_chunk=Default(value=100),
    num_chunks=Default(value=5),
    short_name='hurst',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [HURST](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `method`: Hurst exponent computation method (see [HurstMethod](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod"))

* `max_lag`: Maximum lag parameter for the standard computation.

* `min_log`: Minimum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `max_log`: Maximum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `log_step`: Increment on the logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `min_chunk`: Minimum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

* `max_chunk`: Maximum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

* `num_chunks`: Number of chunks for RS and DMA methods.

__Outputs__

* `hurst`: Hurst exponent series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [HURST](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### HURST.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/hurst.py#L1-L206)

```python
HURST.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=200),
    method=Default(value='standard'),
    max_lag=Default(value=20),
    min_log=Default(value=1),
    max_log=Default(value=2),
    log_step=Default(value=0.25),
    min_chunk=Default(value=8),
    max_chunk=Default(value=100),
    num_chunks=Default(value=5),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [HURST](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `method`: Hurst exponent computation method (see [HurstMethod](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.HurstMethod"))

* `max_lag`: Maximum lag parameter for the standard computation.

* `min_log`: Minimum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `max_log`: Maximum logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `log_step`: Increment on the logarithmic scale for the LogRS method.

* `min_chunk`: Minimum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

* `max_chunk`: Maximum chunk size for RS and DMA methods.

* `num_chunks`: Number of chunks for RS and DMA methods.

__Outputs__

* `hurst`: Hurst exponent series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [HURST.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [HURST.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/hurst/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.hurst.HURST.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py)

Module defining the [MA](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA") class for calculating the moving average.

## MA | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py#L25-L57)

```python
MA(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the Moving Average (MA) indicator.

A moving average is a popular technical analysis indicator that smooths out price
fluctuations by filtering out short-term noise from the price data.

__See__

* [MA.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.run") for the main entry point.

* [ma_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.ma_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.ma_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/m/movingaverage.asp> for the definition of MA.

### MA.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py#L63-L117)

```python
MA.apply_func(
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=0,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

2-dim version of `ma_1d_nb`.

Computes the moving average for each column of a 2-dimensional array.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D array where each column represents a data series.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2D array of moving average values.

### MA.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
MA.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [MA.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[MA.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func"). If [MA.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[MA.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [MA.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### MA.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py#L72-L150)

```python
_MA.plot(
    column=None,
    plot_close=True,
```

Plot the moving average alongside the close price.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

### MA.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/ma.py#L1-L206)

```python
MA.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    short_name='ma',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [MA](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/ma/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `ma`: Moving Average (MA) series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.ma.MA.run_pipeline").
