### RSI.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/rsi.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
RSI.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [RSI.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[RSI.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func"). If [RSI.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[RSI.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`

Plot the [RSI.rsi](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.rsi "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.rsi") output of the RSI indicator.

### RSI.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/rsi.py#L1-L206)

```python
RSI.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    short_name='rsi',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [RSI](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `rsi`: Relative Strength Index (RSI) series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [RSI](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### RSI.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/rsi.py#L1-L206)

```python
RSI.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='wilder'),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [RSI](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `rsi`: Relative Strength Index (RSI) series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [RSI.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [RSI.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/rsi/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.rsi.RSI.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py)

## SIGDET | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L26-L97)

For additional details, see [this StackOverflow answer]().

__See__

* <https://stackoverflow.com/a/22640362> for the original algorithm.

### SIGDET.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L2750-L2853)

```python
SIGDET.apply_func(
    close,
    lag=14,
    factor=1.0,
    influence=1.0,
    up_factor=None,
    down_factor=None,
    mean_influence=None,
    std_influence=None
)
```

Compute the 2-dim signal detection.

Applies the one-dimensional `signal_detection_1d_nb` function to each column of the input array
to detect signals and compute corresponding upper and lower bands for multi-dimensional data.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of close prices.

**```lag```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size for computing moving averages and standard deviations.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```factor```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Factor to determine the threshold for signal detection.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

**```influence```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Influence factor for updating the filtering process.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

**```up_factor```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray2dLike]`
:   Factor for the upward threshold.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

    If None, uses `factor`.

**```down_factor```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray2dLike]`
:   Factor for the downward threshold.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

    If None, uses `factor`.

**```mean_influence```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray2dLike]`
:   Influence factor for updating the moving average filter.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

    If None, uses `influence`.

**```std_influence```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray2dLike]`
:   Influence factor for updating the standard deviation filter.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

    If None, uses `influence`.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple containing
    the signal array, upper band, and lower band arrays.

### SIGDET.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
SIGDET.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [SIGDET.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[SIGDET.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func"). If [SIGDET.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[SIGDET.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [SIGDET.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### SIGDET.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L111-L160)

Plot the signal from [SIGDET.signal](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.signal "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.signal").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [SIGDET.signal](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.signal "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.signal").

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

:   Figure object containing the plotted signal.

### SIGDET.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L1-L206)

```python
SIGDET.run(
    close,
    lag=Default(value=14),
    factor=Default(value=1.0),
    influence=Default(value=1.0),
    up_factor=Default(value=None),
    down_factor=Default(value=None),
    mean_influence=Default(value=None),
    std_influence=Default(value=None),
    short_name='sigdet',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [SIGDET](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `lag`: Lag period for the z-score calculation.

* `factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by, as a scalar or an array.

* `influence`: Influence of the z-score on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

* `up_factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by for upward signals, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by for downward signals, as a scalar or an array.

* `mean_influence`: Influence of the mean on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

* `std_influence`: Influence of the standard deviation on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `signal`: Signal series.

* `upper_band`: Upper band series.

* `lower_band`: Lower band series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [SIGDET](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### SIGDET.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/sigdet.py#L1-L206)

```python
SIGDET.run_combs(
    close,
    lag=Default(value=14),
    factor=Default(value=1.0),
    influence=Default(value=1.0),
    up_factor=Default(value=None),
    down_factor=Default(value=None),
    mean_influence=Default(value=None),
    std_influence=Default(value=None),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [SIGDET](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `lag`: Lag period for the z-score calculation.

* `factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by, as a scalar or an array.

* `influence`: Influence of the z-score on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

* `up_factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by for upward signals, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_factor`: Factor to multiply the z-score by for downward signals, as a scalar or an array.

* `mean_influence`: Influence of the mean on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

* `std_influence`: Influence of the standard deviation on the signal, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `signal`: Signal series.

* `upper_band`: Upper band series.

* `lower_band`: Lower band series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [SIGDET.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [SIGDET.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/sigdet/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.sigdet.SIGDET.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py)

Module defining the [STOCH](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH") class for calculating the Stochastic Oscillator indicator.

## STOCH | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L25-L96)

```python
STOCH(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the Stochastic Oscillator (STOCH) indicator.

Implements a stochastic oscillator, a momentum indicator that compares a security's closing
price to its price range over a specified period. It is used to identify overbought and oversold
conditions with values typically bounded between 0 and 100.

See [Investopedia – Stochastic Oscillator](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/s/stochasticoscillator.asp).

__See__

### STOCH.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L874-L1006)

```python
STOCH.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    fast_k_window=14,
    slow_k_window=3,
    slow_d_window=3,
    wtype=0,
    slow_k_wtype=None,
    slow_d_wtype=None,
    minp=None,
    fast_k_minp=None,
    slow_k_minp=None,
    slow_d_minp=None,
    adjust=False,
    slow_k_adjust=None,
    slow_d_adjust=None
)
```

Calculate the Stochastic Oscillator for two-dimensional price arrays column-wise.

This function computes the fast %K, slow %K, and slow %D values for each column using `stoch_1d_nb`.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of close prices.

**```fast_k_window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size for fast %K calculation.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```slow_k_window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size for the slow %K moving average.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```slow_d_window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size for the slow %D moving average.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```slow_k_wtype```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Weighting type for the slow %K moving average.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType"). Uses `wtype` if not provided.

**```slow_d_wtype```** :&ensp;`Optional[FlexArray1dLike]`
:   Weighting type for the slow %D moving average.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType"). Uses `wtype` if not provided.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```fast_k_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum periods for fast %K calculation.

    Falls back to `minp` if not specified.

**```slow_k_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum periods for slow %K calculation.

    Falls back to `minp` if not specified.

**```slow_d_minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum periods for slow %D calculation.

    Falls back to `minp` if not specified.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

**```slow_k_adjust```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag for adjusting the slow %K moving average.

    Defaults to `adjust` if not provided.

**```slow_d_adjust```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Flag for adjusting the slow %D moving average.

    Defaults to `adjust` if not provided.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple containing fast %K, slow %K, and slow %D values for each column.

### STOCH.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
STOCH.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [STOCH.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[STOCH.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func"). If [STOCH.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[STOCH.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [STOCH.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### STOCH.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L114-L222)

```python
_STOCH.plot(
    column=None,
    limits=(20, 80),
    fast_k_trace_kwargs=None,
    slow_k_trace_kwargs=None,
    slow_d_trace_kwargs=None,
    add_shape_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Plot [STOCH.slow_k](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_k "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_k") and [STOCH.slow_d](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_d "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_d").

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```limits```** :&ensp;`Tuple[float, float]`
:   Lower and upper y-axis limits for the filled range.

**```fast_k_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [STOCH.fast_k](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.fast_k "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.fast_k").

**```slow_k_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [STOCH.slow_k](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_k "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_k").

**```slow_d_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [STOCH.slow_d](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_d "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.slow_d").

**```add_shape_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_shape` for each shape.

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

**```**layout_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.update_layout`.

__Returns__

`BaseFigure`
:   Updated or newly created figure with the plotted STOCH traces and filled range.

```pycon
>>> vbt.STOCH.run(ohlcv['High'], ohlcv['Low'], ohlcv['Close']).plot().show()
```

### STOCH.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L1-L206)

```python
STOCH.run(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    fast_k_window=Default(value=14),
    slow_k_window=Default(value=3),
    slow_d_window=Default(value=3),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    slow_k_wtype=Default(value=None),
    slow_d_wtype=Default(value=None),
    short_name='stoch',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [STOCH](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `fast_k_window`: Window size for Fast %K.

* `slow_k_window`: Window size for Slow %K.

* `slow_d_window`: Window size for Slow %D.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `slow_k_wtype`: Weighting type for Slow %K (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `slow_d_wtype`: Weighting type for Slow %D (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `fast_k`: Fast %K series.

* `slow_k`: Slow %K series.

* `slow_d`: Slow %D series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [STOCH](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### STOCH.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/stoch.py#L1-L206)

```python
STOCH.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    fast_k_window=Default(value=14),
    slow_k_window=Default(value=3),
    slow_d_window=Default(value=3),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    slow_k_wtype=Default(value=None),
    slow_d_wtype=Default(value=None),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [STOCH](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `fast_k_window`: Window size for Fast %K.

* `slow_k_window`: Window size for Slow %K.

* `slow_d_window`: Window size for Slow %D.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `slow_k_wtype`: Weighting type for Slow %K (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `slow_d_wtype`: Weighting type for Slow %D (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

__Outputs__

* `fast_k`: Fast %K series.

* `slow_k`: Slow %K series.

* `slow_d`: Slow %D series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [STOCH.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [STOCH.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/stoch/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.stoch.STOCH.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py)

Module defining the [SUPERTREND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND") class for calculating the Supertrend indicator.

## SUPERTREND | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py#L24-L66)

```python
SUPERTREND(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the supertrend indicator.

The supertrend indicator is a trend-following overlay that appears directly on price charts,
providing clear buy and sell signals based on the underlying asset's price action and volatility.

__See__

* [SUPERTREND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run") for the main entry point.

* [supertrend_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.supertrend_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.supertrend_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://www.investopedia.com/supertrend-indicator-7976167> for the definition of the supertrend indicator.

### SUPERTREND.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py#L2572-L2629)

```python
SUPERTREND.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    period=7,
    multiplier=3.0
)
```

Compute the 2-dim Supertrend indicator.

Applies the one-dimensional `supertrend_1d_nb` to each column of the input arrays to compute
the Supertrend indicator for multi-dimensional data.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of close prices.

**```period```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Period for the indicator calculation.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```multiplier```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Multiplier used to determine the volatility threshold.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple containing
    the trend, direction, long, and short arrays.

### SUPERTREND.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
SUPERTREND.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [SUPERTREND.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[SUPERTREND.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func"). If [SUPERTREND.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[SUPERTREND.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [SUPERTREND.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### SUPERTREND.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py#L81-L172)

```python
_SUPERTREND.plot(
    column=None,
    plot_close=True,
    close_trace_kwargs=None,
    superl_trace_kwargs=None,
    supers_trace_kwargs=None,
    add_trace_kwargs=None,
    fig=None,
    make_figure_kwargs=None,
    **layout_kwargs
)
```

Plot the long and short signals of the Supertrend indicator, and optionally the close prices.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [plotting](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.plotting "vectorbtpro._settings.plotting").

__Args__

**```column```** :&ensp;`Optional[Column]`
:   Identifier of the column to plot.

**```plot_close```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to plot the close price.

**```close_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [SUPERTREND.close](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.close "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.close").

**```superl_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [SUPERTREND.long](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.long "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.long").

**```supers_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `plotly.graph_objects.Scatter` for [SUPERTREND.short](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.short "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.short").

**```add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for each trace;
    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`
:   Figure to update; if None, a new figure is created.

### SUPERTREND.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/supertrend.py#L1-L206)

```python
SUPERTREND.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    period=Default(value=7),
    multiplier=Default(value=3),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [SUPERTREND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `period`: Period for the Supertrend calculation.

* `multiplier`: Multiplier for the ATR calculation.

__Outputs__

* `trend`: Supertrend trend series.

* `direction`: Supertrend direction series.

* `long`: Supertrend long signal series.

* `short`: Supertrend short signal series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [SUPERTREND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [SUPERTREND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/supertrend/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.supertrend.SUPERTREND.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py)

Module defining the [VWAP](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP") class for calculating the Volume-Weighted Average Price indicator.

## substitute_anchor | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L29-L49)

```python
substitute_anchor(
    wrapper,
    anchor
)
```

Substitute the reset frequency with group lengths.

Computes group lengths based on the provided `anchor`. If `anchor` is None, returns an array
with the number of rows in the wrapper; otherwise, calculates group lengths using the
wrapper's index grouper.

__Args__

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`ArrayWrapper`
:   Array wrapper instance.

    See [ArrayWrapper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper").

**```anchor```** :&ensp;`Optional[FrequencyLike]`
:   Reset frequency for grouping.

    See [ArrayWrapper.get_index_grouper](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.get_index_grouper "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.get_index_grouper").

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array containing the group lengths.

## VWAP | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L52-L85)

```python
VWAP(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing the Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) indicator.

Calculates the volume-weighted average price commonly used in intraday charts.
The calculation resets at the beginning of each trading session.

The `anchor` parameter specifies the grouping for when the VWAP resets and can be any valid index grouper.

__See__

* [VWAP.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run") for the main entry point.

* [vwap_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/nb/#vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.vwap_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.nb.vwap_nb") for the underlying implementation.

* <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/v/vwap.asp> for the definition of VWAP.

### VWAP.anchor_list | class property | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L1964-L1965)

### VWAP.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L1970-L2015)

```python
VWAP.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    volume,
    group_lens
)
```

Compute the volume weighted average price (VWAP) for 2D arrays.

Apply the 1D computation from `vwap_1d_nb` to each column independently.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of close prices.

**```volume```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array of traded volumes.

**```group_lens```** :&ensp;`GroupLens`
:   Array defining the number of columns in each group.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2D array containing the calculated VWAP values.

### VWAP.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
VWAP.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [VWAP.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[VWAP.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func"). If [VWAP.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[VWAP.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [VWAP.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### VWAP.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L1-L206)

```python
VWAP.run(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    volume,
    anchor=Default(value='D'),
    short_name='vwap',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [VWAP](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

* `volume`: Volume series.

__Parameters__

* `anchor`: Reset frequency for grouping (see [substitute_anchor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.substitute_anchor "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.substitute_anchor")).

__Outputs__

* `vwap`: Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [VWAP](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### VWAP.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/indicators/custom/vwap.py#L1-L206)

```python
VWAP.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    close,
    volume,
    anchor=Default(value='D'),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [VWAP](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

* `volume`: Volume series.

__Parameters__

* `anchor`: Reset frequency for grouping (see [substitute_anchor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.substitute_anchor "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.substitute_anchor")).

__Outputs__

* `vwap`: Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [VWAP.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [VWAP.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/custom/vwap/#vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run "vectorbtpro.indicators.custom.vwap.VWAP.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.knowledge | package | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/__init__.py)

Package providing utility functions and classes for constructing and managing knowledge assets.

Run for the examples:

```pycon
>>> dataset = [
...     {"s": "ABC", "b": True, "d2": {"c": "red", "l": [1, 2]}},
...     {"s": "BCD", "b": True, "d2": {"c": "blue", "l": [3, 4]}},
...     {"s": "CDE", "b": False, "d2": {"c": "green", "l": [5, 6]}},
...     {"s": "DEF", "b": False, "d2": {"c": "yellow", "l": [7, 8]}},
...     {"s": "EFG", "b": False, "d2": {"c": "black", "l": [9, 10]}, "xyz": 123}
... ]
>>> asset = vbt.KnowledgeAsset(dataset)
```

!!! info
    For default settings, see [knowledge](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.knowledge "vectorbtpro._settings.knowledge").

## ComplexAssetPipeline | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/asset_pipelines.py#L241-L474)

```python
ComplexAssetPipeline(
    expression,
    context=None,
    prepare_once=True,
    **resolve_task_kwargs
)
```

Class representing a complex asset pipeline.

This pipeline takes an expression string that may contain nested function calls and
a context mapping. It resolves functions within the expression and evaluates the expression
using [evaluate](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/eval_/#vectorbtpro.utils.eval_.evaluate "vectorbtpro.utils.eval_.evaluate").

__Args__

**```expression```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Expression string to evaluate.

**```context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Mapping of variables for expression evaluation.

**```prepare_once```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to prepare the function's arguments only once.

**```**resolve_task_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for task resolution.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> asset_pipeline = vbt.ComplexAssetPipeline("query(flatten(d), len)")
>>> asset_pipeline(dataset[0])
5
```

__Superclasses__

* [AssetPipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/asset_pipelines/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.asset_pipelines.AssetPipeline "vectorbtpro.knowledge.asset_pipelines.AssetPipeline")

### ComplexAssetPipeline.resolve_expression_and_context | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/asset_pipelines.py#L276-L452)

```python
ComplexAssetPipeline.resolve_expression_and_context(
    expression,
    context=None,
    prepare=True,
    prepare_once=True,
    **resolve_task_kwargs
)
```

Resolve an expression and update its context.

Parses the expression string to extract function calls and their arguments,
then removes the first positional argument from each function call.
It also builds a new context by merging resolved functions with the existing context.

__Args__

**```expression```** :&ensp;`str`
:   Expression string to process.

**```context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Mapping of context variables.

**```prepare```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to prepare the function's arguments before execution.

**```prepare_once```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to prepare the function's arguments only once.

**```**resolve_task_kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for task resolution.

__Returns__

`Tuple[str, Kwargs]`
:   Tuple containing the modified expression and the updated context.

### FindAssetFunc.match_func | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_asset_funcs.py#L942-L1023)

```python
FindAssetFunc.match_func(
    k,
    d,
    target,
    find_all=False,
    **kwargs
)
```

Return whether the given data item matches the specified target criteria used in [FindAssetFunc.call](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_asset_funcs/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.AssetFunc.call "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.FindAssetFunc.call").

This function evaluates `target` against the provided data `d` using different strategies:

* For strings, it utilizes [find](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find") with `return_type="bool"`.

* For other types, it performs equality comparisons.

A `target` may be a callable that takes a key and a value, and returns a boolean or an instance of
[Not](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not") to indicate negation.

__Args__

**```k```** :&ensp;`Optional[Hashable]`
:   Key associated with the current element.

**```d```** :&ensp;`Any`
:   Data item to test.

**```target```** :&ensp;`MaybeList[Any]`
:   Target value(s) or callable(s) to determine if a match occurs.

    Also supports negation using [Not](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not").

**```find_all```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag specifying if all targets should be evaluated.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [find](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find").

__Returns__

`bool`
:   True if the data item matches the target criteria, False otherwise.

### FindAssetFunc.prepare | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_asset_funcs.py#L830-L940)

```python
FindAssetFunc.prepare(
    target,
    path=None,

    find_all=None,
    keep_path=None,
    skip_missing=None,
    source=None,
    in_dumps=None,

    asset_cls=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Prepare positional and keyword arguments for an asset function call.

__Args__

**```target```** :&ensp;`MaybeList[Any]`
:   Target value(s) or callable(s) to determine if a match occurs.

    Also supports negation using [Not](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.Not").

**```path```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Path(s) within the data item to search (e.g. "x.y[0].z").

**```per_path```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, consider targets provided per path.

**```find_all```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Require all targets to be found when multiple targets are provided.

**```keep_path```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, returns results structured as nested dictionaries
    mirroring the specified path.

**```skip_missing```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, skips data items where the specified path is missing.

**```source```** :&ensp;`Optional[CustomTemplateLike]`
:   Template or function to preprocess the source data.

**```in_dumps```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, converts the entire data item to string for searching.

**```dump_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for dumping structured data.

    See [dump](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/formatting/#vectorbtpro.utils.formatting.dump "vectorbtpro.utils.formatting.dump").

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```return_type```** :&ensp;`Optional[str]`
:   Indicates the return type: "item", "field", or "bool".

**```return_path```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Specifies whether to include the path in the returned result.

**```asset_cls```** :&ensp;`Optional[Type[KnowledgeAsset]]`
:   Asset class to use for resolving settings.

    Defaults to [KnowledgeAsset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_assets/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments distributed between [find_in_obj](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find_in_obj "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find_in_obj")
    and [find](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.find").

__Returns__

`ArgsKwargs`
:   Tuple containing the positional arguments and keyword arguments.

### FindReplaceAssetFunc.replace_func | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_asset_funcs.py#L1363-L1429)

```python
FindReplaceAssetFunc.replace_func(
    k,
    d,
    target,
    replacement,
    **kwargs
)
```

Replace a value based on matching criteria.

This method is used by [FindReplaceAssetFunc.call](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_asset_funcs/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.AssetFunc.call "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.FindReplaceAssetFunc.call") to determine the replacement for
a matched value. For string inputs, it applies [replace](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.replace "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.replace") for
text substitution. For other types, it returns the replacement directly if the specified
target condition is met. Both `target` and `replacement` may be callables that take a key and a value,
where `target` returns a boolean indicating a match and `replacement` computes the new value.

__Args__

**```k```** :&ensp;`Optional[Hashable]`
:   Key associated with the current element.

**```d```** :&ensp;`Any`
:   Original value to evaluate for a match.

**```target```** :&ensp;`MaybeList[Any]`
:   Target value(s) or callable(s) to determine if a match occurs.

**```replacement```** :&ensp;`MaybeList[Any]`
:   Replacement value or callable to apply when a match is found.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [replace](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.replace "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.replace").

__Returns__

`Any`
:   Resulting value after replacement if a match is found; otherwise, the original value.

Prepare positional and keyword arguments for an asset function call.

__Args__

**```path```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Path(s) within the data item to get (e.g. "x.y[0].z").

**```keep_path```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, returns results structured as nested dictionaries
    mirroring the specified path.

**```skip_missing```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, skips data items where the specified path is missing.

**```source```** :&ensp;`Optional[CustomTemplateLike]`
:   Template, function, or string for preprocessing;
    in the template, "i" denotes the index, "d" the full data item, and "x" the extracted part.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```asset_cls```** :&ensp;`Optional[Type[KnowledgeAsset]]`
:   Asset class to use for resolving settings.

    Defaults to [KnowledgeAsset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_assets/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset").

:   Additional keyword arguments.

`ArgsKwargs`

```python
    **kwargs
)
```

Prepare positional and keyword arguments for an asset function call.

__Args__

**```path```** :&ensp;`Union[PathMoveDict, MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Mapping or path(s) within the data item
    to move (e.g. "x.y[0].z").

    When provided as a dictionary, keys are source paths and values are the corresponding new tokens.

**```new_path```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Path(s) for the moved element(s)
    when `path` is not a dictionary.

**```skip_missing```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, skips data items where the specified path is missing.

**```make_copy```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, operates on a copy rather than modifying the original data.

**```changed_only```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, returns only data items that were modified.

**```asset_cls```** :&ensp;`Optional[Type[KnowledgeAsset]]`
:   Asset class to use for resolving settings.

    Defaults to [KnowledgeAsset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_assets/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset").

:   Additional keyword arguments.

`ArgsKwargs`
:   Tuple containing the positional arguments and keyword arguments.

### ReorderAssetFunc.prepare | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_asset_funcs.py#L589-L678)

```python
ReorderAssetFunc.prepare(
    new_order,
    path=None,
    skip_missing=None,
    make_copy=None,
    changed_only=None,
    template_context=None,
    asset_cls=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Prepare positional and keyword arguments for an asset function call.

__Args__

**```new_order```** :&ensp;`Union[str, PathKeyTokens]`
:   New order specification, which can be:

    * Sequence with tokens and an ellipsis (`...`) to preserve segments (e.g. ["a", ..., "z"]).

    * String "asc", "ascending", "desc", or "descending" indicating the sort order.

    * Function or template that generates an order using variables: `i` for the item index,
        `d` for the data item, `x` for the value at the specified path, and field names for
        individual fields.

**```path```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Path(s) within the data item to reorder (e.g. "x.y[0].z").

**```skip_missing```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, skips data items where the specified path is missing.

**```make_copy```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, operates on a copy rather than modifying the original data.

**```changed_only```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, returns only data items that were modified.

**```template_context```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Additional context for template substitution.

**```asset_cls```** :&ensp;`Optional[Type[KnowledgeAsset]]`
:   Asset class to use for resolving settings.

    Defaults to [KnowledgeAsset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_assets/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`ArgsKwargs`
:   Tuple containing the positional arguments and keyword arguments.

```python
UnflattenAssetFunc.prepare(
    path=None,
    skip_missing=None,
    make_copy=None,
    changed_only=None,
    asset_cls=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Prepare positional and keyword arguments for an asset function call.

__Args__

**```path```** :&ensp;`Optional[MaybeList[PathLikeKey]]`
:   Path(s) within the data item to unflatten (e.g. "x.y[0].z").

**```skip_missing```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, skips data items where the specified path is missing.

**```make_copy```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, operates on a copy rather than modifying the original data.

**```changed_only```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, returns only data items that were modified.

**```asset_cls```** :&ensp;`Optional[Type[KnowledgeAsset]]`
:   Asset class to use for resolving settings.

    Defaults to [KnowledgeAsset](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_assets/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_assets.KnowledgeAsset").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [unflatten_obj](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/search_/#vectorbtpro.utils.search_.unflatten_obj "vectorbtpro.utils.search_.unflatten_obj").

__Returns__

`ArgsKwargs`
:   Tuple containing the positional arguments and keyword arguments.

!!! info

__Args__

**```persist_cache```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Whether to persist the cache to disk.

**```cache_dir```** :&ensp;`Optional[PathLike]`
:   Directory for saving knowledge assets.

:   Keyword arguments for cache directory creation.

    See [check_mkdir](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/path_/#vectorbtpro.utils.path_.check_mkdir "vectorbtpro.utils.path_.check_mkdir").

**```clear_cache```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Remove the cache directory before operation if True.

**```save_cache_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for saving assets to disk.

:   Additional context for template substitution.

## KnowledgeAsset | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_assets.py#L277-L3033)

Class for working with a knowledge asset.

This class behaves like a mutable sequence.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [knowledge](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.knowledge "vectorbtpro._settings.knowledge").

__Args__

**```data```** :&ensp;`Optional[List[Any]]`

    If more than one item is provided, the asset is not considered a single item.

### KnowledgeAsset.apply | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/knowledge/base_assets.py#L953-L1092)

```python
KnowledgeAsset.apply(
    func,
    *args,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    wrap=None,
    single_item=None,
    return_iterator=False,
    **kwargs
)
```

Apply a function or pipeline to each data item in the asset.

The `func` parameter accepts various types:

* Callable or a tuple containing a callable and its arguments.

* Instance of [Task](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.Task "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.Task").

* Subclass of [AssetFunc](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/knowledge/base_asset_funcs/#vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.AssetFunc "vectorbtpro.knowledge.base_asset_funcs.AssetFunc") or its prefix/full name.

* List of any of the above, which will use `BasicAssetPipeline`.

* Valid expression, which will use `ComplexAssetPipeline`.

Execution is handled by [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

__Args__

**```func```** :&ensp;`MaybeList[Union[AssetFuncLike, AssetPipeline]]`
:   Function, pipeline, or expression to apply.

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for the asset pipeline or function.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```wrap```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   If True, return the result wrapped as an asset.

**```single_item```** :&ensp;`Optional[bool]`
:   Determines if a single item should not be wrapped in a list.

**```return_iterator```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return an iterator instead of executing tasks.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for the asset pipeline or function.

__Returns__

`MaybeKnowledgeAsset`
:   New asset with processed data if `wrap` is True; otherwise, raw output.

__Examples__

```pycon
>>> asset.apply(["flatten", ("query", len)])
[5, 5, 5, 5, 6]

>>> asset.apply("query(flatten(d), len)")
[5, 5, 5, 5, 6]
```
