### FMIN.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fmin.py#L263-L309)

```python
FMIN.apply_func(
    close,
    window=14,
    wait=1,
    minp=None
)
```

Calculate rolling minimum over future values for each column.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-D array of input values.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wait```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Waiting period.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2-D array containing the computed rolling minimum values over future values for each column.

### FMIN.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fmin.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
FMIN.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,
    jitted_loop=False,
    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [FMIN.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[FMIN.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func"). If [FMIN.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[FMIN.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [FMIN.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### FMIN.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fmin.py#L1-L206)

```python
FMIN.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    short_name='fmin',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [FMIN](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the future minimum.

__Outputs__

* `fmin`: Future minimum series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [FMIN](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### FMIN.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fmin.py#L1-L206)

```python
FMIN.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [FMIN](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the future minimum.

__Outputs__

* `fmin`: Future minimum series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [FMIN.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [FMIN.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fmin/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fmin.FMIN.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

### FSTD.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fstd.py#L169-L233)

```python
FSTD.apply_func(
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=0,
    wait=1,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False,
    ddof=0
)
```

Calculate rolling standard deviation over future values for each column.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2-D array of input values.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```wait```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Waiting period.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

**```ddof```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Delta degrees of freedom.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2-D array containing the computed rolling standard deviations
    over future values for each column.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[FSTD.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.apply_func"). [FSTD.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

:   Additional positional arguments.

:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

### FSTD.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fstd.py#L1-L206)

```python
FSTD.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    short_name='fstd',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [FSTD](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the future standard deviation.

__Outputs__

* `fstd`: Future standard deviation series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [FSTD](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### FSTD.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/fstd.py#L1-L206)

```python
FSTD.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [FSTD](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the future standard deviation.

__Outputs__

* `fstd`: Future standard deviation series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [FSTD.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [FSTD.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/fstd/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.fstd.FSTD.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

## PIVOTLB | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/pivotlb.py#L25-L58)

Class representing the look-ahead pivot label generator.

This class generates labels based on pivot thresholds applied to high and low values.

__See__

* [PIVOTLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run") for the main entry point.

* [pivots_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/nb/#vectorbtpro.labels.nb.pivots_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.nb.pivots_nb") for the underlying implementation.

### PIVOTLB.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/pivotlb.py#L668-L714)

```python
PIVOTLB.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th
)
```

Generate pivot labels column-wise for two-dimensional input arrays.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of high values.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of low values.

**```up_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Upper threshold for detecting peaks.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

**```down_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Lower threshold for detecting valleys.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional integer array containing pivot labels.

### PIVOTLB.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/pivotlb.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
PIVOTLB.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,

    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [PIVOTLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[PIVOTLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func"). If [PIVOTLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[PIVOTLB.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [PIVOTLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### PIVOTLB.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/pivotlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
PIVOTLB.run(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th,
    short_name='pivotlb',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [PIVOTLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

__Parameters__

* `up_th`: Upper threshold for the pivot label, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_th`: Lower threshold for the pivot label, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Labels generated based on the pivot thresholds (see [Pivot](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.Pivot "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.Pivot")).

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [PIVOTLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### PIVOTLB.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/pivotlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
PIVOTLB.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th,
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [PIVOTLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

__Parameters__

* `up_th`: Upper threshold for the pivot label, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_th`: Lower threshold for the pivot label, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Labels generated based on the pivot thresholds (see [Pivot](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/enums/#vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.Pivot "vectorbtpro.indicators.enums.Pivot")).

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [PIVOTLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [PIVOTLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/pivotlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.pivotlb.PIVOTLB.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

### MEANLB.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/meanlb.py#L483-L543)

```python
MEANLB.apply_func(
    close,
    window=14,
    wtype=0,
    wait=1,
    minp=None,
    adjust=False
)
```

Return a 2-dim array of percentage changes computed for each column,
where each value is derived by comparing the current price to the average of future periods.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```close```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array of close prices.

**```window```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Window size.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```wtype```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Weighting type.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType").

**```wait```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Number of periods to wait before applying the window.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

**```minp```** :&ensp;`Optional[int]`
:   Minimum number of observations required.

**```adjust```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to adjust weights.

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   Two-dimensional array where each column contains the computed percentage changes.

### MEANLB.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/meanlb.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
MEANLB.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    per_column=False,
    split_columns=False,
    skipna=False,
    return_cache=False,
    use_cache=True,

    jitted_warmup=False,
    param_index=None,
    final_index=None,
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [MEANLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[MEANLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func"). If [MEANLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[MEANLB.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [MEANLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### MEANLB.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/meanlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
MEANLB.run(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    short_name='meanlb',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [MEANLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the mean labels.

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Mean labels series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [MEANLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### MEANLB.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/meanlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
MEANLB.run_combs(
    close,
    window=Default(value=14),
    wtype=Default(value='simple'),
    wait=Default(value=1),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [MEANLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `close`: Close price series.

__Parameters__

* `window`: Window size.

* `wtype`: Weighting type (see [WType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.WType")).

* `wait`: Number of periods to wait before calculating the mean labels.

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Mean labels series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [MEANLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [MEANLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/meanlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.meanlb.MEANLB.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

### TRENDLB.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/trendlb.py#L1081-L1136)

```python
TRENDLB.apply_func(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th,
    mode=0
)
```

Compute 2D trend labels for each column from high and low prices using specified thresholds and mode.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```high```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D array of low prices.

**```up_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Upper threshold for detecting peaks.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

**```down_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2dLike`
:   Lower threshold for detecting valleys.

    Provided as a scalar, or per row, column, or element.

**```mode```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Trend mode.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [TrendLabelMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/enums/#vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode "vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode").

__Returns__

`Array2d`
:   2D array of computed trend labels.

### TRENDLB.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/trendlb.py#L3177-L3526)

```python
TRENDLB.custom_func(
    input_tuple,
    in_output_tuple,
    param_tuple,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,

```

Forward inputs and parameters to [TRENDLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[TRENDLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func"). If [TRENDLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[TRENDLB.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [TRENDLB.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### TRENDLB.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/trendlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
TRENDLB.run(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th,
    mode=Default(value='binary'),
    short_name='trendlb',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [TRENDLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

__Parameters__

* `up_th`: Upper threshold for trend labels, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_th`: Lower threshold for trend labels, as a scalar or an array.

* `mode`: Trend label mode (see [TrendLabelMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/enums/#vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode "vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode")).

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Trend labels series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [TRENDLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### TRENDLB.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/labels/generators/trendlb.py#L1-L206)

```python
TRENDLB.run_combs(
    high,
    low,
    up_th,
    down_th,
    mode=Default(value='binary'),
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [TRENDLB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

__Parameters__

* `up_th`: Upper threshold for trend labels, as a scalar or an array.

* `down_th`: Lower threshold for trend labels, as a scalar or an array.

* `mode`: Trend label mode (see [TrendLabelMode](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/enums/#vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode "vectorbtpro.labels.enums.TrendLabelMode")).

__Outputs__

* `labels`: Trend labels series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [TRENDLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [TRENDLB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/labels/generators/trendlb/#vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.run "vectorbtpro.labels.generators.trendlb.TRENDLB.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.ohlcv.accessors | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/accessors.py)

Module providing custom Pandas accessors for OHLC(V) data.

Access the methods via:

* [OHLCVDFAccessor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/accessors/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.accessors.OHLCVDFAccessor "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.accessors.OHLCVDFAccessor") -> `pd.DataFrame.vbt.ohlcv.*`

The accessors inherit from [vectorbtpro.generic.accessors](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/ "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors").

!!! note
    Accessors do not utilize caching.

## Column names

By default, vectorbtpro searches for columns with names 'open', 'high', 'low', 'close', and 'volume'
(case-insensitive). You can change the naming by either using `feature_map` in
[ohlcv](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.ohlcv "vectorbtpro._settings.ohlcv") or by providing a custom `feature_map` directly to the accessor.

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     'my_open1': [2, 3, 4, 3.5, 2.5],
...     'my_high2': [3, 4, 4.5, 4, 3],
...     'my_low3': [1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 2.5, 1.5],
...     'my_close4': [2.5, 3.5, 4, 3, 2],
...     'my_volume5': [10, 11, 10, 9, 10]
... })
>>> df.vbt.ohlcv.get_feature('open')
None

>>> my_feature_map = {
...     "my_open1": "Open",
...     "my_high2": "High",
...     "my_low3": "Low",
...     "my_close4": "Close",
...     "my_volume5": "Volume",
... }
>>> ohlcv_acc = df.vbt.ohlcv(freq='d', feature_map=my_feature_map)
>>> ohlcv_acc.get_feature('open')
0    2.0
1    3.0
2    4.0
3    3.5
4    2.5
Name: my_open1, dtype: float64
```

## Stats

!!! tip

## OHLCVDFAccessor | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/accessors.py#L127-L767)

```python
OHLCVDFAccessor(
    wrapper,
    obj=None,
    feature_map=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing an accessor on top of OHLCV data for Pandas DataFrames.

Accessible via `pd.DataFrame.vbt.ohlcv`.

!!! info
    For default settings, see [ohlcv](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.ohlcv "vectorbtpro._settings.ohlcv").

__Args__

**```wrapper```** :&ensp;`Union[ArrayWrapper, ArrayLike]`
:   Array wrapper instance or array-like object.

**```obj```** :&ensp;`Optional[ArrayLike]`
:   Underlying data object.

**```feature_map```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Dictionary mapping feature names to OHLCV components.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [GenericDFAccessor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/accessors/#vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor "vectorbtpro.generic.accessors.GenericDFAccessor").

### OHLCVDFAccessor.mirror_ohlc | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/accessors.py#L225-L283)

```python
OHLCVDFAccessor.mirror_ohlc(
    jitted=None,
    chunked=None,
    start_value=nan,
    ref_feature=-1
)
```

Mirror OHLC features.

Applies a mirror transformation to the OHLC columns ("Open", "High", "Low", "Close")
using the specified starting value and reference feature.

__See__

[mirror_ohlc_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/nb/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.nb.mirror_ohlc_nb "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.nb.mirror_ohlc_nb")

__Args__

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

**```chunked```** :&ensp;`ChunkedOption`
:   Option to control chunked processing.

    See [resolve_chunked_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/chunking/#vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option "vectorbtpro.utils.chunking.resolve_chunked_option").

**```start_value```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Starting value used in the mirror operation.

**```ref_feature```** :&ensp;`ArrayLike`
:   Reference feature used for mirroring.

    Mapped using [PriceFeature](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/enums/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature") if provided as a string.

__Returns__

`Frame`
:   DataFrame with mirrored OHLC features.

### OHLCVDFAccessor.plot | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/accessors.py#L631-L733)

    for example, `dict(row=1, col=1)`.

**```volume_add_trace_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for `fig.add_trace` for the volume trace.

**```fig```** :&ensp;`Optional[BaseFigure]`

### OHLCVDFAccessor.resample | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/accessors.py#L285-L339)

```python
OHLCVDFAccessor.resample(
    *args,
    wrapper_meta=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Resample OHLCV data.

Resamples each feature based on default reduction rules:

* For "open", applies the first value.

* For "high", applies the maximum value.

* For "low", applies the minimum value.

* For "close", applies the last value.

* For "volume", applies the sum.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments for [ArrayWrapper.resample_meta](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.resample_meta "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.resample_meta").

**```wrapper_meta```** :&ensp;`DictLike`
:   Metadata from the resampling operation on the wrapper.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [ArrayWrapper.resample_meta](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.resample_meta "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.ArrayWrapper.resample_meta").

__Returns__

[OHLCVDFAccessor](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/accessors/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.accessors.OHLCVDFAccessor "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.accessors.OHLCVDFAccessor")
:   New accessor instance with resampled OHLCV data.

__Overridden methods__

* [Wrapping.resample](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/base/wrapping/#vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.Wrapping.resample "vectorbtpro.base.wrapping.Wrapping.resample")

# vectorbtpro.ohlcv.nb | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/nb.py)

Module providing Numba-compiled functions for processing OHLCV data.

!!! note
    Vectorbtpro treats matrices as first-class citizens and expects input arrays to be
    two-dimensional unless a function has a `_1d` suffix or is used as input to another function.
    Data is processed along the index (axis 0).

## mirror_ohlc_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/nb.py#L84-L205)

```python
mirror_ohlc_1d_nb(
    n_rows,
    open=None,
    high=None,
    low=None,
    close=None,
    start_value=nan,
    ref_feature=-1
)
```

Mirror OHLC arrays by applying a cumulative scaling based on logarithmic returns.

__Args__

**```n_rows```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of rows for the output arrays.

**```open```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array1d]`
:   1D array of open prices.

**```high```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array1d]`
:   1D array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array1d]`
:   1D array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array1d]`
:   1D array of close prices.

**```start_value```** :&ensp;`float`
:   Initial value for the reference price.

    If provided and not NaN, it replaces the first valid reference price.

**```ref_feature```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Indicator for the reference price feature.

    See [PriceFeature](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/enums/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature").
    A value of -1 enables auto-detection of the first non-NaN price.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Mirrored open, high, low, and close arrays.

## mirror_ohlc_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/nb.py#L208-L277)

```python
mirror_ohlc_nb(
    target_shape,
    open=None,
    high=None,
    low=None,
    close=None,
    start_value=nan,
    ref_feature=-1
)
```

Generate mirrored OHLC arrays for two-dimensional inputs by applying the 1D operation column-wise.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```target_shape```** :&ensp;`Shape`
:   Base dimensions (rows, columns).

**```open```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   2D array of open prices.

**```high```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   2D array of high prices.

**```low```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   2D array of low prices.

**```close```** :&ensp;`Optional[Array2d]`
:   2D array of close prices.

**```start_value```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Starting value.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    If provided and not NaN, it replaces the first valid reference price.

**```ref_feature```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1dLike`
:   Reference price feature.

    Provided as a scalar or per column.

    See [PriceFeature](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/ohlcv/enums/#vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature "vectorbtpro.ohlcv.enums.PriceFeature").
    A value of -1 enables auto-detection of the first non-NaN price.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Mirrored open, high, low, and
    close arrays with the specified shape.

## ohlc_every_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/ohlcv/nb.py#L35-L81)


    Provided as a scalar or per bar.

__Returns__

# vectorbtpro.portfolio.base | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/portfolio/base.py)

Module providing the base class for simulating a portfolio and measuring its performance.

## Stats

!!! tip
    See [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats") and [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics").

Let us simulate a portfolio with two columns:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> data = vbt.YFData.pull("BTC-USD", start="2020", end="2021")

>>> pf = vbt.Portfolio.from_random_signals(data.close, n=[10, 20], seed=42)
>>> pf.wrapper.columns
Index([10, 20], dtype='int64', name='randnx_n')
```

### Metric selection

To select specific metrics, use the `metrics` argument (see [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics") for supported metrics):

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(metrics=["sharpe_ratio", "sortino_ratio"], column=10)
Sharpe Ratio     0.842891
Sortino Ratio    1.045106
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

You can also select metrics by tag (see any metric in [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics") that defines a tag key):

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(column=10, tags=["trades"])
Total Trades                                10
Win Rate [%]                              80.0
Best Trade [%]                       28.151123
Worst Trade [%]                     -43.164326
Avg Winning Trade [%]                11.824565
Avg Losing Trade [%]                -22.193211
Avg Winning Trade Duration    12 days 00:00:00
Avg Losing Trade Duration     30 days 00:00:00
Profit Factor                         1.754294
Expectancy                            3.318427
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

Or provide a boolean expression:

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(column=10, tags="trades and open and not closed")
Total Open Trades      0
Open Trade PnL       0.0
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

We include "not closed" alongside "open" because some metrics, such as win rate,
have both tags since they are based on both open and closed trades or positions.
To observe this, pass `settings=dict(incl_open=True)` and `tags="trades and open"`.

!!! info
    In newer versions of vectorbtpro, many trade metrics have been moved to `pf.trades.stats()`.

### Passing parameters

Use `settings` to pass parameters shared across multiple metrics.
For example, we can pass the required return and risk free rate to all return metrics:

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(column=10, settings=dict(required_return=0.1, risk_free=0.01))
Start Index                   2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00
End Index                     2020-12-31 00:00:00+00:00
Total Duration                        366 days 00:00:00
Start Value                                       100.0
Min Value                                     53.920674
Max Value                                    133.184269
End Value                                    133.184269
Total Return [%]                              33.184269
Benchmark Return [%]                         302.791925
Position Coverage [%]                         42.622951
Max Gross Exposure [%]                            100.0
Max Drawdown [%]                              54.330618
Max Drawdown Duration                 309 days 00:00:00
Total Orders                                         20
Total Fees Paid                                     0.0
Total Trades                                         10
Win Rate [%]                                       80.0
Best Trade [%]                                28.151123
Worst Trade [%]                              -43.164326
Avg Winning Trade [%]                         11.824565
Avg Losing Trade [%]                         -22.193211
Avg Winning Trade Duration             12 days 00:00:00
Avg Losing Trade Duration              30 days 00:00:00
Profit Factor                                  1.754294
Expectancy                                     3.318427
Sharpe Ratio                                  -5.954819
Calmar Ratio                                   0.608865
Omega Ratio                                    0.297155
Sortino Ratio                                -18.377491
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

Any argument passed via `settings` either overrides an existing default or acts as an optional argument
passed to the calculation function during resolution. Both `required_return` and `risk_free` appear
in the signatures of the four ratio methods, so vectorbtpro knows to pass them automatically.

If the signature of [ReturnsAccessor.sharpe_ratio](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/returns/accessors/#vectorbtpro.returns.accessors.ReturnsAccessor.sharpe_ratio "vectorbtpro.returns.accessors.ReturnsAccessor.sharpe_ratio") did not list these arguments,
vectorbtpro would call the method without them. In that case, there are two options.

1) Set parameters globally using `settings` and explicitly enable passing them with
`pass_{arg}=True` in `metric_settings`:

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(
...     column=10,
...     settings=dict(required_return=0.1, risk_free=0.01),
...     metric_settings=dict(
...         sharpe_ratio=dict(pass_risk_free=True),
...         omega_ratio=dict(pass_required_return=True, pass_risk_free=True),
...         sortino_ratio=dict(pass_required_return=True)
...     )
... )
```

2) Set parameters individually using `metric_settings`:

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(
...     column=10,
...     metric_settings=dict(
...         sharpe_ratio=dict(risk_free=0.01),
...         omega_ratio=dict(required_return=0.1, risk_free=0.01),
...         sortino_ratio=dict(required_return=0.1)
...     )
... )
```

### Custom metrics

To compute a custom metric, provide at least two elements: a short name and a settings dictionary with
a title and a calculation function (see arguments in [StatsBuilderMixin](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin "vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin")):

```pycon
>>> max_winning_streak = (
...     "max_winning_streak",
...     dict(
...         title="Max Winning Streak",
...         calc_func=lambda trades: trades.winning_streak.max(),
...         resolve_trades=True
...     )
... )
>>> pf.stats(metrics=max_winning_streak, column=10)
Max Winning Streak    6.0
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

You may wonder how vectorbtpro determines which arguments to pass to `calc_func`?

In this example, the calculation function expects `trades` and `group_by`. To pass these automatically,
vectorbtpro searches for each argument in the current settings. If an argument such as `trades` is not found,
vectorbtpro either raises an error or attempts to resolve it if `resolve_{arg}=True` is set.

Argument resolution involves searching for a property or method with the same name (or prefixed with `get_`)
on the current portfolio. Any relevant settings such as `group_by` are automatically passed if they appear
in the target method signature. The resolved result is then passed as `arg` (or `trades` in our example)
to the calculation function as the argument.

Here is an example without argument resolution:

```pycon
>>> max_winning_streak = (
...     "max_winning_streak",
...     dict(
...         title="Max Winning Streak",
...         calc_func=lambda self, group_by:
...         self.get_trades(group_by=group_by).winning_streak.max()
...     )
... )
>>> pf.stats(metrics=max_winning_streak, column=10)
Max Winning Streak    6.0
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

And here is an example without calculation function resolution:

```pycon
>>> max_winning_streak = (
...     "max_winning_streak",
...     dict(
...         title="Max Winning Streak",
...         calc_func=lambda self, settings:
...         self.get_trades(group_by=settings["group_by"]).winning_streak.max(),
...         resolve_calc_func=False
...     )
... )
>>> pf.stats(metrics=max_winning_streak, column=10)
Max Winning Streak    6.0
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

Since the `max_winning_streak` computation can be expressed as a path from the portfolio,
we can simplify it further:

```pycon
>>> max_winning_streak = (
...     "max_winning_streak",
...     dict(
...         title="Max Winning Streak",
...         calc_func="trades.winning_streak.max"
...     )
... )
```

In this case, there is no need to pass `resolve_trades=True` because vectorbtpro resolves it automatically.
Another benefit is that vectorbtpro can inspect the signature of the final method in the path
([MappedArray.max](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/records/mapped_array/#vectorbtpro.records.mapped_array.MappedArray.max "vectorbtpro.records.mapped_array.MappedArray.max") in this case) and resolve its arguments accordingly.

To switch between entry trades, exit trades, and positions, use the `trades_type` setting.
You can also include open trades by passing `incl_open=True`.

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(column=10, settings=dict(trades_type="positions", incl_open=True))
```

The following example demonstrates how vectorbtpro overrides settings, from least to most important,
using a simple metric that returns a passed value:

```pycon
>>> # vbt.settings.portfolio.stats
>>> vbt.settings.portfolio.stats["settings"]["custom_value"] = 100
>>> custom_metric = (
...     "custom_metric",
...     dict(title="Custom Metric", calc_func=lambda custom_value: custom_value)
... )
>>> pf.stats(custom_metric, column=10)
Custom Metric    100
Name: 10, dtype: object

>>> # settings > vbt.settings.portfolio.stats
>>> pf.stats(custom_metric, column=10, settings=dict(custom_value=200))
Custom Metric    200
Name: 10, dtype: object

>>> # metric settings > settings
>>> custom_metric = (
...     "custom_metric",
...     dict(title="Custom Metric", custom_value=300, calc_func=lambda custom_value: custom_value)
... )
>>> pf.stats(custom_metric, column=10, settings=dict(custom_value=200))
Custom Metric    300
Name: 10, dtype: object

>>> # metric_settings > metric settings
>>> pf.stats(
...     custom_metric,
...     column=10,
...     settings=dict(custom_value=200),
...     metric_settings=dict(custom_metric=dict(custom_value=400))
... )
Custom Metric    400
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

Here is an example of a parameterized metric that counts the number of trades with PnL above a given threshold:

```pycon
>>> trade_min_pnl_cnt = (
...     "trade_min_pnl_cnt",
...     dict(
...         title=vbt.Sub("Trades with PnL over $$${min_pnl}"),
...         calc_func=lambda trades, min_pnl: trades.apply_mask(trades.pnl.values >= min_pnl).count(),
...         resolve_trades=True
...     )
... )
>>> pf.stats(
...     metrics=trade_min_pnl_cnt, column=10,
...     metric_settings=dict(trade_min_pnl_cnt=dict(min_pnl=0))
... )
Trades with PnL over $0    8
Name: 10, dtype: object

>>> pf.stats(
...     metrics=trade_min_pnl_cnt, column=10,
...     metric_settings=dict(trade_min_pnl_cnt=dict(min_pnl=10))
... )
Trades with PnL over $10    3
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

If the same metric name appears multiple times, vectorbtpro automatically appends an underscore
and an index, allowing you to pass keyword arguments to each instance separately:

```pycon
>>> pf.stats(
...     metrics=[
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt,
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt,
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt
...     ],
...     column=10,
...     metric_settings=dict(
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt_0=dict(min_pnl=0),
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt_1=dict(min_pnl=10),
...         trade_min_pnl_cnt_2=dict(min_pnl=20)
...     )
... )
Trades with PnL over $0     8
Trades with PnL over $10    3
Trades with PnL over $20    1
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

To add a custom metric to the full list of metrics, there are three options.

The first option is to modify [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics") in place, which appends the metric to the end:

```pycon
>>> pf.metrics["max_winning_streak"] = max_winning_streak[1]
>>> pf.stats(column=10)
Start Index                   2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00
End Index                     2020-12-31 00:00:00+00:00
Total Duration                        366 days 00:00:00
Start Value                                       100.0
Min Value                                     53.920674
Max Value                                    133.184269
End Value                                    133.184269
Total Return [%]                              33.184269
Benchmark Return [%]                         302.791925
Position Coverage [%]                         42.622951
Max Gross Exposure [%]                            100.0
Max Drawdown [%]                              54.330618
Max Drawdown Duration                 309 days 00:00:00
Total Orders                                         20
Total Fees Paid                                     0.0
Total Trades                                         10
Win Rate [%]                                       80.0
Best Trade [%]                                28.151123
Worst Trade [%]                              -43.164326
Avg Winning Trade [%]                         11.824565
Avg Losing Trade [%]                         -22.193211
Avg Winning Trade Duration             12 days 00:00:00
Avg Losing Trade Duration              30 days 00:00:00
Profit Factor                                  1.754294
Expectancy                                     3.318427
Sharpe Ratio                                   0.842891
Calmar Ratio                                   0.608865
Omega Ratio                                    1.271266
Sortino Ratio                                  1.045106
Max Winning Streak                                  6.0  << here
Name: 10, dtype: object
```

Since [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics") is a [Config](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/config/#vectorbtpro.utils.config.Config "vectorbtpro.utils.config.Config") object, it can be reset at any
time to restore the default metrics:

```pycon
>>> pf.metrics.reset()
```

The second option is to copy [Portfolio.metrics](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.metrics"), append the custom metric, and pass it via the `metrics` argument:

```pycon
>>> my_metrics = list(pf.metrics.items()) + [max_winning_streak]
>>> pf.stats(metrics=my_metrics, column=10)
```

The third option is to set `metrics` globally under `portfolio.stats` in [settings](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/_settings/#vectorbtpro._settings.settings "vectorbtpro._settings.settings"):

```pycon
>>> vbt.settings.portfolio["stats"]["metrics"] = my_metrics
>>> pf.stats(column=10)
```

## Returns stats

## Plots

!!! tip
    See [PlotsBuilderMixin.plots](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/plots_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.plots "vectorbtpro.generic.plots_builder.PlotsBuilderMixin.plots").

    The functionality provided here closely mirrors [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.stats").
    Refer to the examples under [StatsBuilderMixin.stats](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/stats_builder/#vectorbtpro.generic.stats_builder.StatsBuilderMixin.stats "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.stats") as well.

Plot the portfolio of a random strategy:

```pycon
>>> pf.plot(column=10)
```

![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot.light.svg#only-light){: .iimg loading=lazy }
![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot.dark.svg#only-dark){: .iimg loading=lazy }

You can select any subplots from [Portfolio.subplots](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/portfolio/base/#vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.subplots "vectorbtpro.portfolio.base.Portfolio.subplots"), arrange them in any order, and
control their appearance using keyword arguments:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro.utils.colors import adjust_opacity

>>> pf.plot(
...     subplots=["drawdowns", "underwater"],
...     column=10,
...     subplot_settings=dict(
...         drawdowns=dict(top_n=3),
...         underwater=dict(
...             trace_kwargs=dict(
...                 line=dict(color="#FF6F00"),
...                 fillcolor=adjust_opacity("#FF6F00", 0.3)
...             )
...         )
...     )
... )
```

![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_drawdowns.light.svg#only-light){: .iimg loading=lazy }
![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_drawdowns.dark.svg#only-dark){: .iimg loading=lazy }

To create a new subplot, the preferred approach is to pass a plotting function:

```pycon
>>> def plot_order_size(pf, size, column=None, add_trace_kwargs=None, fig=None):
...     size = pf.select_col_from_obj(size, column=column, wrapper=pf.wrapper.regroup(False))
...     size.rename("Order Size").vbt.barplot(add_trace_kwargs=add_trace_kwargs, fig=fig)

>>> order_size = pf.orders.size.to_pd(fill_value=0.)
>>> pf.plot(subplots=[
...     "orders",
...     ("order_size", dict(
...         title="Order Size",
...         yaxis_kwargs=dict(title="Order size"),
...         check_is_not_grouped=True,
...         plot_func=plot_order_size
...     ))
... ],
...     column=10,
...     subplot_settings=dict(
...         order_size=dict(
...             size=order_size
...         )
...     )
... )
```

Alternatively, you can create a placeholder and overwrite it manually afterward:

```pycon
>>> fig = pf.plot(subplots=[
...     "orders",
...     ("order_size", dict(
...         title="Order Size",
...         yaxis_kwargs=dict(title="Order size"),
...         check_is_not_grouped=True
...     ))  # placeholder
... ], column=10)
>>> order_size[10].rename("Order Size").vbt.barplot(
...     add_trace_kwargs=dict(row=2, col=1),
...     fig=fig
... )
```

![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_custom.light.svg#only-light){: .iimg loading=lazy }
![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_custom.dark.svg#only-dark){: .iimg loading=lazy }

If a plotting function can be accessed from the current portfolio, you can pass its path directly
(see [deep_getattr](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/attr_/#vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.deep_getattr "vectorbtpro.utils.attr_.deep_getattr") for the path format). You can also use templates to make
parameters depend on passed keyword arguments:

```pycon
>>> subplots = [
...     ("cumulative_returns", dict(
...         title="Cumulative Returns",
...         yaxis_kwargs=dict(title="Cumulative returns"),
...         plot_func="returns.vbt.returns.cumulative.vbt.plot",
...         pass_add_trace_kwargs=True
...     )),
...     ("rolling_drawdown", dict(
...         title="Rolling Drawdown",
...         yaxis_kwargs=dict(title="Rolling drawdown"),
...         plot_func=(
...             "returns.vbt.returns",  # returns accessor
...             (
...                 "rolling_max_drawdown",  # function name
...                 (vbt.Rep("window"),)),  # positional arguments
...             "vbt.plot"  # plotting function
...         ),
...         pass_add_trace_kwargs=True,
...         trace_names=(vbt.Sub("rolling_drawdown(${window})"),),  # add window to the trace name
...     ))
... ]
>>> pf.plot(
...     subplots,
...     column=10,
...     subplot_settings=dict(
...         rolling_drawdown=dict(
...             template_context=dict(
...                 window=10
...             )
...         )
...     )
... )
```

You can also replace templates across all subplots using the global template mapping:

```pycon
>>> pf.plot(subplots, column=10, template_context=dict(window=20))
```

![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_path.light.svg#only-light){: .iimg loading=lazy }
![](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/assets/images/api/portfolio_plot_path.dark.svg#only-dark){: .iimg loading=lazy }
