### SignalFactory.with_place_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/factory.py#L306-L1096)

```python
SignalFactory.with_place_func(
    entry_place_func_nb=None,
    exit_place_func_nb=None,
    generate_func_nb=None,
    generate_ex_func_nb=None,
    generate_enex_func_nb=None,
    cache_func=None,
    entry_settings=None,
    exit_settings=None,
    cache_settings=None,
    jit_kwargs=None,
    jitted=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Build a signal generator class using entry and exit placement functions.

A placement function selects indices for signals and is available in two types:
entry and exit placement functions. Each function accepts broadcast time series,
in-place output arrays, parameter arrays, and other arguments, and returns an array
of indices corresponding to the chosen signals. See [generate_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_nb")
for more details.

The settings dictionary of each function can have the following options:

__Options__

**```pass_inputs```** :&ensp;`List[str]`
:   Names of inputs to pass to the placement function.

    Order matters; each must be in `input_names`.

**```pass_in_outputs```** :&ensp;`List[str]`
:   Names of in-place outputs to pass to the placement function.

    Order matters; each must be in `in_output_names`.

**```pass_params```** :&ensp;`List[str]`
:   Names of parameters to pass to the placement function.

    Order matters; each must be in `param_names`.

**```pass_kwargs```** :&ensp;`Union[dict, List[str], List[Tuple]]`
:   Keyword arguments from the kwargs
    dict to pass as positional arguments.

    Built-in keys include:

    * `input_shape`: Provided when no input time series are passed.

    * `wait`: Number of ticks to wait before placing signals; defaults to 1.

    * `until_next`: (Applied in `generate_ex_func_nb` only) Whether to place
        signals up to the next entry.

    * `skip_until_exit`: (Applied in `generate_ex_func_nb` only) Whether to skip
        processing until the next exit.

    * `pick_first`: Indicates whether to stop at the first exit signal.

    * `temp_idx_arr`: Empty integer array for temporarily storing indices.

**```pass_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates whether to pass cache from `cache_func` to the placement function.

    Defaults to False.

For more arguments, see the custom function of the generated indicator and
[IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline").

!!! note
    Choice functions must be Numba-compiled.

    Which inputs, parameters and arguments to pass to each function must be explicitly indicated
    in the function's settings dictionary. By default, nothing is passed.

    Passing keyword arguments directly to the placement functions is not supported.
    Use `pass_kwargs` in a settings dictionary to pass keyword arguments as positional.

__Args__

**```entry_place_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Optional[PlaceFunc]`
:   Callback function for placing entry signals.

    Defaults to [first_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.first_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.first_place_nb") when used with `FactoryMode.Chain`.

**```exit_place_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Optional[PlaceFunc]`
:   Callback function for placing exit signals.

**```generate_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Generation function for entry signals.

    Defaults to [generate_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_nb").

**```generate_ex_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Generation function for exit signals.

    Defaults to [generate_ex_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_ex_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_ex_nb").

**```generate_enex_func_nb```** :&ensp;`Optional[Callable]`
:   Generation function for both entry and exit signals.

    Defaults to [generate_enex_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_enex_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.generate_enex_nb").

**```cache_func```** :&ensp;`Callable`
:   Caching function to preprocess data.

    Its outputs are appended as the last arguments to placement functions.

**```entry_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings dictionary for the entry placement function.

**```exit_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings dictionary for the exit placement function.

**```cache_settings```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings dictionary for the cache function.

**```jit_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the `@njit` decorator of the parameter
    selection function.

    Has `nogil` set to True by default.

**```jitted```** :&ensp;`JittedOption`
:   Option to control JIT compilation.

    See [resolve_jitted_option](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/jitting/#vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option "vectorbtpro.utils.jitting.resolve_jitted_option").

    If the generation function is not jitted, the apply function will not be jitted.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for `IndicatorFactory.with_custom_func`.

__Returns__

`Type[IndicatorBase]`
:   Custom signal generator class configured with
    the specified placement and generation functions.

__Examples__

Simplest signal indicator that places True at the very first index:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> @njit
... def entry_place_func_nb(c):
...     c.out[0] = True
...     return 0

>>> @njit
... def exit_place_func_nb(c):
...     c.out[0] = True
...     return 0

>>> MySignals = vbt.SignalFactory().with_place_func(
...     entry_place_func_nb=entry_place_func_nb,
...     exit_place_func_nb=exit_place_func_nb,
...     entry_kwargs=dict(wait=1),
...     exit_kwargs=dict(wait=1)
... )

>>> my_sig = MySignals.run(input_shape=(3, 3))
>>> my_sig.entries
        0      1      2
0   True   True   True
1  False  False  False
2   True   True   True
>>> my_sig.exits
        0      1      2
0  False  False  False
1   True   True   True
2  False  False  False
```

Take the first entry and place an exit after waiting `n` ticks. Find the next entry and repeat.
Test three different `n` values.

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro.signals.factory import SignalFactory

>>> @njit
... def wait_place_nb(c, n):
...     if n < len(c.out):
...         c.out[n] = True
...         return n
...     return -1

>>> # Build signal generator
>>> MySignals = SignalFactory(
...     mode='chain',
...     param_names=['n']
... ).with_place_func(
...     exit_place_func_nb=wait_place_nb,
...     exit_settings=dict(
...         pass_params=['n']
...     )
... )

>>> # Run signal generator
>>> entries = [True, True, True, True, True]
>>> my_sig = MySignals.run(entries, [0, 1, 2])

>>> my_sig.entries  # input entries
custom_n     0     1     2
0         True  True  True
1         True  True  True
2         True  True  True
3         True  True  True
4         True  True  True

>>> my_sig.new_entries  # output entries
custom_n      0      1      2
0          True   True   True
1         False  False  False
2          True  False  False
3         False   True  False
4          True  False   True

>>> my_sig.exits  # output exits
custom_n      0      1      2
0         False  False  False
1          True  False  False
2         False   True  False
3          True  False   True
4         False  False  False
```

To combine multiple iterative signals, you would need to create a custom placement function.
Here is an example of combining two random generators using "OR" rule (the first signal wins):

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro.indicators.configs import flex_elem_param_config
>>> from vectorbtpro.signals.factory import SignalFactory
>>> from vectorbtpro.signals.nb import rand_by_prob_place_nb

>>> # Enum to distinguish random generators
>>> RandType = namedtuple('RandType', ['R1', 'R2'])(0, 1)

>>> # Define exit placement function
>>> @njit
... def rand_exit_place_nb(c, rand_type, prob1, prob2):
...     for out_i in range(len(c.out)):
...         if np.random.uniform(0, 1) < prob1:
...             c.out[out_i] = True
...             rand_type[c.from_i + out_i] = RandType.R1
...             return out_i
...         if np.random.uniform(0, 1) < prob2:
...             c.out[out_i] = True
...             rand_type[c.from_i + out_i] = RandType.R2
...             return out_i
...     return -1

>>> # Build signal generator
>>> MySignals = SignalFactory(
...     mode='chain',
...     in_output_names=['rand_type'],
...     param_names=['prob1', 'prob2'],
...     attr_settings=dict(
...         rand_type=dict(dtype=RandType)  # creates rand_type_readable
...     )
... ).with_place_func(
...     exit_place_func_nb=rand_exit_place_nb,
...     exit_settings=dict(
...         pass_in_outputs=['rand_type'],
...         pass_params=['prob1', 'prob2']
...     ),
...     param_settings=dict(
...         prob1=flex_elem_param_config,  # param per frame/row/col/element
...         prob2=flex_elem_param_config
...     ),
...     rand_type=-1  # fill with this value
... )

>>> # Run signal generator
>>> entries = [True, True, True, True, True]
>>> my_sig = MySignals.run(entries, [0., 1.], [0., 1.], param_product=True)

>>> my_sig.new_entries
custom_prob1           0.0           1.0
custom_prob2    0.0    1.0    0.0    1.0
0              True   True   True   True
1             False  False  False  False
2             False   True   True   True
3             False  False  False  False
4             False   True   True   True

>>> my_sig.exits
custom_prob1           0.0           1.0
custom_prob2    0.0    1.0    0.0    1.0
0             False  False  False  False
1             False   True   True   True
2             False  False  False  False
3             False   True   True   True
4             False  False  False  False

>>> my_sig.rand_type_readable
custom_prob1     0.0     1.0
custom_prob2 0.0 1.0 0.0 1.0
0
1                 R2  R1  R1
2
3                 R2  R1  R1
4
```

# vectorbtpro.signals.nb | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py)

Module providing Numba-compiled functions for signals.

Provides an arsenal of Numba-compiled functions that are used by accessors
and in many other parts of the backtesting pipeline, such as technical indicators.
These only accept NumPy arrays and other Numba-compatible types.

!!! note
    vectorbtpro treats matrices as first-class citizens and expects input arrays to be
    2-dim, unless function has suffix `_1d` or is meant to be input to another function.
    Data is processed along index (axis 0).

    All functions passed as argument must be Numba-compiled.

## between_partition_ranges_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1650-L1697)

```python
between_partition_ranges_nb(
    mask
)
```

Create a record array representing ranges between partitions in `mask`.

The function identifies the gaps between consecutive partitions in the boolean array `mask`.
When a new partition starts after an existing one, a range is recorded from the previous
partition start to the current index.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Boolean array indicating partitions with signal presence.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Array of records containing range data between partitions.

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.

## between_ranges_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1465-L1517)

```python
between_ranges_nb(
    mask,
    incl_open=False
)
```

Create a record array representing ranges between signals in `mask`.

The function iterates over each column of the boolean array `mask` to identify consecutive signals.
When a pair of signals is found, a record is created with start and end indices and a closed status.
If `incl_open` is True and the last signal does not have a corresponding closing signal,
an open range is recorded.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Boolean array indicating signal positions.

**```incl_open```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Include an open range if no closing signal is found.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Array of records containing range metadata.

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.

## between_two_ranges_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1520-L1586)

```python
between_two_ranges_nb(
    source_mask,
    target_mask,
    relation=1,
    incl_open=False
)
```

Create a record array representing ranges between source and target masks.

The function uses [relation_idxs_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.relation_idxs_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.relation_idxs_1d_nb") to determine paired indices from the `source_mask`
and `target_mask` for each column. When valid index pairs are found, a closed range record is created.
If only the source index is valid and `incl_open` is True, an open range record is recorded.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```source_mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Boolean array indicating positions of source signals.

**```target_mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Boolean array indicating positions of target signals.

**```relation```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Relation mode for pairing signals.

    See [SignalRelation](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.SignalRelation "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.SignalRelation").

**```incl_open```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Include an open range if no closing signal is found.

__Returns__

`RecordArray`
:   Array of records containing range data.

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.

## clean_enex_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1115-L1171)

```python
clean_enex_1d_nb(
    entries,
    exits,
    force_first=True,
    keep_conflicts=False,
    reverse_order=False
)
```

Clean entry and exit arrays by selecting the first valid signal in each partition.

Parameters determine the ordering and conflict handling:

* `force_first`: If True, the first signal (entry or exit) is forced before its counterpart.

* `keep_conflicts`: If True, simultaneous signals are processed sequentially without removal.

* `reverse_order`: If True, the order of signals is reversed.

__Args__

**```entries```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D boolean array indicating entry signals.

**```exits```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D boolean array indicating exit signals.

**```force_first```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Determines whether the first signal is forced to precede its counterpart.

**```keep_conflicts```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Determines if simultaneous signals are processed sequentially.

**```reverse_order```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Determines whether to reverse the order of signals.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple containing the cleaned entry and exit arrays.

## clean_enex_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1174-L1223)

```python
clean_enex_nb(
```

    Each column represents signals for a distinct series.

**```keep_conflicts```** :&ensp;`bool`

**```reverse_order```** :&ensp;`bool`

__Returns__

## distance_from_last_1d_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1039-L1082)

```python
distance_from_last_1d_nb(
    mask,
    nth=1
)
```

Compute the distance from the n-th last True value to the current index.

Unless `nth` is zero, the current True value is not considered among the last True values.

__Args__

**```mask```** :&ensp;`Array1d`
:   1D boolean array indicating signal positions.

**```nth```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Index of the last True value to measure the distance from.

__Returns__

`Array1d`
:   Array of distances.

## generate_enex_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L223-L345)

Place entry and exit signals sequentially using provided placement functions.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```target_shape```** :&ensp;`Shape`

    and additional arguments, and returns the index of the last entry signal (-1 to break the loop).

    To place multiple signals, modify `c.out` in the context and return the last index.

    To place multiple signals, modify `c.out` in the context and return the last index.

## generate_ex_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L121-L220)

```python
generate_ex_nb(
    entries,
    exit_place_func_nb,
    exit_place_args=(),
    wait=1,
    until_next=True,
    skip_until_exit=False
)
```

Place exit signals using `exit_place_func_nb` after each signal in `entries`.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```entries```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Boolean array with entry signals.

**```exit_place_func_nb```** :&ensp;`PlaceFunc`
:   Callback function that accepts [GenExContext](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.GenExContext "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.GenExContext")
    and additional arguments, and returns the index of the last exit signal (-1 to break the loop).

    To place multiple signals, modify `c.out` in the context and return the last index.

**```exit_place_args```** :&ensp;`Args`
:   Positional arguments for `exit_place_func_nb`.

**```wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of ticks to wait before placing exits.

    !!! note

**```until_next```** :&ensp;`bool`

    !!! note

**```skip_until_exit```** :&ensp;`bool`

    Has only effect when `until_next` is disabled.

    !!! note

## generate_rand_enex_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L401-L500)

```python
generate_rand_enex_nb(
    target_shape,
    n,
    entry_wait=1,
    exit_wait=1
)
```

Pick a number of entries and the same number of exits one after another.

Respects `entry_wait` and `exit_wait` constraints through a number of tricks.
Tries to mimic a uniform distribution as much as possible.

The idea is the following: with constraints, there is some fixed amount of total
space required between the first entry and the last exit. Upscale this space so that
the distribution of entries and exits mimics a uniform distribution. This involves
randomizing the position of the first entry, the last exit, and all signals in between.

!!! tip
    This function is parallelizable.

__Args__

**```target_shape```** :&ensp;`Shape`
:   Base dimensions (rows, columns).

**```n```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1d`
:   Flexible array specifying the number of entry-exit pairs per column.

**```entry_wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of periods to wait before an entry signal is triggered.

    !!! note
        Setting `entry_wait` to 0 or False assumes that both entry and exit can be processed
        within the same bar, and exit can be processed before entry.

**```exit_wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of periods to wait before an exit signal is triggered.

    !!! note
        Setting `exit_wait` to 0 or False assumes that both entry and exit can be processed
        within the same bar, and entry can be processed before exit.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple containing a boolean array for entries and a boolean array for exits.

## ohlc_stop_place_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L666-L875)

```python
ohlc_stop_place_nb(
    c,
    entry_price,
    open,
    high,
    low,
    close,
    stop_price_out,
    stop_type_out,
    sl_stop,
    tsl_th,
    tsl_stop,
    tp_stop,
    reverse,
    is_entry_open=False
)
```

Place an exit signal when a threshold is hit using OHLC data.

This function extends [stop_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.stop_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.stop_place_nb") by considering the entire bar.
It simultaneously checks for trailing stop loss and take profit thresholds,
tracking the hit price and corresponding stop type.

!!! note
    The waiting time must not exceed 1.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`Union[GenExContext, GenEnExContext]`
:   Signal generation context.

**```entry_price```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Entry price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```open```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Open price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is True, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```high```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   High price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```low```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Low price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```close```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Close price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is False, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```stop_price_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the hit price of each exit; must have full shape.

**```stop_type_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the exit signal stop type; must have full shape.

    Typically, uses `StopType.SL` for stop loss, `StopType.TP` for take profit,
    and trailing stop types (`StopType.TSL` or `StopType.TTP`).
    See [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType").

**```sl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit threshold percentage for trailing stop loss.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Trailing stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tp_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```reverse```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Array indicating reversal (prices are followed downwards).

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```is_entry_open```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if the entry price is available at or before open.

    If True, uses the bar's high and low; otherwise, uses only close.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Index offset (relative to `c.from_i`) of the bar at which an exit signal was triggered,
    or -1 if no exit signal was generated.

## partition_ranges_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1589-L1647)

```python
    mask
```

Create a record array representing partitions of signals in `mask`.

The function scans each column of the boolean array `mask` to identify contiguous
sequences of signals. Each identified partition is recorded with its start and end indices;

    Has the [range_dt](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/generic/enums/#vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt "vectorbtpro.generic.enums.range_dt") dtype.

## sig_pos_rank_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1001-L1018)

```python
sig_pos_rank_nb(
    c,
    allow_gaps
)
```

Return the signal rank based on its position.

Computes the rank for a signal using its order in the partition. If `allow_gaps` is True,
the function returns a global rank ignoring partition gaps; otherwise, it uses the rank within
the current partition. Resets occur at each reset signal.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`RankContext`
:   Ranking context.

**```allow_gaps```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to determine whether to allow gaps in ranking.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Computed rank.

## stop_place_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L568-L663)

```python
stop_place_nb(
    c,
    entry_ts,
    ts,
    follow_ts,
    stop_ts_out,
    stop,
    trailing
)
```

Place an exit signal when a threshold is reached, implementing `place_func_nb`.

!!! note
    Waiting time cannot exceed 1.

    * If waiting time is 0, `entry_ts` corresponds to the first value in the bar.

    * If waiting time is 1, `entry_ts` corresponds to the last value in the bar.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`Union[GenExContext, GenEnExContext]`
:   Signal generation context.

**```entry_ts```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Entry price array.

    Uses flexible indexing.

**```ts```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Price array for comparing the stop value.

    Uses flexible indexing. If NaN, defaults to the corresponding entry price.

**```follow_ts```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Array of following prices.

    Uses flexible indexing. If NaN, defaults to the corresponding value from `ts`.
    Applied only when the stop is trailing.

**```stop_ts_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the hit price of each exit.

    Must have the complete shape.

**```stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Stop value array.

    Uses flexible indexing. An element set to `np.nan` disables it.

**```trailing```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Array indicating whether the stop is trailing.

    Uses flexible indexing. An element set to False disables trailing.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Relative index at which the exit signal was placed, or -1 if no exit signal occurred.

## unravel_between_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1768-L1851)

```python
unravel_between_nb(
    mask,
    incl_open_source=False,
    incl_empty_cols=True
)
```

Unravel each pair of successive True values in a mask into a separate column.

__Args__

**```mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Input 2D boolean mask.

**```incl_open_source```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to include the source True value even if a valid target is absent.

**```incl_empty_cols```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to include columns that contain no resolved pairs.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple containing:

    * New mask with each pair of successive True values unwrapped into a separate column.

    * Index position of the source True value within its new column.

    * Index position of the target True value within its new column.

    * Row indices of the source True values in the original mask.

    * Row indices of the target True values in the original mask.

    * Original column indices corresponding to each True value.

## unravel_between_two_nb | function | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/nb.py#L1854-L1974)

```python
unravel_between_two_nb(
    source_mask,
    target_mask,
    relation=1,
    incl_open_source=False,
    incl_open_target=False,
    incl_empty_cols=True
)
```

Unravel each pair of successive True values between a source and target mask into separate columns.

This function resolves index pairs with [relation_idxs_1d_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.relation_idxs_1d_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.relation_idxs_1d_nb") and returns
new masks along with relevant indices.

__Args__

**```source_mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D boolean mask for source signals.

**```target_mask```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   2D boolean mask for target signals.

**```relation```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Relation mode for pairing signals.

    See [SignalRelation](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.SignalRelation "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.SignalRelation").

**```incl_open_source```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag to include the source True value even if a valid target is absent.

**```incl_open_target```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Include open target signals when a matching source is not found.

**```incl_empty_cols```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to include columns that contain no resolved pairs.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d, Array1d]`
:   Tuple containing:

    * New source mask.

    * New target mask.

    * Array of source range values.

    * Array of target range values.

    * Array of source indices.

    * Array of target indices.

    * Array of original column indices.

# vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstcx.py)

Module providing the [OHLCSTCX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX") class for generating stop signals based on OHLC data.

## OHLCSTCX | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstcx.py#L22-L33)

```python
OHLCSTCX(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing a chained exit signal generator based on OHLC data and stop values.

Generates a chain of `new_entries` and `exits` derived from input `entries`.

__See__

* [OHLCSTCX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run") for the main entry point.

* [ohlc_stop_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.ohlc_stop_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.ohlc_stop_place_nb") for details on the exit placement.

* [OHLCSTX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX") for parameter details.

### OHLCSTCX.exit_place_func_nb | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstcx.py#L666-L875)

```python
OHLCSTCX.exit_place_func_nb(
    c,
    entry_price,
    open,
    high,
    low,
    close,
    stop_price_out,
    stop_type_out,
    sl_stop,
    tsl_th,
    tsl_stop,
    tp_stop,
    reverse,
    is_entry_open=False
)
```

Place an exit signal when a threshold is hit using OHLC data.

This function extends `stop_place_nb` by considering the entire bar.
It simultaneously checks for trailing stop loss and take profit thresholds,
tracking the hit price and corresponding stop type.

!!! note
    The waiting time must not exceed 1.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`Union[GenExContext, GenEnExContext]`
:   Signal generation context.

**```entry_price```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Entry price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```open```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Open price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is True, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```high```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   High price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```low```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Low price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```close```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Close price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is False, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```stop_price_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the hit price of each exit; must have full shape.

**```stop_type_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the exit signal stop type; must have full shape.

    Typically, uses `StopType.SL` for stop loss, `StopType.TP` for take profit,
    and trailing stop types (`StopType.TSL` or `StopType.TTP`).
    See [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType").

**```sl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit threshold percentage for trailing stop loss.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Trailing stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tp_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```reverse```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Array indicating reversal (prices are followed downwards).

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```is_entry_open```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if the entry price is available at or before open.

    If True, uses the bar's high and low; otherwise, uses only close.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Index offset (relative to `c.from_i`) of the bar at which an exit signal was triggered,
    or -1 if no exit signal was generated.

### OHLCSTCX.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstcx.py#L1-L206)

```python
OHLCSTCX.run(
    entries,
    entry_price,
    open=nan,
    high=nan,
    low=nan,
    close=nan,
    sl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_th=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tp_stop=Default(value=nan),
    reverse=Default(value=False),
    stop_price=nan,
    stop_type=-1,
    short_name='ohlcstcx',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [OHLCSTCX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

* `entry_price`: Entry price series.

* `open`: Open price series.

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__In-place outputs__

* `stop_price`: Stop price series.

* `stop_type`: Stop type series (see [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType")).

__Parameters__

* `sl_stop`: Stop loss value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_th`: Trailing stop threshold value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_stop`: Trailing stop value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tp_stop`: Take profit value, as a scalar or an array.

* `reverse`: Whether to reverse the position, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `new_entries`: New entry signal series.

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [OHLCSTCX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### OHLCSTCX.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstcx.py#L1-L206)

```python
OHLCSTCX.run_combs(
    entries,
    entry_price,
    open=nan,
    high=nan,
    low=nan,
    close=nan,
    sl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_th=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tp_stop=Default(value=nan),
    reverse=Default(value=False),
    stop_price=nan,
    stop_type=-1,
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [OHLCSTCX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

* `entry_price`: Entry price series.

* `open`: Open price series.

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__In-place outputs__

* `stop_price`: Stop price series.

* `stop_type`: Stop type series (see [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType")).

__Parameters__

* `sl_stop`: Stop loss value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_th`: Trailing stop threshold value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_stop`: Trailing stop value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tp_stop`: Take profit value, as a scalar or an array.

* `reverse`: Whether to reverse the position, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `new_entries`: New entry signal series.

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [OHLCSTCX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [OHLCSTCX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstcx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstcx.OHLCSTCX.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

Exit function configuration for the [OHLCSTX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX") signal generator.

## OHLCSTX | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstx.py#L130-L130)

```python
OHLCSTX(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing an exit signal generator based on OHLC data and stop values.

!!! tip
    All parameters may be provided as a single value (per frame) or as a NumPy array
    (per row, column, or element).

    To generate multiple combinations, pass them as lists.

!!! warning
    The generator checks for an exit after every entry. If two entries occur consecutively,
    no exit signal is generated. Consider cleaning up entry signals before passing them, or use `OHLCSTCX`.

__See__

* [OHLCSTX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run") for the main entry point.

* [ohlc_stop_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.ohlc_stop_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.ohlc_stop_place_nb") for details on the exit placement.

__Examples__

Test each stop type:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> entries = pd.Series([True, False, False, False, False, False])
>>> price = pd.DataFrame({
...     'open': [10, 11, 12, 11, 10, 9],
...     'high': [11, 12, 13, 12, 11, 10],
...     'low': [9, 10, 11, 10, 9, 8],
...     'close': [10, 11, 12, 11, 10, 9]
... })
>>> ohlcstx = vbt.OHLCSTX.run(
...     entries,
...     price['open'],
...     price['open'],
...     price['high'],
...     price['low'],
...     price['close'],
...     sl_stop=[0.1, np.nan, np.nan, np.nan],
...     tsl_th=[np.nan, np.nan, 0.2, np.nan],
...     tsl_stop=[np.nan, 0.1, 0.3, np.nan],
...     tp_stop=[np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, 0.1],
...     is_entry_open=True
... )

>>> ohlcstx.entries
ohlcstx_sl_stop      0.1    NaN    NaN    NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_th       NaN    NaN    0.2    NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_stop     NaN    0.1    0.3    NaN
ohlcstx_tp_stop      NaN    NaN    NaN    0.1
0                   True   True   True   True
1                  False  False  False  False
2                  False  False  False  False
3                  False  False  False  False
4                  False  False  False  False
5                  False  False  False  False

>>> ohlcstx.exits
ohlcstx_sl_stop      0.1    NaN    NaN    NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_th       NaN    NaN    0.2    NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_stop     NaN    0.1    0.3    NaN
ohlcstx_tp_stop      NaN    NaN    NaN    0.1
0                  False  False  False  False
1                  False  False  False   True
2                  False  False  False  False
3                  False   True  False  False
4                   True  False   True  False
5                  False  False  False  False

>>> ohlcstx.stop_price
ohlcstx_sl_stop    0.1   NaN  NaN   NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_th     NaN   NaN  0.2   NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_stop   NaN   0.1  0.3   NaN
ohlcstx_tp_stop    NaN   NaN  NaN   0.1
0                  NaN   NaN  NaN   NaN
1                  NaN   NaN  NaN  11.0
2                  NaN   NaN  NaN   NaN
3                  NaN  11.7  NaN   NaN
4                  9.0   NaN  9.1   NaN
5                  NaN   NaN  NaN   NaN

>>> ohlcstx.stop_type_readable
ohlcstx_sl_stop     0.1   NaN   NaN   NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_th      NaN   NaN   0.2   NaN
ohlcstx_tsl_stop    NaN   0.1   0.3   NaN
ohlcstx_tp_stop     NaN   NaN   NaN   0.1
0                  None  None  None  None
1                  None  None  None    TP
2                  None  None  None  None
3                  None   TSL  None  None
4                    SL  None   TTP  None
5                  None  None  None  None
```

### OHLCSTX.custom_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstx.py#L807-L1081)

```python
OHLCSTX.custom_func(
    input_list,
    in_output_list,
    param_list,
    *args_,
    input_shape=None,
    place_args=None,
    entry_place_args=None,
    exit_place_args=None,

    exit_args=None,
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [OHLCSTX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Arguments passed to any placement function (depending on the mode).

**```entry_place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Positional arguments for `entry_place_func_nb`.

**```exit_place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Positional arguments for [OHLCSTX.exit_place_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.exit_place_func_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.exit_place_func_nb").

**```entry_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Alias for `entry_place_args`.

**```exit_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Alias for `exit_place_args`.

**```cache_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Arguments passed to the cache function.

**```entry_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings for the entry placement function,
    including arguments from `pass_kwargs`.

**```exit_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings for the exit placement function,
    including arguments from `pass_kwargs`.

**```cache_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings for the cache function,
    including arguments from `pass_kwargs`.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Optional[IFCacheOutput]`
:   Cache to use.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs```**
:   Default keyword arguments based on the mode.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [OHLCSTX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### OHLCSTX.exit_place_func_nb | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstx.py#L666-L875)

```python
OHLCSTX.exit_place_func_nb(
    c,
    entry_price,
    open,
    high,
    low,
    close,
    stop_price_out,
    stop_type_out,
    sl_stop,
    tsl_th,
    tsl_stop,
    tp_stop,
    reverse,
    is_entry_open=False
)
```

Place an exit signal when a threshold is hit using OHLC data.

This function extends `stop_place_nb` by considering the entire bar.
It simultaneously checks for trailing stop loss and take profit thresholds,
tracking the hit price and corresponding stop type.

!!! note
    The waiting time must not exceed 1.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`Union[GenExContext, GenEnExContext]`
:   Signal generation context.

**```entry_price```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Entry price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```open```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Open price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is True, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```high```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   High price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```low```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Low price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan`, it is computed from `open` and `close`.

**```close```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Close price array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. If `np.nan` and `is_entry_open` is False, defaults to `entry_price`.

**```stop_price_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the hit price of each exit; must have full shape.

**```stop_type_out```** :&ensp;`Array2d`
:   Array to store the exit signal stop type; must have full shape.

    Typically, uses `StopType.SL` for stop loss, `StopType.TP` for take profit,
    and trailing stop types (`StopType.TSL` or `StopType.TTP`).
    See [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType").

**```sl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_th```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit threshold percentage for trailing stop loss.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tsl_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Trailing stop loss percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```tp_stop```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Take profit percentage array.

    Utilizes flexible indexing. Set an element to `np.nan` to disable.

**```reverse```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Array indicating reversal (prices are followed downwards).

    Utilizes flexible indexing.

**```is_entry_open```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Indicates if the entry price is available at or before open.

    If True, uses the bar's high and low; otherwise, uses only close.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Index offset (relative to `c.from_i`) of the bar at which an exit signal was triggered,
    or -1 if no exit signal was generated.

### OHLCSTX.run | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstx.py#L1-L206)

```python
OHLCSTX.run(
    entries,
    entry_price,
    open=nan,
    high=nan,
    low=nan,
    close=nan,
    sl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_th=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tp_stop=Default(value=nan),
    reverse=Default(value=False),
    stop_price=nan,
    stop_type=-1,
    short_name='ohlcstx',
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Run [OHLCSTX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

* `entry_price`: Entry price series.

* `open`: Open price series.

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__In-place outputs__

* `stop_price`: Stop price series.

* `stop_type`: Stop type series (see [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType")).

__Parameters__

* `sl_stop`: Stop loss value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_th`: Trailing stop threshold value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_stop`: Trailing stop value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tp_stop`: Take profit value, as a scalar or an array.

* `reverse`: Whether to reverse the position, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [OHLCSTX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

### OHLCSTX.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/ohlcstx.py#L1-L206)

```python
OHLCSTX.run_combs(
    entries,
    entry_price,
    open=nan,
    high=nan,
    low=nan,
    close=nan,
    sl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_th=Default(value=nan),
    tsl_stop=Default(value=nan),
    tp_stop=Default(value=nan),
    reverse=Default(value=False),
    stop_price=nan,
    stop_type=-1,
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [OHLCSTX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Inputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

* `entry_price`: Entry price series.

* `open`: Open price series.

* `high`: High price series.

* `low`: Low price series.

* `close`: Close price series.

__In-place outputs__

* `stop_price`: Stop price series.

* `stop_type`: Stop type series (see [StopType](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/enums/#vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType "vectorbtpro.signals.enums.StopType")).

__Parameters__

* `sl_stop`: Stop loss value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_th`: Trailing stop threshold value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tsl_stop`: Trailing stop value, as a scalar or an array.

* `tp_stop`: Take profit value, as a scalar or an array.

* `reverse`: Whether to reverse the position, as a scalar or an array.

__Outputs__

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [OHLCSTX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [OHLCSTX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/ohlcstx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.ohlcstx.OHLCSTX.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rand.py)

Module providing the [RAND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND") class for generating random entry signals.

## RAND | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rand.py#L24-L44)

```python
RAND(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing a random entry signal generator based on probabilities.

!!! tip
    The parameter `n` may be provided as either a single value (per frame) or a NumPy array (per column).

    To create multiple combinations, specify `n` as a list.

__See__

* [RAND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run") for the main entry point.

* [rand_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_place_nb") for details on the entry placement.

__Examples__

Test three different entry count values:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> rand = vbt.RAND.run(input_shape=(6,), n=[1, 2, 3], seed=42)

>>> rand.entries
rand_n      1      2      3
0        True   True   True
1       False  False   True
2       False  False  False
3       False   True  False
4       False  False   True
5       False  False  False
```

Entry count can also be set per column:

```pycon
>>> rand = vbt.RAND.run(input_shape=(8, 2), n=[np.array([1, 2]), 3], seed=42)

>>> rand.entries
rand_n      1      2      3      3
            0      1      0      1
0       False  False   True  False
1        True  False  False  False
2       False  False  False   True
3       False   True   True  False
4       False  False  False  False
5       False  False  False   True
6       False  False   True  False
7       False   True  False   True
```

```python
RAND.apply_func(
    i,
    target_shape,
    n,
    entry_args,
    only_once,
    wait
```

Apply the selected placement/generation function(s) for a single parameter combination.

This function is dynamically generated by [SignalFactory.with_place_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/factory/#vectorbtpro.signals.factory.SignalFactory.with_place_func "vectorbtpro.signals.factory.SignalFactory.with_place_func")
and its exact signature depends on the factory `mode` and the function settings.

Forward inputs and parameters to [RAND.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Arguments passed to any placement function (depending on the mode).

**```entry_place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Positional arguments for [RAND.entry_place_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.entry_place_func_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.entry_place_func_nb").

**```exit_place_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`

**```entry_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Alias for `entry_place_args`.

**```exit_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Alias for `exit_place_args`.

**```cache_args```** :&ensp;`ArgsLike`
:   Arguments passed to the cache function.

**```entry_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Settings for the entry placement function,
    including arguments from `pass_kwargs`.

**```exit_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`

__Parameters__

### RAND.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rand.py#L1-L206)

```python
RAND.run_combs(
    input_shape,
    n,
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    input_index=None,
    input_columns=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [RAND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Parameters__

* `n`: Number of entries to place, as a scalar or an array (per column).

__Outputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [RAND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [RAND.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randnx.py)

Module providing the [RANDNX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX") class for generating random entry and exit signals.

## RANDNX | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randnx.py#L24-L45)


Class representing a random entry and exit signal generator based on probabilities.

__See__

* [RANDNX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run") for the main entry point.

* [rand_enex_apply_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_enex_apply_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_enex_apply_nb") for details on the entry and exit placement.

* [RAND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND") for parameter details.

__Examples__

Test three different entry and exit signal configurations:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> randnx = vbt.RANDNX.run(
...     input_shape=(6,),
...     n=[1, 2, 3],
...     seed=42)

>>> randnx.entries
randnx_n      1      2      3
0          True   True   True
1         False  False  False
2         False   True   True
3         False  False  False
4         False  False   True
5         False  False  False

>>> randnx.exits
randnx_n      1      2      3
0         False  False  False
1          True   True   True
2         False  False  False
3         False   True   True
4         False  False  False
5         False  False   True
```

__Subclasses__

* `vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx._RANDNX`

### RANDNX.apply_func | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randnx.py#L503-L539)

```python
RANDNX.apply_func(
    target_shape,
    n,
    entry_wait=1,
    exit_wait=1
)
```

Call `generate_rand_enex_nb` using `apply_func_nb`.

__Args__

**```target_shape```** :&ensp;`Shape`
:   Base dimensions (rows, columns).

**```n```** :&ensp;`FlexArray1d`
:   Flexible array specifying the number of entry-exit pairs per column.

**```entry_wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of periods to wait before an entry signal is triggered.

    !!! note
        Setting `entry_wait` to 0 or False assumes that both entry and exit can be processed
        within the same bar, and exit can be processed before entry.

**```exit_wait```** :&ensp;`int`
:   Number of periods to wait before an exit signal is triggered.

    !!! note
        Setting `exit_wait` to 0 or False assumes that both entry and exit can be processed
        within the same bar, and entry can be processed before exit.

__Returns__

`Tuple[Array2d, Array2d]`
:   Tuple containing boolean arrays for entries and exits.

```python
    single_comb=False,
    execute_kwargs=None,
    **kwargs_
)
```

Forward inputs and parameters to [RANDNX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func"), performing caching and pre-processing.

Caching is performed using `cache_func` if provided, and the results are passed to
[RANDNX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func"). If [RANDNX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func") is a Numba-compiled function, the actual apply-function becomes
[RANDNX.param_select_func_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.param_select_func_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.param_select_func_nb"), which handles the selection of parameters and the passing of arguments.

__Args__

**```input_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[AnyArray, ...]`
:   Tuple of input arrays.

**```in_output_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[AnyArray], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of in-place output arrays.

**```param_tuple```** :&ensp;`Tuple[List[ParamValue], ...]`
:   Tuple of lists of parameter values.

**```*args_```**
:   Additional positional arguments.

**```input_shape```** :&ensp;`Optional[Shape]`
:   Shape of the input arrays.

**```per_column```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, processes parameters separately for each column.

**```split_columns```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to split arrays into separate columns.

**```skipna```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Whether to skip NaN values.

**```return_cache```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, return the cache result instead of processing further.

**```use_cache```** :&ensp;`Union[bool, IFCacheOutput]`
:   Flag or configuration indicating whether to use caching.

**```jitted_loop```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether to use a JIT-compiled loop.

**```jitted_warmup```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, perform a warm-up call for the JIT-compiled function.

**```param_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Index for parameter combinations.

**```final_index```** :&ensp;`Optional[Index]`
:   Final index used for the output.

**```single_comb```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   Flag indicating whether there is only one parameter combination.

**```execute_kwargs```** :&ensp;`KwargsLike`
:   Keyword arguments for the execution handler.

    See [execute](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/utils/execution/#vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute "vectorbtpro.utils.execution.execute").

**```**kwargs_```**
:   Additional keyword arguments.

__Returns__

`Union[None, IFCacheOutput, Array2d, List[Array2d]]`
:       Result of applying [RANDNX.apply_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.apply_func"), which may be:

    * Cache output if `return_cache` is True.

    * 2D array.

    * List of 2D arrays.

    * None.

### RANDNX.run_combs | class method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randnx.py#L1-L206)

```python
RANDNX.run_combs(
    input_shape,
    n,
    r=2,
    param_product=False,
    comb_func=itertools.combinations,
    run_unique=True,
    short_names=None,
    hide_params=None,
    hide_default=True,
    input_index=None,
    input_columns=None,
    **kwargs
)
```

Create multiple [RANDNX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX") indicator instances based on parameter combinations.

__Parameters__

* `n`: Number of entries to place, as a scalar or an array (per column).

__Outputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

`comb_func` must accept an iterable of parameter tuples along with `r`. 
It also supports combinatoric iterators from `itertools`, like `itertools.combinations`.

!!! note
    Use this method only when multiple indicator instances are required.
    To test multiple parameters, pass them as lists to [RANDNX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run").

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for pipeline configuration and combination settings, including:

    * `r`: Number of indicators to run.

    * `param_product`: Flag controlling parameter combination behavior.

    * `comb_func`: Function to combine parameter tuples (e.g., `itertools.combinations`).

    * `run_unique`: If True, computes raw outputs before constructing indicators.

    * `short_names`: Custom short names for each indicator.

    * `hide_params`: Parameter names to hide column levels.

    * `hide_default`: Whether to hide parameters with default values.

    Other keyword arguments are passed to [RANDNX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randnx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randnx.RANDNX.run").

__Returns__

`Tuple[Indicator, ...]`
:   Tuple of indicator instances generated.

# vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randx.py)

Module providing the [RANDX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX") class for generating random exit signals.

## RANDX | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/randx.py#L24-L35)

```python
RANDX(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing a random exit signal generator based on probabilities.

__See__

* [RANDX.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX.run") for the main entry point.

* [rand_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_place_nb") for details on the exit placement.

* [RAND](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rand/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rand.RAND") for parameter notes.

__Examples__

Generate an exit signal for each entry:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> entries = pd.Series([True, False, False, True, False, False])
>>> randx = vbt.RANDX.run(entries, seed=42)

>>> randx.exits
0    False
1    False
2     True
3    False
4     True
5    False
dtype: bool
```

This function is dynamically generated by [SignalFactory.with_place_func](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/factory/#vectorbtpro.signals.factory.SignalFactory.with_place_func "vectorbtpro.signals.factory.SignalFactory.with_place_func")

Run [RANDX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX") indicator.

__Inputs__

* `entries`: Entry signal series.

__Outputs__

* `exits`: Exit signal series.

Pass a list of parameter names as `hide_params` to hide their column levels, or `True` to hide all.
Set `hide_default` to False to display column levels for parameters with default values.

__Args__

**```*args```**
:   Positional arguments corresponding to inputs, parameters, and in-place outputs.

**```**kwargs```**
:   Keyword arguments for [IndicatorBase.run_pipeline](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/indicators/factory/#vectorbtpro.indicators.factory.IndicatorBase.run_pipeline "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX.run_pipeline").

__Returns__

`Indicator`
:   Instance of the [RANDX](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/randx/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.randx.RANDX") indicator, or a tuple of additional objects if applicable.

# vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rprob | module | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rprob.py)

Module providing the [RPROB](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rprob/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rprob.RPROB "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rprob.RPROB") class for generating random entry signals based on probabilities.

## RPROB | class | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rprob.py#L24-L45)

```python
RPROB(
    wrapper,
    input_list,
    input_mapper,
    in_output_list,
    output_list,
    param_list,
    mapper_list,
    short_name,
    **kwargs
)
```

Class representing a random entry signal generator based on probabilities.

!!! tip
    All parameters can be provided as a single value (per frame) or as a NumPy array
    (per row, column, or element).

    To generate multiple combinations, pass them as lists.

__See__

* [RPROB.run](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/generators/rprob/#vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rprob.RPROB.run "vectorbtpro.signals.generators.rprob.RPROB.run") for the main entry point.

* [rand_by_prob_place_nb](https://vectorbt.pro/pvt_74d2a4ff/api/signals/nb/#vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_by_prob_place_nb "vectorbtpro.signals.nb.rand_by_prob_place_nb") for details on the entry placement.

__Examples__

Generate three columns with different entry probabilities:

```pycon
>>> from vectorbtpro import *

>>> rprob = vbt.RPROB.run(input_shape=(5,), prob=[0., 0.5, 1.], seed=42)

>>> rprob.entries
rprob_prob    0.0    0.5   1.0
0           False   True  True
1           False   True  True
2           False  False  True
3           False  False  True
4           False  False  True
```

Probability can also be set per row, column, or element:

```pycon
>>> rprob = vbt.RPROB.run(input_shape=(5,), prob=np.array([0., 0., 1., 1., 1.]), seed=42)

>>> rprob.entries
0    False
1    False
2     True
3     True
4     True
Name: array, dtype: bool
```

### RPROB.entry_place_func_nb | method | [source](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt.pro/blob/b08e819029eb56e38352bae72e703d3681d6400c/vectorbtpro/signals/generators/rprob.py#L375-L398)

```python
RPROB.entry_place_func_nb(
    c,
    prob,
    pick_first=False
)
```

Randomly place signals based on probabilities by marking positions in the context's output array.

__Args__

**```c```** :&ensp;`Union[GenEnContext, GenExContext, GenEnExContext]`
:   Signal generation context.

**```prob```** :&ensp;`FlexArray2d`
:   Flexible 2D array of probabilities used for signal placement.

**```pick_first```** :&ensp;`bool`
:   If True, stop after placing the first signal.

__Returns__

`int`
:   Index (relative to the start of the context's array) of the last placed signal.
